Activity-activity.list.description:
`list_activities` (fase 5): the activity timeline of one contact, company or opportunity, newest first. Generated
from the proposal by fase-5/tools/gen_meetings_api.py; the texts are the proposal's.

The operation is open to whoever reads contacts, companies or opportunities (`security` with ` or `); the provider
then demands the barrier of the kind of record asked for, as the use case does. It pages forward only by cursor
(`cursor[gt]`, decision 3 of the coordinator): {@see ForwardOnlyCursor} drops `hydra:previous`. A row has no item
operation; API Platform still names it after the collection (`@id` `/activities/{uuid}`), an IRI that leads to no
route (404): it is not a link to follow and the documentation does not publish it.

`data` is `{}` when the row is not available (`preserve_empty_objects`).

actor.description: Who did it. Rows that are not available to the user have kind `system` and no name. Never contains an email address.

kind.description: Kind of actor: `user` for a person of the account, otherwise `contact`, `automation`, `integration`, `system` or `external`.

name.description: Name of the person. `null` when the actor is not a person of the account or is no longer a member of it.

availability.description: `available`: the row is complete. `unavailable`: it exists but the user cannot see its content (an email, meeting, task or note outside their access); `data` is empty. `deleted`: the email or meeting it pointed to was deleted for good; `data` is empty.

category.description: Area of the product the fact belongs to. `crm` groups everything about companies, opportunities, tasks, notes, files, emails and meetings.

causation_id.description: Identifier of the operation that caused the row. Rows with the same value are the effects of one intention (for example a bulk action). `null` for hidden rows and when the row has none.

channel.description: Channel the fact happened on, when it applies. `null` otherwise.

data.description: What the row shows, as an object whose keys depend on `type` (for example `opportunity.stage_changed` carries the old and new stage names, `note.created` the title of the note). It is `{}` when `availability` is not `available`. Free text typed by people (titles, names, subjects) is returned as written and must be escaped before showing it as HTML. Besides the keys of each type, the API adds these when they apply: `email` (rows `email.sent` and `email.received`), `meeting` (rows `meeting.*`), `campaign` (rows of email and SMS campaigns) and `reference` (the object the row is about).

campaign.description: The campaign of a campaign row (`marketing.email.campaign`, `marketing.sms.campaign`, `marketing.email.bounced`, `marketing.email.complaint`, `marketing.sms.replied`, `audience.email.revalidated`). Only for users who can read campaign reports and while the campaign still exists.

subject.description: Subject. `null` for an SMS campaign.

uuid.description: UUID of the campaign.

email.description: The email message of an `email.sent` or `email.received` row, read when the page is served with the same privacy as the email itself: what appears depends on how much of the mailbox the user can read (`access`). Fields the user may not read are `null`.

example.preview: Thanks, we will confirm on Monday.
example.subject: Re: Annual plan

access.description: How much of the message the user can read: `metadata_only` (addresses and date), `subject_and_metadata` or `full_access`.

ai_summary.description: AI summary of the email. Only when `ai_summary_state` is `ready`.
ai_summary.example: Ana will confirm the annual plan on Monday.

ai_summary_state.description: State of the AI summary; `null` unless the email is incoming, complete, readable with full access and AI summaries are available in the account.

content_state.description: Whether the body is stored: `index_only`, `hydrating` (still being downloaded from Google), `full` or `unavailable`.

id.description: UUID of the email message.

preview.description: The snippet without the quoted previous email and the unsubscribe footer. `null` without snippet.
preview.example: Thanks, we will confirm on Monday.

recipient_contact_id.description: UUID of the contact when the first recipient is one.

recipient_kind.description: Who the first recipient is in the account.

recipient_name.description: Name, or address if it has no name, of the first `to` recipient.

recipient_others.description: How many more `to` recipients there are.

sender_contact_id.description: UUID of the contact when the sender is one.

sender_kind.description: Who the sender is in the account (a user, a contact, an unknown address).

sent_by_name.description: Member who sent it from the CRM when the sender is a shared mailbox.

snippet.description: Start of the message as stored.
snippet.example: Thanks, we will confirm on Monday.

subject.description: Subject. `null` with `metadata_only` access.

meeting.description: The meeting of a `meeting.*` row, read when the page is served and only when the user can see that meeting in the calendars it is allowed to read.

booking.description: The booking page that created the meeting. `null` when it does not come from a booking page. `guest_name` is the name the guest wrote (or their email), `null` once it was withdrawn.

conference_type.description: Kind of video call, if any.

conference_url.description: Join link of the video call.

id.description: UUID of the meeting.

location.description: Physical location.

original_time_zone.description: IANA time zone of the meeting in its source calendar. `null` for an all-day meeting or when unknown.

title.description: Title of the meeting.

reference.description: The object the row is about, so you can read it with its own operations. Only for users who can open that object and while it exists. Never on rows that are not available.

id.description: UUID of the object.

kind.description: Kind of object.

preview.description: Small summary of the object, only for notes, tasks, contacts, companies and opportunities. Notes: title, author_name, updated_at, excerpt (plain text, up to 400 characters). Tasks: title, due_at, status, task_type, assignee_name. Companies: name, domain. Contacts: name, email, company_name. Opportunities: name, amount, currency, stage_name, pipeline_name.

first_occurred_at.description: First time the grouped fact happened, ISO 8601. Equal to `occurred_at` when `occurrence_count` is 1.

initiated_via.description: The way it was done: `ui` (the Customer App), `maia`, `api`, `import`, `sync` (a connected Google mailbox or calendar), `automation` or `system`. A change made through this API by Maia appears with the person as `actor` and `initiated_via` `maia`.

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

last_occurred_at.description: Last time the grouped fact happened, ISO 8601.

occurred_at.description: When it happened, ISO 8601. For a grouped row, the same as `last_occurred_at`.

occurrence_count.description: How many times the same fact was grouped into this row (for example the opens of one campaign by the same person). 1 for a single fact.

type.description: Dotted type of the fact, for example `contact.created`, `contact.fields_changed`, `company.fields_changed`, `opportunity.created`, `opportunity.stage_changed`, `opportunity.pipeline_changed`, `note.created`, `note.edited`, `note.deleted`, `task.created`, `task.completed`, `task.reopened`, `meeting.scheduled`, `meeting.rescheduled`, `meeting.cancelled`, `email.sent`, `email.received`, `file.uploaded`, `file.linked`, `file.removed`, `marketing.email.campaign`, `audience.membership.created` or `automation.run`. New types can appear, so do not treat the list as closed. It decides which keys `data` has.

uuid.description: UUID of the activity row.

AsyncTaskStatus.description:
AsyncTask status:
* `pending` - Task is queued and waiting to be processed
* `processing` - Task is currently being processed
* `completed` - Task completed successfully
* `failed` - Task failed with an error

AsyncTaskType.description:
AsyncTask type:
**Segment operations:**
* `segment.add_to_group` - Add segment members to a group
* `segment.remove_from_group` - Remove segment members from a group
* `segment.export` - Export segment members to file
* `segment.unsubscribe` - Unsubscribe segment members
* `segment.delete_contacts` - Delete segment members

**Group operations:**
* `group.export` - Export group members to file
* `group.clear` - Remove all members from group
* `group.add_from_segment` - Add members from segment to group
* `group.remove_from_segment` - Remove members from segment from group
* `group.add_from_conditions` - Add members matching conditions to group
* `group.remove_from_conditions` - Remove members matching conditions from group

AttributeStatus.description:
Attribute status:
* `active` - Accepts new values
* `archived` - Keeps its stored values but no longer accepts new ones

AutomationStep.AutomationStepAddToGroup-.description:
API Resource for automation steps.

This class defines the API endpoints and serves as the base class for all
automation step types. Uses DiscriminatorMap for polymorphic serialization.

parent.description: IRI of the step after which this one is placed (/automations/{uuid}/automation_steps/{uuid}). It cannot be a condition step: use `parent_yes` or `parent_no` for those. Send at most one of `parent`, `parent_yes` and `parent_no`; send none to make this the first step, which is only possible while the automation has no first step.

parent_no.description: IRI of a condition step; this step is placed in its 'no' branch (contacts that do not meet the condition). Only valid for condition steps. Send at most one position field.

parent_yes.description: IRI of a condition step; this step is placed in its 'yes' branch (contacts that meet the condition). Only valid for condition steps. Send at most one position field.

This class defines the API endpoints and serves as the base class for all
automation step types. Uses DiscriminatorMap for polymorphic serialization.

parent.description: IRI of the step after which this one is placed (/automations/{uuid}/automation_steps/{uuid}). It cannot be a condition step: use `parent_yes` or `parent_no` for those. Send at most one of `parent`, `parent_yes` and `parent_no`; send none to make this the first step, which is only possible while the automation has no first step.

parent_no.description: IRI of a condition step; this step is placed in its 'no' branch (contacts that do not meet the condition). Only valid for condition steps. Send at most one position field.

parent_yes.description: IRI of a condition step; this step is placed in its 'yes' branch (contacts that meet the condition). Only valid for condition steps. Send at most one position field.

API Resource for automation steps.

This class defines the API endpoints and serves as the base class for all
automation step types. Uses DiscriminatorMap for polymorphic serialization.

action.description:
Action configuration. Structure depends on step_type:

- **step.delay**: DelayAction (delay_value, delay_unit, time settings)
- **step.condition**: ConditionAction (match, conditions array)
- **step.send.campaign**: SendCampaignAction (subject, from_name, template_html, etc.)
- **step.send.sms**: SendSmsAction (title, message, sms_sender, tracking fields)
- **step.add.to.group**: AddToGroupAction (group IRI)
- **step.remove.from.group**: RemoveFromGroupAction (group IRI)
- **step.update.custom.field**: UpdateCustomFieldAction (field IRI, value)
- **step.update.score**: UpdateScoreAction (value -5..5)
- **step.send.notification**: SendNotificationAction (emails, subject, body)
- **step.trigger.automation**: TriggerAutomationAction (automation IRI)
- **step.unsuscribe**: UnsubscribeAction (empty object)
- **step.move.to.step**: MoveToStepAction (target step IRI)
- **step.send.webhook**: SendWebhookAction (url, secret, payload_items)

children.description:
Child steps. Structure depends on step_type:

- **Normal steps** (delay, send_campaign, etc.): `{ "next": AutomationStep | null }`
- **Condition steps**: `{ "yes": AutomationStep | null, "no": AutomationStep | null }`

BookingPage-booking_page.read.description:
Booking pages of the public API (fase 5), managed by their owner. Generated from the proposal by fase-5/tools/gen_booking_pages_api.py; the texts are the proposal's.

Every operation checks the CRM access in its provider or processor first (`crm.contacts_companies.write` with a seat,
also to read: BookingPageAccess::writer), because API Platform evaluates `security` after the provider. The view is
projected by {@see \App\Api\State\Mapper\Crm\BookingPageMapper}, as the panel's MeetingBookingPageProjector does.

calendar_status.description: `missing` when the destination calendar or an availability calendar of the page is no longer in an active Google connection of the owner. `ok` otherwise, also when the page has no calendar yet.

configuration.description: Everything that defines the page. Keys that were never set are absent. Fields that bind to the CRM carry no internal data here.

example.description: A 30-minute call to see how Easymailing fits your team.

fields.label: What would you like to talk about?

example.title: Intro call with Sergio

allow_duration_selection.description: Whether the person booking can pick any of `allowed_durations`. If `false`, only `default_duration` is offered. Required to publish.

allowed_durations.description: Durations in minutes the person booking can get: any of 15, 30, 45 and 60, without repeats and at least one. Required to publish.

availability_calendar_resource_uuids.description: UUIDs of the calendars whose events block times (from `list_booking_calendars`), up to 50, no repeats. Include the destination calendar so its events block times too. Required to publish.

buffer_after_minutes.description: Free minutes kept after each meeting, 0 to 1,440. Required to publish.

buffer_before_minutes.description: Free minutes kept before each meeting, 0 to 1,440. Required to publish.

company_policy.description: Same as `contact_policy`, for the company. Required to publish.

contact_policy.description: What a booking does to an existing contact: `preserve` never changes it, `fill_empty` only fills empty fields, `update` overwrites the fields answered. Required to publish.

custom_host.description: `false` shows the name and photo of the page owner; `true` shows `host_name` and the image of `host_image_asset_uuid` instead. Required to publish.

daily_limit.description: Maximum meetings per day across all the host's booking pages; `0` means no limit. Required to publish.

dated_exceptions.description: Specific dates that replace the weekly hours: closed days or different hours. Up to 366, one per date. Required to publish (send `[]` for none).

closed.description: `true` closes the whole day; then `ranges` must be empty.

date.description: Date `YYYY-MM-DD` in the page time zone.

ranges.description: Opening ranges of that date when it is not closed.

start.description: Start time `HH:MM`, 24-hour, in the page time zone.

default_duration.description: Duration in minutes used when the person cannot choose; it must be one of `allowed_durations`. Required to publish.

description.description: Text shown on the booking page, up to 10,000 characters.
description.example: A 30-minute call to see how Easymailing fits your team.

destination_calendar_resource_uuid.description: UUID of the writable Google calendar where booked meetings are created (from `list_booking_calendars`). Required to publish.

fields.description: Fields the person booking fills in, up to 50. It must include the contact fields `first_name` and `email` to publish. Required to publish.

example.label: What would you like to talk about?

control.description: Kind of input. For `question` fields only `text`, `textarea`, `email` and `tel` are allowed; for record fields it must match the field type (see `list_booking_fields`).

field_reference.description: Which contact or company field this one fills. Required when `source` is `contact` or `company`; not allowed for `question`. Copy it from `list_booking_fields`.

id.description: UUID of the attribute. Only with `kind` = `attribute`.

key.description: Built-in field key such as `first_name` or `email`. Only with `kind` = `structural`.

kind.description: `structural` for built-in fields (`key`), `attribute` for custom attributes (`id`).

id.description: Identifier of the field inside this page, chosen by you. Letters, digits, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter, up to 64 characters, unique in the page.

label.description: Text shown to the person booking, up to 255 characters.

required.description: Whether the person booking must answer. The contact `first_name` and `email` fields are always required.

source.description: `contact` or `company`: the answer is saved on that record. `question`: a free question whose answer stays with the meeting and is saved on no record.

horizon_days.description: How many days ahead the page offers times, 1 to 366. Required to publish.

host_image_asset_uuid.description: UUID of an image uploaded with `upload_booking_page_image` by the same user, shown as host photo when `custom_host` is `true`. `null` for none.

host_name.description: Name shown as host when `custom_host` is `true`, up to 255 characters. Required to publish when `custom_host` is `true`.

hour_format.description: How times are shown on the page. Required to publish.

location.description: Where the meeting happens. `google_meet` adds a Meet link to the event; `phone`, `in_person` and `custom` use `location_value`. Required to publish.

location_value.description: Phone number, address or video-call link, up to 2,000 characters. Required to publish when `location` is not `google_meet`.

logo_asset_uuid.description: UUID of an image uploaded with `upload_booking_page_image` by the same user, shown as logo on the page. `null` for none.

notice_minutes.description: Minimum minutes between now and the start of a meeting, 0 to 525,600. Required to publish.

require_email_verification.description: Whether the person booking must confirm their email by a link before the meeting is created. Turning it on needs a page sender that can send (see `update_booking_email_settings`). Required to publish.

schema_version.description: Version of the configuration format. Always `1`.

slug.description: Optional label up to 120 characters. It is stored but not used: the public link is built from the page UUID. Leave it out.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone of the host in which `weekly_ranges`, `dated_exceptions` and the daily limit are read. Required to publish.

title.description: Name of the meeting shown to the person booking and used as the event title. Up to 255 characters. Required to publish.

weekly_ranges.description: Weekly opening hours: one entry per day that has hours (up to 7). `day` is 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday); a day that is absent has no availability. Required to publish.

day.description: Day of the week, 1 = Monday to 7 = Sunday.

ranges.description: Opening ranges of the day, up to 24, in order and without overlap.

start.description: Start time `HH:MM`, 24-hour, in the page time zone.

created_at.description: When the page was created, ISO 8601.

host_image_url.description: Photo shown as host. `null` when there is none.

host_name.description: Name shown as host: the owner's name or `configuration.host_name`.

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

logo_url.description: URL of `configuration.logo_asset_uuid`. `null` when there is none.

public_url.description: Link people use to book. Only present while `state` is `published`; `null` otherwise.

sender_status.description: `missing` when the page has no sender that can send its booking emails (none, deleted, unconfirmed or needing domain authentication). `ok` otherwise.

sharing.description: Who else can use this page in their emails.

mode.description: Who can use the page in their emails: `owner_only`, every user of the account (`account`) or the users and teams listed (`selected`).

subjects.description: The users and teams that have access, with their names. Empty unless `mode` is `selected`.

avatar_url.description: Photo of the user; `null` for teams or without photo.

id.description: UUID of the user (`subject_type` = `user`) or team (`team`).

name.description: Name of the user or team.

selectable.description: Whether the subject can be given access now. A suspended user keeps an existing grant but cannot be added.

selected.description: Whether the subject currently has access.

status.description: `suspended` when the user no longer has CRM access.

team_ids.description: UUIDs of the teams with access when `mode` is `selected`.

user_ids.description: UUIDs of the users with access when `mode` is `selected`.

state.description: `draft` (never published), `published` (public link works), `paused` (link closed, can be published again) or `archived` (final).

updated_at.description: When the page last changed, ISO 8601.

uuid.description: UUID of the page.

version.description: Version of the page. It grows with every change of configuration, state or sharing and when Google is reconnected and the page is re-linked to its calendar. Send it as `expected_version` to make sure nobody changed the page in between.

Campaign-campaign.read.description: Email campaign response. SMS campaigns are exposed separately under /sms_campaigns.

audience.description: IRI of the audience the campaign is sent from.

channel.description: Channel of the campaign. Always `email` here.

contact_targeting.description: Recipients chosen with the contacts engine, as Customer App does: a contact segment (`send_to_segment`) or the campaign's own filter, optionally on top of a segment (`send_to_custom_segment`). `null` when the campaign goes to the whole audience, to groups or to an old audience segment (`list_segment`). Recipients are always the confirmed subscribers of the campaign's audience and channel who match. Only `get_campaign`, `create_campaign` and `update_campaign` fill it; `list_campaigns` leaves it `null`, read the campaign to know its recipients.

contact_segment.description: IRI of the segment (`/contact_segments/{uuid}`): the target, or the base of the filter. `null` without segment or if the user lacks `contacts.read`.

contact_segment_deleted.description: True if that segment was deleted: the campaign cannot be sent until its recipients change (unless it was scheduled before).

error_code.description: Why the recipients cannot be calculated now (a code of the filter errors, e.g. `segment_reference_deleted` or `unknown_filter_field`); then `recipient_count` is 0 and the campaign cannot be sent. `null` when they can.

filter.description: The campaign's own conditions, in the shape of `filter` of `create_contact_segment`. `null` for `kind: segment` or if the user lacks `contacts.read`.

conditions.description: Conditions and groups of the top level, in order. At least one.

audience.description: Condition: UUID of the audience whose subscription is checked. Only for fields with `audience_required: true`, where it is required.

conditions.description: Group: its conditions (at least one), each with `field`, `operator`, `value` and `audience` as above. A group cannot contain a group.

field.description: Condition: `id` of a field of `list_contact_filter_fields`. Leave it out in a group.

match.description: Group: `all` or `any`, how its conditions combine. Leave it out in a condition.

value.description: Condition: value for the operator, shaped as its `value_shape` says. Leave it out when the shape is `none`.

match.description: How the top-level items combine: `all` (AND) or `any` (OR).

kind.description: `segment`: the campaign goes to a contact segment. `filter`: to its own filter.

pinned_at.description: When the revisions were fixed (scheduling or sending). `null` while following the latest.

revision_status.description: `following_latest`: the campaign uses the current revision of its segment (drafts). `pinned_current`: it was scheduled or sent with a revision that is still the current one. `pinned_outdated`: the segment changed after it was scheduled; the campaign keeps the old revision.

created_at.description: Date and time the campaign was created.

finished_at.description: Date and time the sending finished. Empty until the campaign has been sent.

groups.description: IRIs of the groups that receive the campaign. Empty unless it is sent to groups.

hash.description: Unique code of the campaign, used to attribute store orders and revenue. It is added to the links of the emails as `?em_ch=<hash>`.

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

list_segment.description: IRI of the old audience segment that receives the campaign. `null` unless it goes to one; campaigns that use a contact segment or their own filter have it `null` and describe their recipients in `contact_targeting`.

send_to.description: Who receives the campaign: `send_to_all`, `send_to_groups` (see `groups`), `send_to_segment` (see `contact_targeting`, or `list_segment` for an old audience segment) or `send_to_custom_segment` (its own filter, see `contact_targeting`).

started_at.description: Date and time the sending started. Empty until the campaign starts sending.

status.description: Current state of the campaign.

template.description: IRI of the template used as the email content.

template_thumbnail.description: URL of the preview image of the email.

title.description: Name of the campaign in your account.

type.description: Kind of campaign.

updated_at.description: Date and time the campaign was last changed.

uuid.description: Unique identifier of the campaign.

Campaign.jsonld-campaign.read.description: Email campaign response. SMS campaigns are exposed separately under /sms_campaigns.

audience.description: IRI of the audience the campaign is sent from: `/audiences/{uuid}` (see `list_audiences`).

campaign_config.description: Tracking and publishing options of the campaign. Required.

channel.description: Campaign channel. Always `email` for this endpoint.

contact_targeting.description: Recipients chosen with the contacts engine, as Customer App does: a contact segment (`send_to_segment`) or the campaign's own filter, optionally on top of a segment (`send_to_custom_segment`). `null` when the campaign goes to the whole audience, to groups or to an old audience segment (`list_segment`). Recipients are always the confirmed subscribers of the campaign's audience and channel who match. Only `get_campaign`, `create_campaign` and `update_campaign` fill it; `list_campaigns` leaves it `null`, read the campaign to know its recipients.

contact_segment.description: IRI of the segment (`/contact_segments/{uuid}`): the target, or the base of the filter. `null` without segment or if the user lacks `contacts.read`.

contact_segment_deleted.description: True if that segment was deleted: the campaign cannot be sent until its recipients change (unless it was scheduled before).

error_code.description: Why the recipients cannot be calculated now (a code of the filter errors, e.g. `segment_reference_deleted` or `unknown_filter_field`); then `recipient_count` is 0 and the campaign cannot be sent. `null` when they can.

filter.description: The campaign's own conditions, in the shape of `filter` of `create_contact_segment`. `null` for `kind: segment` or if the user lacks `contacts.read`.

conditions.description: Conditions and groups of the top level, in order. At least one.

audience.description: Condition: UUID of the audience whose subscription is checked. Only for fields with `audience_required: true`, where it is required.

conditions.description: Group: its conditions (at least one), each with `field`, `operator`, `value` and `audience` as above. A group cannot contain a group.

field.description: Condition: `id` of a field of `list_contact_filter_fields`. Leave it out in a group.

match.description: Group: `all` or `any`, how its conditions combine. Leave it out in a condition.

value.description: Condition: value for the operator, shaped as its `value_shape` says. Leave it out when the shape is `none`.

match.description: How the top-level items combine: `all` (AND) or `any` (OR).

kind.description: `segment`: the campaign goes to a contact segment. `filter`: to its own filter.

pinned_at.description: When the revisions were fixed (scheduling or sending). `null` while following the latest.

revision_status.description: `following_latest`: the campaign uses the current revision of its segment (drafts). `pinned_current`: it was scheduled or sent with a revision that is still the current one. `pinned_outdated`: the segment changed after it was scheduled; the campaign keeps the old revision.

created_at.description: Date and time the campaign was created.

email_config.description: Sender, reply-to, recipient name, subject and preview text of the email. Required.

finished_at.description: Date and time the sending finished. Empty until the campaign has been sent.

groups.description: IRIs of the groups that receive the campaign: `/audiences/{audienceUuid}/groups/{uuid}` (see `list_audience_groups`). They must belong to the same audience. Required when `send_to` is set to groups.

hash.description: Unique code of the campaign, used to attribute store orders and revenue. It is added to the links of the emails as `?em_ch=<hash>`.

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

list_segment.description: IRI of an old audience segment: `/audiences/{audienceUuid}/list_segments/{uuid}` (see `list_audience_segments`), from the same audience, with `send_to_segment`. Deprecated: Customer App does not show these segments; use `contact_segment` instead. Cannot be combined with `contact_segment` or `filter`.

send_to.description: Who receives the campaign, always among the confirmed subscribers of `audience`: the whole audience (`send_to_all`), some of its groups (`send_to_groups`, also send `groups`), a segment (`send_to_segment`, also send `contact_segment`, or `list_segment` for an old audience segment) or the campaign's own filter (`send_to_custom_segment`, also send `filter` and, optionally, `contact_segment`).

started_at.description: Date and time the sending started. Empty until the campaign starts sending.

status.description: Current state of the campaign.

template.description: IRI of an existing template to use as the email content: `/templates/{uuid}` (see `list_templates`). Alternative to `template_html` and `template_simple_json_code`; one of the three is required.

template_thumbnail.description: URL of the preview image of the email.

title.description: Name of the campaign in your account, for your own reference. Recipients do not see it.

type.description: Kind of campaign.

updated_at.description: Date and time the campaign was last changed.

uuid.description: Unique identifier of the campaign.

CampaignContactTargetingKind.description:
How the recipients of a campaign were chosen:
* `segment` - A contact segment
* `filter` - The campaign's own filter, optionally on top of a segment

CampaignContactTargetingRevisionStatus.description:
Which revision of its segments a campaign uses:
* `following_latest` - The current revision (drafts)
* `pinned_current` - The revision it was scheduled or sent with, still the current one
* `pinned_outdated` - The revision it was scheduled with; the segment changed afterwards

CampaignDeferredBatchCount.description:
Campaign deferredBatchCount:
Defines the number of batches the campaign will be split into.
Used with `incremental` and `fixed_batches_by_count` strategies.
The system will calculate the size of each batch automatically based on the total number of recipients.
Example: 5 → campaign will be sent in 5 equal or progressively sized batches.

CampaignDeferredBatchSize.description:
Campaign deferredBatchSize:
Defines the number of recipients to send in each batch (used with fixed_batches_by_size strategy).

CampaignDeferredInterval.description:
Campaign deferredInterval:
Defines the interval between each batch (e.g., 30 minutes, 1 hour).

CampaignDeferredStrategy.description:
Campaign deferredStrategy:
* `incremental` - Sends the campaign in a predefined number of batches at regular intervals. Each batch increases in size automatically.
* `fixed_batches_by_size` - Sends a fixed number of recipients in each batch (e.g., 5,000 recipients every 30 minutes).
* `fixed_batches_by_count` - Sends the campaign in a predefined number of batches, automatically calculating the size of each batch (e.g., 5 batches every 30 minutes).

CampaignDeliveryWarningCode.description:
Campaign delivery warning codes:
* `campaign.delivery_warning.no_active_subscribers` - No active subscribers (danger, blocks sending)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.insufficient_credits` - Insufficient credits (danger, blocks sending)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.daily_limit_exceeded` - Daily limit exceeded (warning, blocks sending)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.send_disabled` - Sending disabled (danger, blocks sending)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.approval_required` - Approval required (danger, blocks sending)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.approval_pending` - Approval pending (danger, blocks sending)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.cannot_send_without_authenticate` - Cannot send >1000 without auth (danger, blocks sending)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.sender_domain_not_authenticated` - Domain not authenticated (warning)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.custom_tracking_links_error` - Tracking links SSL/DNS error (warning)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.free_email_provider` - Free email provider (warning)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.domain_authentication_not_created` - Domain auth not created (warning)

CampaignSendTo.description:
Campaign sendTo:
* `send_to_all` - Send to all
* `send_to_segment` - Send to a saved segment
* `send_to_groups` - Send to one or more groups

min.description: Lower bound.

label.description: Name of the industry.

Contact.ContactCreateInput.description:
Contacts of the public API (plan fase 3, Task 16): the person, one record whatever the audiences they belong to.
Generated from the approved proposal by fase-3/tools/gen_contact_read.py and edited by hand afterwards: the texts
are the proposal's. Reads over ReadContacts; the writes (Tasks 17-18) are added to this resource.

additional_emails.description: Other email addresses of the same person. They identify the contact (for example to match incoming emails) but are never subscribed to an audience: only the primary `email` is used by marketing. Replaces the whole list; send `[]` to remove them.

additional_phones.description: Other phone numbers of the same person, in E.164 format. Never used by marketing, only the primary `phone` is. Replaces the whole list; send `[]` to remove them.

attributes.description: Attribute values keyed by the attribute `public_code`, for example `{"lead_source": "Webinar"}`. Get the codes, types and options with `list_contact_attributes`. `enum` and `multi_enum` attributes accept the UUID of an option or its exact label; `money` is `{amount, currency}`; `null` removes the value. An unknown or archived code is rejected with a 422. Attributes you leave out keep their value.

company.description: IRI of the company the contact works for (`/companies/{uuid}`). A contact has at most one company; changing or removing it does not affect their audiences, tasks or opportunities. Setting it requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. The company must already exist: create it first with `create_company`. `null` removes the link.

description.description: Free-text notes about the person.
description.example: Met at the Madrid e-commerce summit.

email.description: Primary email address. At least one of `email` or `phone` is required. It must not belong to another contact of the account (the other contact is not merged or updated).

facebook_url.description: Facebook profile, as a username (with or without `@`) or a URL. It is stored and returned as the full URL.

instagram_url.description: Instagram profile, as a username (with or without `@`) or a URL. It is stored and returned as the full URL.

job_title.description: Job title as free text (up to 190 characters).

linkedin_url.description: LinkedIn profile, as a username (with or without `@`) or a URL. It is stored and returned as the full URL.

locale.description: Language and region of the person, as a locale code such as `es_ES` or `en_US`.

location.description: Where the person lives. All fields are optional. Fields you leave out keep their value.

owner.description: Email of the user of the account in charge of this contact, exactly as they sign in. It must be an active user of the account. `null` leaves the contact without owner. Being the owner does not change who can see the contact.

phone.description: Primary phone number in E.164 format. At least one of `email` or `phone` is required. It must not belong to another contact.

tags.description: Tags of the contact, each one as the UUID of an existing tag or its name. A name that matches no tag (ignoring case) creates that tag. Check the existing tags with `list_contact_tags` first, so you reuse them instead of creating near-duplicates.

x_url.description: X profile, as a username (with or without `@`) or a URL. It is stored and returned as the full URL.

ContactAttributeType.description:
Contact attributes attribute type:
* `text` - Short text
* `long_text` - Long text, several lines
* `integer` - Whole number
* `decimal` - Decimal number
* `percentage` - Percentage
* `money` - Amount of money in the currency of the attribute
* `boolean` - Yes or no
* `date` - Calendar date
* `datetime` - Date and time
* `birthday` - Birthday (day and month, year optional)
* `enum` - One option from a list
* `multi_enum` - Several options from a list
* `email` - Email address
* `phone` - Phone number
* `url` - Web address
* `country` - Country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code)
* `language` - Language (ISO 639-1 code)
* `timezone` - IANA time zone name

name.description: Name of the segment, unique in the account (ignoring case and spaces), up to 190 characters.

revision_number.description: Number of the active revision. Every saved change of name or conditions publishes revision N+1; earlier revisions are kept for the campaigns that were scheduled or sent with them.

saved_views.description: Saved views of the Contacts list in Customer App that load the segment.

segments.description: Other segments that reference it. Always 0 for segments created today: definitions are flat and cannot reference segments.

uuid.description: UUID of the segment.

version.description: Version of the segment. It grows with every change (rename or new revision); send it as `expected_version` to change or delete the segment safely.

ContactSegment.ContactSegmentCreateInput.description:
Contact segments of the public API (fase 6): the global segments of Customer App, over ContactSegmentManager and its
readers in CoreBundle. Generated from the proposal by fase-6/tools/b_gen_contact_segments.py; the texts are the
proposal's. `filter` is the public conditions tree: the API never exposes the stored filter document or the editor
presentation, it builds both from the tree (ContactFilterTreeConverter) so the segment shows and edits in the app.

filter.description:
Which contacts match, written as the conditions editor of Customer App shows them: a top level with `match` (`all` = every item must hold, `any` = at least one) and `conditions`, a list of conditions and of groups. A group is `{match, conditions}` with conditions only: a group never contains another group. Up to 10 groups and 50 conditions in total.
A condition is `{field, operator, value, audience}`:
- `field`: the `id` of a field of `list_contact_filter_fields`.
- `operator`: one of that field's `operators[].id`.
- `value`: depends on the operator's `value_shape`: `none` = leave it out; `scalar` = one value; `set` = a list; `range` = `{lower, upper}`; `activity` = `{message_scope}` (see the field). For a field with `options`, copy the option's `value`; when the field has a `reference_type` (audience, group, tag, campaign, user…), the value is that record's UUID. Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- `audience`: UUID of an audience. Required, and only accepted, when the field has `audience_required: true` (the subscription fields: status, source, dates, groups, consent, forms and custom fields of an audience). Conditions on the same audience joined by `all` are checked on the same subscription.
To say «is subscribed to audience A» use the field `contact.audience_memberships` with `exists` and `audience`; `not_exists` means the person has no subscription to it, in any status.

CrmActorKind.description:
Kind of actor behind a CRM change:
* `user` - A person of the account
* `contact` - A contact
* `automation` - An automation
* `integration` - An integration
* `system` - Easymailing itself
* `external` - Someone outside the account

CrmFileOwnerType.description:
Kind of record a file is attached to:
* `contact` - A contact
* `company` - A company
* `opportunity` - An opportunity

CrmFileSource.description:
Where a CRM file is stored:
* `upload` - Stored in Easymailing

CrmFileStatus.description:
State of a CRM file:
* `uploading` - Declared, waiting for its content
* `analyzing` - Content received, being checked
* `available` - Stored and visible on its record

CrmInitiatedVia.description:
How a CRM record or change was made:
* `ui` - From the Easymailing app
* `maia` - By Maia, the assistant, on behalf of a person
* `api` - Through the API
* `import` - By a file import
* `sync` - By a synchronization with a connected service
* `automation` - By an automation
* `system` - By Easymailing itself

CrmRecordSource.description:
Where a CRM record came from:
* `manual` - Created by a person in the panel
* `api` - Created through the API
* `automation` - Created by an automation
* `connected_mailbox` - Created from a connected mailbox
* `connected_calendar` - Created from a connected calendar
* `integration` - Created by an integration
* `import` - Created by a file import
* `public_form` - Created from a public form
* `meeting_booking` - Created from a meeting booking

CrmTaskPriority.description:
Task priority:
* `none` - No priority set
* `low` - Low urgency
* `normal` - Normal urgency
* `high` - High urgency

CrmTaskType.description:
Task type. It only classifies the task:
* `general` - Any work
* `call` - A call to make
* `email` - An email to write

Email-email.list.description:
Synchronized emails of a record in the public API (fase 5). Generated from the proposal by
fase-5/tools/gen_emails_api.py; the texts are the proposal's. Every operation checks the CRM access in its provider
before anything else, because API Platform evaluates `security` after the provider.

Both operations need exactly one record in the query (`contact`, `company` or `opportunity`): the privacy of an
email (Bcc, visible edges, the open window of an opportunity) is decided per record, so there is no lookup of an
email on its own. The fields above the access level travel as `null`, never absent (`skip_null_values: false`).

`list_emails` pages forward only by cursor (`cursor[gt]`): `cursor` is the opaque position API Platform copies into
`hydra:next`, and {@see ForwardOnlyCursor} drops the `hydra:previous` it would also build. It is never published.
The images embedded in the body and the attachments are other resources (EmailInlineImagesResource and
EmailAttachmentContentResource): they read Gmail in the request.

access.description: What the user may see of this email, decided by the sharing level of the mailbox that holds it, the user's own mailboxes and the grants given to them. `metadata_only`: participants and date. `subject_and_metadata`: also the subject. `full_access`: also the snippet, body, attachments and AI summary. A field above the level comes as `null`, never absent.

ai_summary.description: AI summary of one or two sentences in the language of the email. Only when `ai_summary_state` is `ready`; `null` otherwise.
ai_summary.example: Ana accepts the annual plan and asks for quarterly invoices.

ai_summary_state.description: `null` when the email cannot carry a summary: it is outgoing, its content is not complete, the user lacks `full_access`, or AI summaries are off or not in the plan. Otherwise `none` (never requested), `pending`, `ready` or `failed`.

attachment_count.description: Number of attachments, not counting images embedded in the body. `null` without `full_access`.

can_share.description: Whether the user owns a mailbox that holds this email and can therefore share it with `set_email_access_grants`. People who were given access can never share it again.

content_state.description: Whether Easymailing already has the content. `index_only`: only participants and date are stored; the content is requested when you list it, so read again in a moment. `hydrating`: the content is being downloaded from Gmail. `full`: stored. `unavailable`: Gmail no longer has it and it cannot be recovered. While it is not `full`, subject, snippet and body come as `null`, which is not the same as being hidden by `access`.

direction.description: `incoming` if it was received in the mailbox, `outgoing` if it was sent from it.

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

mailboxes.description: The readable mailboxes that hold the email. The one that gives the user's access level comes first.

owner_name.description: Name of the member who connected the mailbox; `null` when they are no longer a member.

uuid.description: UUID of the mailbox (the connected Google account). Use it as the `mailbox` filter of `list_emails`.

occurred_at.description: When the email was sent or received, ISO 8601 (UTC).

participants.description: Everyone in the email (`from`, `to`, `cc` and, for the owner of the mailbox, `bcc`).

avatar_url.description: Photo of the member or contact. `null` for `shared_mailbox`, `internal` and `external`. For a contact it may be a Gravatar URL derived from the email, which may not exist.

contact.description: IRI of the contact when `kind` is `contact`; `null` otherwise.

kind.description: Who the address is for the reader, resolved when reading: `member` (an active member of the account), `shared_mailbox` (a shared mailbox such as sales@), `contact` (a CRM contact by its primary email or an alias), `internal` (internal address without identity, pending invitation or departed member) or `external`.

name.description: Name of the member or contact when it has one; otherwise the display name in the email header; `null` without either.

role.description: Role in the email. A `bcc` is only shown to the owner of the mailbox through which it was revealed, never to anyone else.

sender.description: The `from` participant; `null` if the email has none visible.

avatar_url.description: Photo of the member or contact. `null` for `shared_mailbox`, `internal` and `external`. For a contact it may be a Gravatar URL derived from the email, which may not exist.

contact.description: IRI of the contact when `kind` is `contact`; `null` otherwise.

kind.description: Who the address is for the reader, resolved when reading: `member` (an active member of the account), `shared_mailbox` (a shared mailbox such as sales@), `contact` (a CRM contact by its primary email or an alias), `internal` (internal address without identity, pending invitation or departed member) or `external`.

name.description: Name of the member or contact when it has one; otherwise the display name in the email header; `null` without either.

role.description: Role in the email. A `bcc` is only shown to the owner of the mailbox through which it was revealed, never to anyone else.

sent_by.description: The member who sent it from the CRM when the sender is a shared mailbox (for example "sales@, sent by Jhon"); `null` otherwise, also when it was written in Gmail.

avatar_url.description: Photo of that member.

uuid.description: UUID of the member who sent it.

snippet.description: Start of the text. `null` without `full_access` or while the content is not retrieved.
snippet.example: Thanks Sergio, we would like to move forward with the annual plan...

subject.description: Subject. `null` when the access level is `metadata_only` or the content has not been retrieved yet (see `content_state`).

uuid.description: UUID of the email.

EmailBatch-email_batch.read.description:
Email batches of the public API (fase 5): the same message as a separate email to each of 2 to 50 people. Generated
from the proposal by fase-5/tools/gen_email_sending_api.py; the texts are the proposal's. `sends` are the sends of the
batch with the fields of `get_email_send` and their `@id`. A batch belongs to its author: for anyone else it answers
404 `email_send_not_found`.

cancellable.description: `true` while at least one email of the batch is still queued.

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

release_at.description: Release time of the first email of the batch (the others follow at least five minutes apart, within the mailbox limits).

sends.description: One send per recipient, each with the same fields as `get_email_send`.

uuid.description: UUID of the batch.

EmailBatch.EmailBatchScheduleInput.description:
Email batches of the public API (fase 5): the same message as a separate email to each of 2 to 50 people. Generated
from the proposal by fase-5/tools/gen_email_sending_api.py; the texts are the proposal's. `sends` are the sends of the
batch with the fields of `get_email_send` and their `@id`. A batch belongs to its author: for anyone else it answers
404 `email_send_not_found`.

acknowledged_opt_outs.description: Addresses of recipients who asked not to receive CRM email and that the user has confirmed they still want to write to. Leave it out unless a previous attempt answered `recipient_opted_out`.

attachment_ids.description: UUIDs of files uploaded with `upload_email_attachment` that go with the email. Up to 100; 25 MB in total between attachments, inline images and forwarded files.

bcc.description: Addresses in Bcc. Must be empty in a batch.

body_html.description:
Body of the email as limited HTML: paragraphs, line breaks, headings, bold, italic, underline, links, lists, quotes, tables and images. Scripts and unknown markup are removed. Three special pieces are understood: (1) a personalization chip `First name`, filled in for the recipient when the email leaves (ids from `list_email_personalization_tags`; the fallback is optional); (2) the signature, which is not added for you: paste the `html` of the signature you want from `list_email_senders` at the end; (3) an optional unsubscribe block `
`, which becomes a signed opt-out link (see `get_contact_email_opt_out`). Without that block the email carries no unsubscribe link. When replying or forwarding, the quoted original is added for you; do not paste it.
body_html.example:
Hi First name,

Here is the proposal we talked about.

cc.description: Addresses in Cc. Must be empty in a batch.

draft.description: IRI of the draft this email comes from (`/email_drafts/{uuid}`). The draft is deleted in the same transaction that creates the send. Optional.

forwarded_attachment_ids.description: Only with `mode` `forward`: ids of attachments of the original email to forward too (up to 40). They are downloaded from Gmail when the email leaves.

idempotency_key.description: A UUID you generate for this intended email. Repeating the request with the same key returns the same send instead of creating a second email, so reuse it only to retry after a timeout or a 503. Use a new UUID for every new email.

mode.description: `compose` (default) writes a new email. `reply`, `reply_all` and `forward` answer `source_email`, quote it and keep the thread (reply, reply_all) or attach its files (forward).

record.description: IRI of the record the email is written from and recorded on: `/contacts/{uuid}`, `/companies/{uuid}` or `/opportunities/{uuid}`. The recipient addresses do not have to belong to it.

replaces_send.description: IRI of a failed or unconfirmed send of the user (`/email_sends/{uuid}`) that this email replaces: it is discarded in the same transaction, so both never exist. A send that is alive (queued, sending or sent) gives 409 `replaced_send_changed`. Optional.

scheduled_at.description: When the email must leave: ISO 8601 date-time WITH a time zone offset, from 90 seconds to 365 days ahead. The effective time (`release_at`) can be later if the mailbox is at its limit. There is no undo window for a scheduled email, but it can be cancelled until it starts to leave.

sender_uuid.description: UUID of the mailbox to send from, taken from `list_email_senders`.

source_email.description: IRI of the email being answered or forwarded (`/emails/{uuid}`). Required unless `mode` is `compose`. The user must be able to see the whole original.

subject.description: Subject, up to 998 characters. It may contain personalization tags written as `{{ contact.first_name | default: "there" }}` (ids from `list_email_personalization_tags`). Line breaks are turned into spaces. Replies and forwards keep the original subject: write `Re: ...` or `Fwd: ...` yourself if you want it.

to.description: Recipients, one email each: 2 to 50 plain email addresses. Each gets their own email and their own unsubscribe link; they do not see each other.

Whether the content of an email is stored:
* `index_only` - Only participants and date; the content is requested when listed
* `hydrating` - The content is being downloaded
* `full` - The content is stored
* `unavailable` - The content cannot be retrieved

EmailDirection.description:
Direction of an email:
* `incoming` - Received in the mailbox
* `outgoing` - Sent from the mailbox

EmailDraft.description:
Email drafts of the public API (fase 5). Generated from the proposal by fase-5/tools/gen_email_sending_api.py; the
texts are the proposal's. Every operation checks the CRM access in its provider or processor before anything else,
because API Platform evaluates `security` after the provider.

A draft belongs to its author: for anyone else it answers 404 `email_draft_not_found`. `create_email_draft` and
`update_email_draft` answer without `body_html` (the panel's use case returns the draft without its body, so that an
autosave never echoes megabytes); `get_email_draft` has it.

body_html.description: Body of the draft. Only returned by `get_email_draft`; the list and the answers of create and update leave it out.
body_html.example: Hi Ana,

forwarded_attachment_ids.description: Attachments of the original email chosen to be forwarded.

mode.description: `compose`, `reply`, `reply_all` or `forward`.

record.description: IRI of the contact, company or opportunity the draft is written from; null if none.

record_name.description: Name of the record; null if none.

revision.description: Version of the draft, 1 on creation and +1 on every save. Send it back in `update_email_draft` so two saves cannot overwrite each other.

sender_uuid.description: UUID of the mailbox chosen to send from; null if none was chosen or the user lost access to it.

source_email.description: IRI of the email being answered or forwarded; null for `compose`.

subject.description: Subject; null if not written yet.

to.description: Addresses in To, as typed (they are not validated until the email is sent).

uuid.description: UUID of the draft.

EmailDraft.EmailDraftCreateInput.description:

attachment_ids.description: UUIDs of files uploaded with `upload_email_attachment` that belong to the draft (up to 100, 25 MB in total). Files no longer listed are detached and deleted.

body_html.description:
Body of the email as limited HTML: paragraphs, line breaks, headings, bold, italic, underline, links, lists, quotes, tables and images. Scripts and unknown markup are removed. Three special pieces are understood: (1) a personalization chip `First name`, filled in for the recipient when the email leaves (ids from `list_email_personalization_tags`; the fallback is optional); (2) the signature, which is not added for you: paste the `html` of the signature you want from `list_email_senders` at the end; (3) an optional unsubscribe block `
`, which becomes a signed opt-out link (see `get_contact_email_opt_out`). Without that block the email carries no unsubscribe link. When replying or forwarding, the quoted original is added for you; do not paste it.
body_html.example:
Hi Ana,

Here is the proposal we talked about.

forwarded_attachment_ids.description: Only for `forward`: attachments of the original email to forward (up to 100).

mode.description: `compose` (default), `reply`, `reply_all` or `forward`.

record.description: IRI of the record the email is written from: `/contacts/{uuid}`, `/companies/{uuid}` or `/opportunities/{uuid}`. Optional in a draft; required when the email is sent. A contact that does not exist is ignored; a company or opportunity the user cannot send from is refused.

sender_uuid.description: UUID of the mailbox to send from (`list_email_senders`). Optional in a draft; it is required when the email is sent.

source_email.description: IRI of the email being answered or forwarded (`/emails/{uuid}`).

subject.description: Subject, up to 998 characters. It may contain personalization tags written as `{{ contact.first_name | default: "there" }}` (ids from `list_email_personalization_tags`). Line breaks are turned into spaces. Replies and forwards keep the original subject: write `Re: ...` or `Fwd: ...` yourself if you want it.

to.description: Addresses in To. A draft may be incomplete: addresses are kept as typed, lower-cased, without repeats.

EmailDraft.EmailDraftUpdateInput.description:

texts are the proposal's. Every operation checks the CRM access in its provider or processor before anything else,
because API Platform evaluates `security` after the provider.

A draft belongs to its author: for anyone else it answers 404 `email_draft_not_found`. `create_email_draft` and
`update_email_draft` answer without `body_html` (the panel's use case returns the draft without its body, so that an
autosave never echoes megabytes); `get_email_draft` has it.

body_html.description:
Body of the email as limited HTML: paragraphs, line breaks, headings, bold, italic, underline, links, lists, quotes, tables and images. Scripts and unknown markup are removed. `, which becomes a signed opt-out link (see `get_contact_email_opt_out`). Without that block the email carries no unsubscribe link. When replying or forwarding, the quoted original is added for you; do not paste it.

EmailSend-email_send.read.description:
Email sends of the public API (fase 5). Generated from the proposal by fase-5/tools/gen_email_sending_api.py; the
texts are the proposal's. Every operation checks the CRM access in its provider or processor before anything else,
because API Platform evaluates `security` after the provider.

Sending and scheduling are two operations over the same use case (QueueEmailSend): `send_email` takes no
`scheduled_at` and `schedule_email` requires it. Both answer 202: the email is queued and the `worker` sends it.
The actions (`cancel`, `send_now`, `retry`, `discard`) take no body and answer the send as it is afterwards. A send
belongs to its author: for anyone else it answers 404 `email_send_not_found`.

batch.description: IRI of the batch it belongs to when it was sent with `send_email_batch`; null for a single email.

canceled_at.description: When it was cancelled; null otherwise.

contact.description: IRI of the contact the email is linked to, or null when it was written from a company or opportunity.

copy_visible.description: Whether the copy synced from Gmail will appear in the email history of the record. Null until it is known; false when the mailbox rules hide it.

draft.description: IRI of the draft this email comes from (`/email_drafts/{uuid}`). The draft is deleted in the same transaction that creates the send. Optional.

sender_uuid.description: UUID of the mailbox to send from, taken from `list_email_senders`.

source_email.description: IRI of the email being answered or forwarded (`/emails/{uuid}`). Required unless `mode` is `compose`. The user must be able to see the whole original.

subject.description: Subject, up to 998 characters. It may contain personalization tags written as `{{ contact.first_name | default: "there" }}` (ids from `list_email_personalization_tags`). to.description: Addresses in To (plain email addresses, no display names). Up to 500 addresses between `to`, `cc` and `bcc`. All of them get the same single email and see each other.

EmailSendState.description:
State of the send:
* `queued` - Waiting for its time; it can be cancelled
* `sending` - Leaving now
* `sent` - Gmail accepted it
* `failed` - It did not leave, see `failure_reason`
* `unconfirmed` - Gmail's answer was unclear: it may or may not have left
* `canceled` - Cancelled before leaving

EmailSequence-email_sequence.list.description:
Email sequences of the public API (fase 5). Generated from the proposal by fase-5/tools/gen_email_sequences_api.py;
the texts are the proposal's. Every operation checks its capability in the provider or processor before anything
else ({@see \App\Application\Crm\ApiEmailSequenceAccess}), because API Platform evaluates `security` after the
provider. The rules, transactions and authority live in the CoreBundle use cases (`Service\App\Automation\Sequences`).

The list shows the summary; every other operation answers the whole sequence as it is afterwards. `delete` answers
202 without a body: the purge ends in the background (EmailSequenceTombstone). `/email_sequences/personalization_tags`
is list_email_sequence_personalization_tags, not a sequence.

can_enroll.description: Whether the user who owns the token can enroll contacts right now: the sequence is `active`, its published sender is sound and the user owns that mailbox or has the send permission on it.

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

last_activity_at.description: Last event of the sequence (enrollment, send, exit…), ISO 8601. `null` while nothing has happened.

published_revision.description: Revision number of the current published version; 0 when it was never published.

published_sender.description: Sender (mailbox and signature) of the current published version: the one every new enrollment uses. `null` without a published version or sender.

address.description: Address of that mailbox. `null` when the mailbox no longer exists in the account.

mailbox.description: UUID of the connected Gmail mailbox the emails are sent from.

signature.description: UUID of the signature of that mailbox added to every email, or `null` for none.

signature_name.description: Name of that signature. `null` without signature or when it no longer exists.

status.description: State of the sequence. `draft`: never published. `active`: published and open to new enrollments. `paused`: published but closed to new enrollments and sending nothing to anybody (paused with `pause_email_sequence`, or just restored). `archived`: hidden from the default list and closed to new enrollments, but the enrollments already running keep sending. `commercial-paused`: paused by Easymailing because the account lost CRM Pro; `reactivate_email_sequence` brings it back.

title.description: Name of the sequence, up to 120 characters. Empty in sequences created before titles existed: see `untitled`.

total_days.description: Sum of the days of the waits in the draft: how long the sequence lasts from its first email to its last.

unpublished_changes.description: The draft differs from the published version: what you edited is not what new enrollments will send until `publish_email_sequence`.

updated_at.description: When the sequence was last edited or published, ISO 8601.

updated_by.description: UUID of the account member who last edited or published it.

uuid.description: UUID of the sequence.

can_enroll.description: Whether the user who owns the token can enroll contacts right now: the sequence is `active`, its published sender is sound and the user owns that mailbox or has the send permission on it.

draft_version.description: Concurrency token of the draft. Send it back as `expected_draft_version` to `update_email_sequence_draft` and `publish_email_sequence`; every save and publish raises it.

exit_on_meeting.description: A meeting booked by the contact ends the enrollment.

exit_on_reply.description: A human reply from the contact ends the enrollment (automatic replies only pause it).

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

last_activity_at.description: Last event of the sequence (enrollment, send, exit…), ISO 8601. `null` while nothing has happened.

meeting_exit_undetectable.description: Some live enrollment exits on meetings but its mailbox has no Google Calendar connected for reading, so that exit cannot be detected.

published_revision.description: Revision number of the current published version; 0 when it was never published.

published_sender.description: Sender (mailbox and signature) of the current published version: the one every new enrollment uses. `null` without a published version or sender.

address.description: Address of that mailbox. `null` when the mailbox no longer exists in the account.

mailbox.description: UUID of the connected Gmail mailbox the emails are sent from.

signature.description: UUID of the signature of that mailbox added to every email, or `null` for none.

signature_name.description: Name of that signature. `null` without signature or when it no longer exists.

schedule.description: When emails may leave: days of the week and daily window. A wait is a minimum; the real send moves to the next slot this allows.

end.description: End of the window (exclusive), `HH:00` or `HH:30`, later than `start`.

start.description: Start of the daily sending window, `HH:00` or `HH:30` (24-hour clock, inclusive), in the effective time zone.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone used for contacts that have none of their own (the time zone of the contact always comes first). `null` falls back to the time zone of the sender, then UTC.

weekdays.description: Days of the week emails may leave, in week order, without repeats: `mon`, `tue`, `wed`, `thu`, `fri`, `sat`, `sun`.

sender.description: Sender (mailbox and signature) chosen in the draft, shown even if the user cannot send from it. `null` while none is chosen; a sequence without sender cannot be published.

address.description: Address of that mailbox. `null` when the mailbox no longer exists in the account.

mailbox.description: UUID of the connected Gmail mailbox the emails are sent from.

signature.description: UUID of the signature of that mailbox added to every email, or `null` for none.

signature_name.description: Name of that signature. `null` without signature or when it no longer exists.

sender_problem.description: Why the current published version takes no new enrollments because of its sender: `missing` (no sender), `mailbox_unavailable` (disconnected or unusable), `not_allowed` (whoever published it lost the send permission) or `signature_missing` (the signature is gone). `null` when sound or unpublished.

stats.description: Counts of the sequence: enrollments by exit reason and emails sent. `get_email_sequence_statistics` adds replies per email and a daily series.

bounced.description: Enrollments that ended because an email bounced.

enrolled.description: Every enrollment ever created, live or finished.

excluded.description: Enrollments that ended for any other reason than the ones above and completion (manual exclusion, invalid or suppressed address, contact removed…).

meetings.description: Enrollments that ended because the contact booked a meeting.

replied.description: Enrollments that ended because the contact replied.

unsubscribed.description: Enrollments that ended because the contact unsubscribed.

status.description: State of the sequence. `draft`: never published. `active`: published and open to new enrollments. `paused`: published but closed to new enrollments and sending nothing to anybody (paused with `pause_email_sequence`, or just restored). `archived`: hidden from the default list and closed to new enrollments, but the enrollments already running keep sending. `commercial-paused`: paused by Easymailing because the account lost CRM Pro; `reactivate_email_sequence` brings it back.

step_stats.description: Emails sent per email of the current published version.

steps.description: The steps of the DRAFT, in order.

attachments.description: Files attached to an `email` step, at most 10 per email and 25 MB in total. Upload each with `upload_email_sequence_asset` first. Not sent for `wait` steps.

asset_uuid.description: UUID you chose when you uploaded the file with `upload_email_sequence_asset`.

filename.description: Name of the file. Read only: ignored if sent.

mime_type.description: Media type of the file. Read only: ignored if sent.

size_bytes.description: Size of the file in bytes. Read only: ignored if sent.

days.description: Length of a `wait` step in whole days, 1 to 365. A wait is a minimum: the real send moves to the next slot the schedule allows. Only for `wait` steps.

html.description: Body of an `email` step as HTML, up to 131,072 characters, in the form the Customer App editor writes. Personalization goes in chips: `First name` (`data-email-tag-id` from `list_email_sequence_personalization_tags`, `data-email-tag-fallback` is the default when the contact has no value, `data-email-tag-required` holds the email until the contact has a value). Do NOT write the unsubscribe footer here: it is built from `unsubscribe`, and one written by hand is removed. Not sent for `wait` steps.
html.example:
Hi First name,

Thanks for your time on Tuesday. Shall I send you the proposal?

kind.description: `email` sends an email; `wait` pauses the enrollment. The first step must be an email, two emails need a wait between them and the last step must be an email to publish.

subject.description: Subject of an `email` step, up to 255 characters. With `threading` on, only the first email has a subject; the follow-ups MUST send `null` (they reply in the same thread with «Re: » and the first subject). Personalization in the subject uses `{{ tag.id }}` or `{{ tag.id | default: "there" }}`. Not sent for `wait` steps.

unsubscribe.description: Footer of an `email` step that lets the recipient unsubscribe. Mandatory to publish. Not sent for `wait` steps.

example.prefix: If you do not want to receive more personal follow-ups, you can unsubscribe

language.description: Language of the footer text as a BCP-47 tag made of a supported locale, such as `en-US` or `es-ES`. A language Easymailing is not translated into is refused when the sequence is published.

link_label.description: Text of the unsubscribe link, up to 64 characters. Cannot be empty to publish.

prefix.description: Text before the unsubscribe link, up to 255 characters. It must not end with the link word (that is `link_label`). Cannot be empty to publish.
prefix.example: If you do not want to receive more personal follow-ups, you can unsubscribe

template_id.description: Wording family the footer was written from.

uuid.description: Identifier of the step, a lowercase UUID chosen by you (generate a new one for a new step; keep the existing one to keep a step). Unique within the sequence.

variables.description: Personalization tags used by an `email` step, one entry per distinct tag found in its subject and body (no more, no fewer: otherwise `variable_undeclared` or `variable_unused` stops the publication). Send `fallback` as an empty string (the default value lives in the chip) and `required: true` only for tags whose chip carries `data-email-tag-required`. Maximum 50. Not sent for `wait` steps.

fallback.description: Always an empty string: the default value of a tag is stored in its chip or its `default:` filter.

required.description: Whether the email is held until the contact has a value for the tag (it leaves the sequence if it stays empty for 72 hours).

tag.description: Tag id, as in `list_email_sequence_personalization_tags`.

threading.description: Follow-ups keep the first subject and reply in the same email thread (default `true`).

title.description: Name of the sequence, up to 120 characters. Empty in sequences created before titles existed: see `untitled`.

total_days.description: Sum of the days of the waits in the draft: how long the sequence lasts from its first email to its last.

unpublished_changes.description: The draft differs from the published version: what you edited is not what new enrollments will send until `publish_email_sequence`.

updated_at.description: When the sequence was last edited or published, ISO 8601.

updated_by.description: UUID of the account member who last edited or published it.

uuid.description: UUID of the sequence.

versions.description: Published versions, newest first. Read one with `get_email_sequence_version`.

published_by.description: UUID of the account member who published it.

exit_on_reply.description: A human reply from the contact ends the enrollment. Automatic replies (out of office) only pause it.

expected_draft_version.description: `draft_version` of the sequence as you read it. If someone saved in between you get `draft_version_conflict` and nothing is saved.

schedule.description: When emails may leave: days of the week and a daily window. A wait is a minimum; the real send moves to the next slot this allows.

start.description: Start of the daily sending window, `HH:00` or `HH:30` (24-hour clock, inclusive), in the effective time zone.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone used for contacts that have none of their own (the time zone of the contact always comes first). `null` falls back to the time zone of the sender, then UTC.

weekdays.description: Days of the week emails may leave, in week order, without repeats: `mon`, `tue`, `wed`, `thu`, `fri`, `sat`, `sun`.

sender.description: Mailbox and signature the emails are sent from. `null` leaves it unset, which makes the sequence unpublishable. You must own the mailbox or hold its send permission on a shared one; the signature must belong to that mailbox.

mailbox.description: UUID of a connected Gmail mailbox you can send from: your own, or a shared one where you have the send permission. Get it from `list_email_senders`.

signature.description: UUID of a signature of that mailbox (also from `list_email_senders`), or `null` for none.

steps.description: ALL the steps of the sequence in order, replacing the current ones. Up to 60 steps and 20 emails. Every step carries exactly the keys of its `kind` (`email`: `uuid`, `kind`, `subject`, `html`, `unsubscribe`, `variables`, `attachments`; `wait`: `uuid`, `kind`, `days`).

kind.description: `email` sends an email; `wait` pauses the enrollment. The first step must be an email, two emails need a wait between them and the last step must be an email to publish.

subject.description: Subject of an `email` step, up to 255 characters. With `threading` on, only the first email has a subject; the follow-ups MUST send `null` (they reply in the same thread with «Re: » and the first subject). Personalization in the subject uses `{{ tag.id }}` or `{{ tag.id | default: "there" }}`. Not sent for `wait` steps.

unsubscribe.description: Footer of an `email` step that lets the recipient unsubscribe. Mandatory to publish. Not sent for `wait` steps.

example.prefix: If you do not want to receive more personal follow-ups, you can unsubscribe

language.description: Language of the footer text as a BCP-47 tag made of a supported locale, such as `en-US` or `es-ES`. A language Easymailing is not translated into is refused when the sequence is published.

link_label.description: Text of the unsubscribe link, up to 64 characters. Cannot be empty to publish.

prefix.description: Text before the unsubscribe link, up to 255 characters. It must not end with the link word (that is `link_label`). Cannot be empty to publish.

template_id.description: Wording family the footer was written from.

uuid.description: Identifier of the step, a lowercase UUID chosen by you (generate a new one for a new step; keep the existing one to keep a step). Unique within the sequence.

variables.description: Personalization tags used by an `email` step, one entry per distinct tag found in its subject and body (no more, no fewer: otherwise `variable_undeclared` or `variable_unused` stops the publication). Send `fallback` as an empty string (the default value lives in the chip) and `required: true` only for tags whose chip carries `data-email-tag-required`. Maximum 50. Not sent for `wait` steps.

fallback.description: Always an empty string: the default value of a tag is stored in its chip or its `default:` filter.

required.description: Whether the email is held until the contact has a value for the tag (it leaves the sequence if it stays empty for 72 hours).

tag.description: Tag id, as in `list_email_sequence_personalization_tags`.

threading.description: On: the first email creates the thread and the follow-ups reply in it, keeping the first subject (their `subject` must be `null`). Off: every email is separate and needs its own subject.

title.description: Name of the sequence, 1 to 120 characters.

can_enroll.description: Whether the user who owns the token can enroll contacts right now: the sequence is `active`, its published sender is sound and the user owns that mailbox or has the send permission on it.

last_activity_at.description: Last event of the sequence (enrollment, send, exit…), ISO 8601. `null` while nothing has happened.

published_revision.description: Revision number of the current published version; 0 when it was never published.

published_sender.description: Sender (mailbox and signature) of the current published version: the one every new enrollment uses. `null` without a published version or sender.

signature.description: UUID of the signature of that mailbox added to every email, or `null` for none.

updated_by.description: UUID of the account member who last edited or published it.

uuid.description: UUID of the sequence.
