exit_on_meeting.description: A meeting booked by the contact ends the enrollment.

exit_on_reply.description: A human reply from the contact ends the enrollment (automatic replies only pause it).

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

meeting_exit_undetectable.description: Some live enrollment exits on meetings but its mailbox has no Google Calendar connected for reading, so that exit cannot be detected.

published_revision.description: Revision number of the current published version; 0 when it was never published.

published_sender.description: Sender (mailbox and signature) of the current published version: the one every new enrollment uses. `null` without a published version or sender.

address.description: Address of that mailbox. `null` when the mailbox no longer exists in the account.

mailbox.description: UUID of the connected Gmail mailbox the emails are sent from.

signature.description: UUID of the signature of that mailbox added to every email, or `null` for none.

signature_name.description: Name of that signature. `null` without signature or when it no longer exists.

schedule.description: When emails may leave: days of the week and daily window. A wait is a minimum; the real send moves to the next slot this allows.

end.description: End of the window (exclusive), `HH:00` or `HH:30`, later than `start`.

start.description: Start of the daily sending window, `HH:00` or `HH:30` (24-hour clock, inclusive), in the effective time zone.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone used for contacts that have none of their own (the time zone of the contact always comes first). `null` falls back to the time zone of the sender, then UTC.

weekdays.description: Days of the week emails may leave, in week order, without repeats: `mon`, `tue`, `wed`, `thu`, `fri`, `sat`, `sun`.

sender.description: Sender (mailbox and signature) chosen in the draft, shown even if the user cannot send from it. `null` while none is chosen; a sequence without sender cannot be published.

address.description: Address of that mailbox. `null` when the mailbox no longer exists in the account.

mailbox.description: UUID of the connected Gmail mailbox the emails are sent from.

signature.description: UUID of the signature of that mailbox added to every email, or `null` for none.

signature_name.description: Name of that signature. `null` without signature or when it no longer exists.

sender_problem.description: Why the current published version takes no new enrollments because of its sender: `missing` (no sender), `mailbox_unavailable` (disconnected or unusable), `not_allowed` (whoever published it lost the send permission) or `signature_missing` (the signature is gone). `null` when sound or unpublished.

stats.description: Counts of the sequence: enrollments by exit reason and emails sent. `get_email_sequence_statistics` adds replies per email and a daily series.

bounced.description: Enrollments that ended because an email bounced.

enrolled.description: Every enrollment ever created, live or finished.

excluded.description: Enrollments that ended for any other reason than the ones above and completion (manual exclusion, invalid or suppressed address, contact removed…).

meetings.description: Enrollments that ended because the contact booked a meeting.

replied.description: Enrollments that ended because the contact replied.

unsubscribed.description: Enrollments that ended because the contact unsubscribed.

status.description: State of the sequence. `draft`: never published. `active`: published and open to new enrollments. `paused`: published but closed to new enrollments and sending nothing to anybody (paused with `pause_email_sequence`, or just restored). `archived`: hidden from the default list and closed to new enrollments, but the enrollments already running keep sending. `commercial-paused`: paused by Easymailing because the account lost CRM Pro; `reactivate_email_sequence` brings it back.

step_stats.description: Emails sent per email of the current published version.

steps.description: The steps of the DRAFT, in order.

EmailSequenceEnrollmentOutcome.description:
What happened to the contact:
* `enrolled` - It was enrolled
* `skipped` - It was not enrolled on purpose, see `reason`
* `failed` - An error that applies to the whole request, see `reason`

EmailSequenceEnrollmentReason.description:
Why the contact was skipped or failed:
* `reentered` - Enrolled again after finishing this sequence before
* `no_email` - No valid primary email
* `opted_out` - The address unsubscribed from CRM emails
* `enrollment_conflict` - The address is already in a live sequence
* `recipient_not_contact_email` - The address is no longer an address of the contact
* `contact_not_found` - The contact does not exist in the account
* `sequence_not_publishable_entry` - The sequence no longer takes enrollments
* `sender_not_allowed` - The user cannot send from the mailbox of the sequence
* `sequence_sender_missing` - The published version has no sender
* `sequence_sender_revoked` - The publisher lost the send permission
* `mailbox_unavailable` - The mailbox is disconnected or cannot send
* `signature_foreign` - The signature is not of that mailbox

EmailSequenceEnrollmentRun-email_sequenc.description:
`enroll_contacts_in_email_sequence` (fase 5, decision 36): the outcome of enrolling up to 25 contacts, one entry per
contact. Generated from the proposal by fase-5/tools/gen_email_sequences_api.py; the texts are the proposal's. A POST
that answers 200: it creates enrollments, not a resource with a reading of its own. `uuid` is only the path.

failed.description: Contacts that could not be enrolled because of an error that applies to the request.

results.description: One entry per contact, in the order sent. `outcome` is `enrolled` (`reason` is `reentered` when the contact had already finished this sequence before and entered again), `skipped` or `failed`. A contact is `skipped` with `reason` `no_email` (no valid primary email), `opted_out` (the address unsubscribed from CRM emails), `enrollment_conflict` (that address is already in a live sequence: an address can be in only one at a time), `recipient_not_contact_email` or `contact_not_found`. If the engine refuses something that applies to the whole request while enrolling (`sequence_not_publishable_entry`, `sender_not_allowed`, `sequence_sender_missing`, `sequence_sender_revoked`, `mailbox_unavailable` or `signature_foreign`), that contact is `failed` with that `reason` and every contact after it is `skipped` with the same `reason`.

reason.description: Why it was skipped or failed, or `reentered` for an enrolled contact that had finished this sequence before. `null` otherwise.

skipped.description: Contacts not enrolled on purpose, see `reason`.

uuid.description: Trailing UUID segment of the entity IRI. Convenience derived from `iri`; absent when the IRI doesn't end in a UUID.

EmailSequenceEnrollmentStatus.description:
State of the enrollment:
* `scheduled` - Waiting for its start
* `active` - Receiving the emails
* `technical-error` - An email could not be sent; retry or exclude it
* `completed` - Received every email
* `excluded` - Taken out by a person or by the system
* `bounced` - An email bounced
* `replied` - The contact replied
* `meeting-booked` - The contact booked a meeting
* `automatic-reply` - Paused by an automatic reply
* `paused` - Paused by a person

EmailSequenceEventType.description:
Type of event:
* `enrolled` - A contact was enrolled
* `email_sent` - An email was sent
* `exited` - An enrollment ended before the last email
* `completed` - An enrollment received every email
* `paused` - The sequence or an enrollment was paused
* `resumed` - The sequence or an enrollment was resumed
* `failed` - An email could not be sent
* `retried` - A failed email was retried
* `commercial_paused` - The sequence was paused because the account lost the CRM Pro plan
* `reactivated` - The sequence was reactivated after the commercial pause
* `archived` - The sequence was archived
* `restored` - The sequence was restored

EmailSequenceExitReason.description:
Why the enrollment ended:
* `completed` - Every email was sent
* `reply` - The contact replied
* `meeting_booked` - The contact booked a meeting
* `unsubscribe` - The contact unsubscribed
* `bounce` - An email bounced
* `invalid_address` - The address is not valid
* `suppressed` - The address is in the suppression list
* `commercial_block` - The account lost the CRM Pro plan
* `manual_exclusion` - A person excluded it
* `subject_removed` - The contact was removed
* `missing_required_data` - A required personalization tag had no value

code.description: What is wrong. `missing_email`: no email step. `first_step_email`: the first step is a wait. `wait_required`: two emails in a row, or the sequence ends in a wait. `minimum_wait`: a wait is not 1 to 365 days. `empty_subject`: an email that needs a subject has none. `empty_rich_body`: an email has no visible text. `mandatory_unsubscribe`: the footer `prefix` or `link_label` is empty. `unsupported_unsubscribe_language`: the footer language is not one Easymailing is translated into. `variable_undeclared`: a tag is used but not in `variables`. `variable_unused`: a tag is in `variables` but not used. `unknown_tag`: a tag id is not in `list_email_sequence_personalization_tags`. `attachment_missing`: an attachment file does not exist. `attachments_too_large`: the attachments of one email add up to more than 25 MB. `too_many_emails`: more than 20 emails. `sender_missing`: no sender chosen. `sender_unavailable`: the mailbox is disconnected or cannot send. `sender_not_allowed`: the user cannot send from the mailbox. `signature_missing`: the signature is not of that mailbox.

severity.description: Always `error` today: every problem stops the publication.

step_uuid.description: `uuid` of the step the problem is in. `null` when it affects the whole sequence.

attachments.description: Files attached to an `email` step, at most 10 per email and 25 MB in total. Upload each with `upload_email_sequence_asset` first. Not sent for `wait` steps.

html.description: Body of an `email` step as HTML, up to 131,072 characters, in the form the Customer App editor writes. Personalization goes in chips: `First name` (`data-email-tag-id` from `list_email_sequence_personalization_tags`, `data-email-tag-fallback` is the default when the contact has no value, `data-email-tag-required` holds the email until the contact has a value). Do NOT write the unsubscribe footer here: it is built from `unsubscribe`, and one written by hand is removed. Not sent for `wait` steps.

Hi First name,

Thanks for your time on Tuesday. Shall I send you the proposal?

kind.description: `email` sends an email; `wait` pauses the enrollment. The first step must be an email, two emails need a wait between them and the last step must be an email to publish.

subject.description: Subject of an `email` step, up to 255 characters. With `threading` on, only the first email has a subject; the follow-ups MUST send `null` (they reply in the same thread with «Re: » and the first subject). Personalization in the subject uses `{{ tag.id }}` or `{{ tag.id | default: "there" }}`. Not sent for `wait` steps.

unsubscribe.description: Footer of an `email` step that lets the recipient unsubscribe. Mandatory to publish. Not sent for `wait` steps.

example.prefix: If you do not want to receive more personal follow-ups, you can unsubscribe

language.description: Language of the footer text as a BCP-47 tag made of a supported locale, such as `en-US` or `es-ES`. A language Easymailing is not translated into is refused when the sequence is published.

link_label.description: Text of the unsubscribe link, up to 64 characters. Cannot be empty to publish.

prefix.description: Text before the unsubscribe link, up to 255 characters. It must not end with the link word (that is `link_label`). Cannot be empty to publish.
prefix.example: If you do not want to receive more personal follow-ups, you can unsubscribe

template_id.description: Wording family the footer was written from.

uuid.description: Identifier of the step, a lowercase UUID chosen by you (generate a new one for a new step; keep the existing one to keep a step). Unique within the sequence.

variables.description: Personalization tags used by an `email` step, one entry per distinct tag found in its subject and body (no more, no fewer: otherwise `variable_undeclared` or `variable_unused` stops the publication). exit_on_meeting.description: A booked meeting ends the enrollment.

exit_on_reply.description: A human reply ends the enrollment.

schedule.description: When emails of this version may leave.

sender.description: Sender frozen with this version. `null` in versions published without one (they take no new enrollments).

signature.description: UUID of the signature of that mailbox added to every email, or `null` for none.

File.description:
CRM Files of the public API (fase 5). Generated from the proposal by fase-5/tools/gen_files_api.py and edited by hand
afterwards: the texts are the proposal's. Every operation checks the CRM access in its provider or processor before
anything else, because API Platform evaluates `security` after the provider.

Two operations are binary, as in the panel's internal API: `set_file_content` takes the raw bytes (`deserialize:
false`, its `Content-Type` is checked by the processor before the body is opened) and `get_file_content` answers a
streamed attachment (`output: false`, `serialize: false`). Their bodies are declared by hand in `openapiContext`.

`list_files` pages forward only by cursor (`cursor[gt]`, the use case has no backwards page): `cursor` is the opaque
position API Platform copies into `hydra:next`, and {@see ForwardOnlyCursor} drops the `hydra:previous` it would also
build. It is never published.

created_at.description: When the file was declared, ISO 8601.

created_by.description: Person or system that uploaded the file. `null` when unknown.

kind.description: Kind of actor: `user` for a person, otherwise `contact`, `automation`, `integration`, `system` or `external`.

name.description: Name of the actor. `null` when the person is no longer a member of the account, and in the response of `create_file` (the name is filled in by later reads).

uuid.description: Identifier of the uploader. Use it as the `created_by` filter of `list_files`.

description.description: Optional description, up to 2,000 characters. `null` when it has none.
description.example: Version signed by the client

display_name.description: Name the file is shown with. It starts as the `filename` sent to `create_file` and can be changed with `update_file`, keeping the same extension. Up to 255 characters.

mime_type.description: Media type of the file, decided from the extension of the declared name. It is also the `Content-Type` of the download.

original_name.description: Name the file was declared with. It never changes; its extension decides the file type.

previewable.description: Whether the Easymailing app can show the file without downloading it (PDF and images). The API always delivers the bytes as an attachment.

record.description: IRI of the contact, company or opportunity the file is attached to. A file belongs to exactly one record and never moves.

record_type.description: Kind of record the file is attached to.

size_bytes.description: Size of the file in bytes (at most 20 MiB = 20,971,520).

source.description: Where the file is stored. Only `upload` (stored in Easymailing) exists today.

status.description: State of the file. `available` once its content is stored; every read of the API returns only `available` files. `uploading` (declared, waiting for its content) and `analyzing` (content received, being checked) are seen only in the response of `create_file`, including when it is repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

updated_at.description: When the file last changed, ISO 8601.

uuid.description: UUID of the file.

version.description: Version of the file; it grows with every edit of its name or description. Send it as `expected_version` to `update_file` and `delete_file`.

FileStorageUsage-file_storage_usage.read.description:
`get_file_storage_usage` (fase 5): the CRM file storage counters of the account. Generated from the proposal by
fase-5/tools/gen_files_api.py; the texts are the proposal's.

The path is `/files/storage_usage` and not the proposal's `/file_storage_usage`: the first segment of a public path is
a plural collection (lint `path_not_snake_plural`). `get_file` keeps `storage_usage` out of its `{uuid}`.

crm_pro_limit_bytes.description: Bytes the CRM Pro level would give, to offer the upgrade. `null` when the account already has that much or more.

exceeded.description: Whether `used_bytes` is above `limit_bytes` (for example after a plan downgrade). Existing files stay readable; new uploads are refused until the usage is back within the limit.

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

limit_bytes.description: Bytes the plan allows: 1 GiB during the trial, 5 GiB with CRM Essentials, 25 GiB with CRM Pro, 0 without CRM. An account with unlimited storage reports 9223372036854775807.

used_bytes.description: Bytes used by the available files of the account. Space reserved by uploads in progress is not included, so `exceeded` can be `false` and a `create_file` can still answer `crm_file_quota_exceeded`.

uuid.description: Trailing UUID segment of the entity IRI. Convenience derived from `iri`; absent when the IRI doesn't end in a UUID.

Meeting-meeting.list.description:
Meetings of the connected Google calendars in the public API (fase 5, read only). Generated from the proposal by
fase-5/tools/gen_meetings_api.py; the texts are the proposal's. Every operation checks the CRM access in its provider
before anything else, because API Platform evaluates `security` after the provider.

`list_meetings` has two modes (the upcoming meetings of one record, or the user's own calendars within a range) and
pages forward only by cursor (`cursor[gt]`): `cursor` is the opaque position API Platform copies into `hydra:next`,
and {@see ForwardOnlyCursor} drops the `hydra:previous` it would also build. It is never published. The fields of the
detail travel only in `get_meeting`; every field travels as `null`, never absent (`skip_null_values: false`).

`status` carries the text of the detail: the list only returns `confirmed` meetings, which its filters say.
`replace_meeting_relations` answers the meeting as `get_meeting` does; the writes in Google answer a receipt
({@see MeetingWriteReceiptResource}).

conference.description: Video call of the meeting. `null` when it has none.

code.description: Access code or meeting ID when the provider gives one. `null` otherwise.

label.description: Name of the video call as Google shows it. `null` when there is none.

type.description: Provider of the video call.

end_date_exclusive.description: Day after the last day of an all-day meeting (`YYYY-MM-DD`). `null` for a timed meeting.

ends_at.description: End of a timed meeting, ISO 8601 in UTC. `null` for an all-day meeting.

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

location.description: Place of the meeting. `null` when there is none.

organizer.description: The organizer: the Google account that owns the event, which is not always the person who owns the token. `null` for imported events without an organizer.

contact.description: IRI of the contact with that email. `null` when the person is not a contact.

email.description: Email address of the person.

internal.description: Whether the person belongs to the account's own team (a user or an internal address) rather than being someone outside it.

kind.description: `user` for a user of this account, `contact` for a person who is a contact in the CRM, `external` for anyone else.

response_status.description: Answer of the guest in Google Calendar: `accepted`, `tentative`, `declined`, or `pending` when they have not answered.

role.description: `organizer` for the Google account that owns the event, `attendee` for everyone else.

original_time_zone.description: IANA time zone of the event in the calendar it comes from.

participant_count.description: Number of people on the meeting, the organizer included.

participant_preview.description: Up to 5 participants other than the user who owns the token, organizer first. Use `get_meeting` for the full list.

contact.description: IRI of the contact with that email. `null` when the person is not a contact.

email.description: Email address.

primary_relation.description: The CRM record that heads the meeting among those the user can open: the company, otherwise the opportunity, otherwise the contact. `null` when none is visible.

iri.description: IRI of the record.

label.description: Name of the record.

series_uuid.description: UUID that groups the occurrences of a recurring meeting. `null` for a single meeting. It is not an addressable resource.

source.description: The calendar the meeting is read from for this user. `null` when the user reaches the meeting only through a record they can see.

calendar_id.description: Google calendar ID (usually an email address).

calendar_name.description: Name of the calendar. `null` when unknown.

connection_uuid.description: UUID of the Google connection (the Google account) where the calendar lives. Send it as `connection_uuid` in the write operations.

owned.description: Whether the calendar belongs to the user who owns the token (`false` for the calendar of a colleague who shared theirs).

writable.description: Whether the user can write to it from Easymailing: it is theirs, Calendar is active on the connection and Google allows writing.

start_date.description: First day of an all-day meeting (`YYYY-MM-DD`), never shifted by a time zone. `null` for a timed meeting.

starts_at.description: Start of a timed meeting, ISO 8601 in UTC. `null` for an all-day meeting.

status.description: `confirmed` for a meeting that takes place, `cancelled` for one that was cancelled (it stays in the history).

time_type.description: `timed` for a meeting with a start and end time, `all_day` for an all-day event.

title.description: Title of the event. `null` when the event has none.

uuid.description: UUID of the meeting.

version.description: Version of the meeting; it grows with every change, including relation changes and synchronizations. Send it as `expected_version` to make sure nobody changed the meeting in between.

Meeting.MeetingRelationsInput.description:
Meetings of the connected Google calendars in the public API (fase 5, read only). Generated from the proposal by
fase-5/tools/gen_meetings_api.py; the texts are the proposal's. Every operation checks the CRM access in its provider
before anything else, because API Platform evaluates `security` after the provider.

`list_meetings` has two modes (the upcoming meetings of one record, or the user's own calendars within a range) and
pages forward only by cursor (`cursor[gt]`): `cursor` is the opaque position API Platform copies into `hydra:next`,
and {@see ForwardOnlyCursor} drops the `hydra:previous` it would also build. It is never published. The fields of the
detail travel only in `get_meeting`; every field travels as `null`, never absent (`skip_null_values: false`).

`status` carries the text of the detail: the list only returns `confirmed` meetings, which its filters say.
`replace_meeting_relations` answers the meeting as `get_meeting` does; the writes in Google answer a receipt
({@see MeetingWriteReceiptResource}).

companies.description: IRIs of the companies the meeting is related to (`/companies/{uuid}`), at most 100. The complete final set; send an empty list to unlink all. Companies related only through the email domain of a guest stay.

contacts.description: IRIs of the contacts the meeting is related to (`/contacts/{uuid}`), at most 100. The complete final set, not an addition: contacts not in the list are unlinked, except those who are guests.

expected_version.description: Version of the meeting you read (`version`). Optional: if you send it and the meeting has changed since, nothing is written and you get `crm_meeting_version_conflict`; if you leave it out, the change is applied over the current state (Google still refuses it, with a `conflict` receipt, when the event changed there after Easymailing last read it).

opportunities.description: IRIs of the opportunities the meeting is related to (`/opportunities/{uuid}`), at most 100. The complete final set; send an empty list to unlink all. Opportunities in pipelines the user cannot read are never unlinked by being absent.

scope.description: What the lists apply to. `occurrence` (default): this meeting only. `series`: the whole recurring series; it is rejected with `series_not_supported` when the meeting is not part of a series.

MeetingWriteReceipt-meeting_write_receip.description:
`get_meeting_write_receipt` (fase 5): the receipt of a create, change or cancel of a meeting, only for the user who
made the write, and the writes that answer it (202): `create_meeting`, `update_meeting` and `cancel_meeting`, which
write the event in Google during the request. Generated from the proposal by fase-5/tools/gen_meetings_api.py; the
texts are the proposal's.

action.description: What the receipt is for: `create_event`, `update_event` or `cancel_event`.

error_code.description: Why a `failed` or `conflict` receipt did not apply the change; `null` otherwise. `permission_missing`: Google rejected the stored permission; the user must reconnect Google in the app. `provider_rejected`: Google refused the request definitively (invalid event, API disabled); nothing was created. `event_id_taken` (conflict): the event ID already belongs to another event, which is never touched. `not_confirmed`: Easymailing could not confirm that Google applied the change, so it may or may not have been applied; read the meeting (`get_meeting`) before repeating it to avoid a duplicate. `provider_version_conflict` (conflict): the event was changed or deleted in Google after Easymailing last read it; nothing was applied and a fresh read was queued, so read the meeting again and decide. `calendar_unavailable`: the calendar or its connection is no longer available. `calendar_not_writable`: Google answered that this account cannot change that event or calendar (for example, the user is not its organizer in Google).

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

meeting.description: IRI of the meeting once it is confirmed and in the CRM (`/meetings/{uuid}`). `null` while the write is not final, when it failed, and in the rare case that the calendar stopped being synchronized meanwhile.

state.description: `confirmed`: Google applied the change and the meeting is in the CRM. `uncertain`: Google did not answer clearly; Easymailing keeps checking in the background for up to about an hour. `pending`: the write was recorded and is not resolved yet. `failed`: nothing was applied (see `error_code`) or it could not be confirmed. `conflict`: the event in Google differs from what the change expected (see `error_code`). `confirmed`, `failed` and `conflict` are final.

uuid.description: UUID of the receipt. Read it with `get_meeting_write_receipt`.

MeetingWriteReceipt.MeetingCancelInput.description:
`get_meeting_write_receipt` (fase 5): the receipt of a create, change or cancel of a meeting, only for the user who
made the write, and the writes that answer it (202): `create_meeting`, `update_meeting` and `cancel_meeting`, which
write the event in Google during the request. Generated from the proposal by fase-5/tools/gen_meetings_api.py; the
texts are the proposal's.

client_request_id.description: UUID you generate for this request, once per intended meeting change. It makes the call safe to retry: sending the same body with the same `client_request_id` returns the same receipt and never writes to Google or invites anybody twice; sending different data with an already used value fails with `crm_meeting_write_rejected` (`client_request_reused`).

connection_uuid.description: UUID of the Google connection that holds the calendar. Take it from the first entry of `writable_sources` in `get_meeting`.

expected_version.description: Version of the meeting you read (`version`). MeetingWriteReceipt.jsonld-meeting_write.description:
`get_meeting_write_receipt` (fase 5): the receipt of a create, change or cancel of a meeting, only for the user who
made the write, and the writes that answer it (202): `create_meeting`, `update_meeting` and `cancel_meeting`, which
write the event in Google during the request. Generated from the proposal by fase-5/tools/gen_meetings_api.py; the
texts are the proposal's.

action.description: What the receipt is for: `create_event`, `update_event` or `cancel_event`.

error_code.description: Why a `failed` or `conflict` receipt did not apply the change; `null` otherwise. `permission_missing`: Google rejected the stored permission; the user must reconnect Google in the app. `provider_rejected`: Google refused the request definitively (invalid event, API disabled); nothing was created. `event_id_taken` (conflict): the event ID already belongs to another event, which is never touched. `not_confirmed`: Easymailing could not confirm that Google applied the change, so it may or may not have been applied; read the meeting (`get_meeting`) before repeating it to avoid a duplicate. `provider_version_conflict` (conflict): the event was changed or deleted in Google after Easymailing last read it; nothing was applied and a fresh read was queued, so read the meeting again and decide. `calendar_unavailable`: the calendar or its connection is no longer available. `calendar_not_writable`: Google answered that this account cannot change that event or calendar (for example, the user is not its organizer in Google).

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

meeting.description: IRI of the meeting once it is confirmed and in the CRM (`/meetings/{uuid}`). `null` while the write is not final, when it failed, and in the rare case that the calendar stopped being synchronized meanwhile.

state.description: `confirmed`: Google applied the change and the meeting is in the CRM. `uncertain`: Google did not answer clearly; Easymailing keeps checking in the background for up to about an hour. `pending`: the write was recorded and is not resolved yet. `failed`: nothing was applied (see `error_code`) or it could not be confirmed. `conflict`: the event in Google differs from what the change expected (see `error_code`). `confirmed`, `failed` and `conflict` are final.

uuid.description: UUID of the receipt. Read it with `get_meeting_write_receipt`.

MeetingWriteState.description:
State of a meeting write:
* `pending` - Recorded, not resolved yet
* `uncertain` - Google did not answer clearly; checked in the background
* `confirmed` - Applied in Google and in the CRM
* `conflict` - The event differs from what the change expected
* `failed` - Not applied, or could not be confirmed

Note.description:
Notes of the public API (plan fase 4, Task 19). Generated from the approved proposal by fase-4/tools/gen_notes.py and
edited by hand afterwards: the texts are the proposal's. Every operation checks the CRM access in its provider or
processor before anything else, because API Platform evaluates `security` after the provider.

`list_notes` pages by cursor (`paginationViaCursor` goes on the resource: on the operation API Platform 3.4.17 loses
it) and gives the total of the record. `cursor` is the opaque position of each item, which API Platform copies into
the `cursor[gt]` of `hydra:next` (the last item) and the `cursor[lt]` of `hydra:previous` (the first one); it is never
published.

body_html.description: Text of the note as limited HTML (paragraphs, headings, lists, bold, italic, underline, links and images).
body_html.example: Ana wants the annual plan with quarterly billing.

can_delete.description: Whether the user who owns the token can delete this note: the same people who can edit it.

can_edit.description: Whether the user who owns the token can edit this note: its author or an account admin with a token that reaches account administration (an API key, or OAuth with the `admin` scope).

created_at.description: When the note was created, ISO 8601.

created_by.description: Author of the note. `null` when unknown.

kind.description: Kind of actor: `user` for a person, otherwise `contact`, `automation`, `integration`, `system` or `external`.

name.description: Name of the actor. `null` when the person is no longer a member of the account.

preview_text.description: Plain-text start of the note, up to 280 characters, to show it in a list.
preview_text.example: Ana wants the annual plan with quarterly billing.

record.description: IRI of the contact, company or opportunity the note belongs to. A note belongs to exactly one record and never moves.

record_type.description: Kind of record the note belongs to.

title.description: Optional title of the note. `null` when it has none.

updated_at.description: When the note last changed, ISO 8601.

updated_by.description: Who last edited the note; the author when it was never edited. `null` when unknown.

kind.description: Kind of actor: `user` for a person, otherwise `contact`, `automation`, `integration`, `system` or `external`.

name.description: Name of the actor. `null` when the person is no longer a member of the account.

uuid.description: UUID of the note.

version.description: Version of the note; it grows with every edit. Send it as `expected_version` to make sure nobody edited the note in between.

Opportunity.description:
Opportunities of the public API (plan fase 4, Tasks 13 and 14). Generated from the approved proposal by
fase-4/tools/gen_opportunity_read.py and edited by hand afterwards: the texts are the proposal's. The providers
check the CRM capability and the pipeline level before anything else, because API Platform evaluates `security`
after the provider.

`opportunity:list` is the summary every item of the list has; `opportunity:detail` adds what only `get_opportunity`
returns. `attributes` is an \ArrayObject so that an empty one is published as `{}`, not as `[]`.

attributes.description: Attribute values keyed by `public_code` (see `list_opportunity_attributes`). `enum` and `multi_enum` values are `{uuid, label}`, `money` is `{amount, currency}`. Attributes without value are omitted.

closed_at.description: When it was won or lost. `null` while it is open; reopening clears it.

company.description: IRI of the company (`/companies/{uuid}`). `null` when there is none.

contacts.description: IRIs of the contacts (`/contacts/{uuid}`) linked to the opportunity. There is no primary contact.

created_by.description: Person who created it. `null` when that user no longer exists.

uuid.description: UUID of the user.

description.description: Free-text description.
description.example: Renewal of the annual plan with a seat upgrade.

expected_close_date.description: Date the deal is expected to close (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

loss_note.description: Free-text note given when it was lost.
loss_note.example: Chose a competitor with a lower price.

loss_reason.description: Reason it was lost. `null` when it is not lost or none was given.

uuid.description: UUID of the loss reason.

owner.description: User in charge of the opportunity. `null` when there is none. An owner who was deactivated stays assigned.

email.description: Email of the user; send it in `owner` to assign this user.

uuid.description: UUID of the user.

pipeline.description: IRI of the pipeline the opportunity belongs to (`/pipelines/{uuid}`).

probability.description: Effective win probability, 0 to 100. It is the stage probability unless `probability_mode` is `custom`; 100 when won and 0 when lost.

probability_mode.description: `stage` when the probability comes from the stage, `custom` when someone overrode it (only open stages of pipelines that allow it).

record_source.description: How the opportunity was created: `manual`, `api`, `automation`, `import`... It never changes.

reference_value.description: Value in the reference currency of the pipeline, calculated by the server. `null` when the opportunity has no amount.

amount.description: Amount converted to the reference currency. `null` while the conversion is pending or unavailable.

basis.description: `latest` for the latest rate, `closure` for the rate of the closing date of a won or lost opportunity.

currency.description: Reference currency of the pipeline.

rate_date.description: Date of the exchange rate used. `null` when no conversion was needed.

status.description: `same_currency`, `converted`, `pending` (no rate yet) or `unavailable`.

weighted_amount.description: Converted amount multiplied by the effective probability (the forecast).

stage.description: Current stage of the opportunity. `null` when it has no stage (it is open and shows in the «no stage» column).

type.description: Stage type: `open`, `won` or `lost`.

uuid.description: UUID of the stage.

stage_entered_at.description: When the opportunity entered its current stage.

status.description: Commercial situation, derived from the stage type: `open`, `won` or `lost`. An opportunity without stage is `open`.

title.description: Name of the opportunity.

uuid.description: UUID of the opportunity.

value.description: Amount and currency of the opportunity. `null` when it has no amount.

amount.description: Decimal amount as a string, never a float.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. It must be one the pipeline accepts.

Opportunity.OpportunityCreateInput.description:
Opportunities of the public API (plan fase 4, Tasks 13 and 14). Generated from the approved proposal by
fase-4/tools/gen_opportunity_read.py and edited by hand afterwards: the texts are the proposal's. The providers
check the CRM capability and the pipeline level before anything else, because API Platform evaluates `security`
after the provider.

`opportunity:list` is the summary every item of the list has; `opportunity:detail` adds what only `get_opportunity`
returns. `attributes` is an \ArrayObject so that an empty one is published as `{}`, not as `[]`.

attributes.description: Values of the account's opportunity attributes, keyed by `public_code` (see `list_opportunity_attributes`). `enum` and `multi_enum` accept the option UUID or its exact label; `money` is `{amount, currency}`; `null` removes a value. Attributes you leave out keep their value.

company.description: IRI of an existing company (`/companies/{uuid}`). `null` removes the link. Linking a company does not change the contacts and the other way round.

contacts.description: IRIs of the contacts of the opportunity (`/contacts/{uuid}`), up to 500. Replaces the whole set; send `[]` to remove all of them.

description.description: Free-text description. `null` clears it.
description.example: Renewal of the annual plan with a seat upgrade.

loss_note.description: Free-text note about the loss, up to 10000 characters.

loss_reason.description: Reason for losing it: the UUID of a loss reason of the pipeline or its exact name (`get_pipeline`, `loss_reasons`). Archived reasons cannot be used. Whether it is required, optional or not allowed depends on `loss_reason_mode` of the lost stage.

owner.description: Email of the user in charge, exactly as they sign in. It must be an active user with access to the pipeline. `null` leaves the opportunity without owner. Nobody is assigned if you leave it out: there is no default owner for the API.

pipeline.description: IRI of the pipeline (`/pipelines/{uuid}`) where the deal starts. Get it from `list_pipelines`. The user needs `work` access to it.

probability.description: Overrides the stage probability, 0 to 99. Allowed only while the opportunity is in an open stage of a pipeline with `allow_custom_probability`. `null` goes back to the probability of the stage.

stage.description: Stage of that pipeline: its UUID or its exact name (`get_pipeline`). Leave it out to create the opportunity without stage; it then sits in the «no stage» column with probability 0. If you pick the stage, its entry requirements must be met by the values you send. Picking a won or lost stage creates the deal already closed.

title.description: Name of the opportunity. Required to create it; it cannot be `null`.

value.description: Amount and currency. The currency must be in the platform exchange-rate catalog and, if the pipeline does not allow several currencies, equal to its reference currency. `null` clears both.

amount.description: Decimal amount as a string, never a float.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. It must be one the pipeline accepts.

Opportunity.OpportunityUpdateInput.description:
Opportunities of the public API (plan fase 4, Tasks 13 and 14). Generated from the approved proposal by
fase-4/tools/gen_opportunity_read.py and edited by hand afterwards: the texts are the proposal's. The providers
check the CRM capability and the pipeline level before anything else, because API Platform evaluates `security`
after the provider.

`opportunity:list` is the summary every item of the list has; `opportunity:detail` adds what only `get_opportunity`
returns. `attributes` is an \ArrayObject so that an empty one is published as `{}`, not as `[]`.

attributes.description: Values of the account's opportunity attributes, keyed by `public_code` (see `list_opportunity_attributes`). `enum` and `multi_enum` accept the option UUID or its exact label; `money` is `{amount, currency}`; `null` removes a value. Attributes you leave out keep their value.

company.description: IRI of an existing company (`/companies/{uuid}`). `null` removes the link. Linking a company does not change the contacts and the other way round.

contacts.description: IRIs of the contacts of the opportunity (`/contacts/{uuid}`), up to 500. Replaces the whole set; send `[]` to remove all of them. Left unchanged if omitted.

description.description: Free-text description. `null` clears it.
description.example: Renewal of the annual plan with a seat upgrade.

owner.description: Email of the user in charge, exactly as they sign in. It must be an active user with access to the pipeline. `null` leaves the opportunity without owner. Nobody is assigned if you leave it out: there is no default owner for the API.

probability.description: Overrides the stage probability, 0 to 99. Allowed only while the opportunity is in an open stage of a pipeline with `allow_custom_probability`. `null` goes back to the probability of the stage.

title.description: Name of the opportunity. Required to create it; it cannot be `null`.

value.description: Amount and currency. The currency must be in the platform exchange-rate catalog and, if the pipeline does not allow several currencies, equal to its reference currency. `null` clears both.

amount.description: Decimal amount as a string, never a float.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. It must be one the pipeline accepts.

Opportunity.jsonld.description:
Opportunities of the public API (plan fase 4, Tasks 13 and 14). Generated from the approved proposal by
fase-4/tools/gen_opportunity_read.py and edited by hand afterwards: the texts are the proposal's. The providers
check the CRM capability and the pipeline level before anything else, because API Platform evaluates `security`
after the provider.

`opportunity:list` is the summary every item of the list has; `opportunity:detail` adds what only `get_opportunity`
returns. `attributes` is an \ArrayObject so that an empty one is published as `{}`, not as `[]`.

attributes.description: Attribute values keyed by `public_code` (see `list_opportunity_attributes`). `enum` and `multi_enum` values are `{uuid, label}`, `money` is `{amount, currency}`. Attributes without value are omitted.

closed_at.description: When it was won or lost. `null` while it is open; reopening clears it.

company.description: IRI of the company (`/companies/{uuid}`). `null` when there is none.

contacts.description: IRIs of the contacts (`/contacts/{uuid}`) linked to the opportunity. There is no primary contact.

created_by.description: Person who created it. `null` when that user no longer exists.

uuid.description: UUID of the user.

description.description: Free-text description.
description.example: Renewal of the annual plan with a seat upgrade.

expected_close_date.description: Date the deal is expected to close (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

loss_note.description: Free-text note given when it was lost.
loss_note.example: Chose a competitor with a lower price.

loss_reason.description: Reason it was lost. `null` when it is not lost or none was given.

uuid.description: UUID of the loss reason.

owner.description: User in charge of the opportunity. `null` when there is none. An owner who was deactivated stays assigned.

email.description: Email of the user; send it in `owner` to assign this user.

uuid.description: UUID of the user.

pipeline.description: IRI of the pipeline the opportunity belongs to (`/pipelines/{uuid}`).

probability.description: Effective win probability, 0 to 100. It is the stage probability unless `probability_mode` is `custom`; 100 when won and 0 when lost.

probability_mode.description: `stage` when the probability comes from the stage, `custom` when someone overrode it (only open stages of pipelines that allow it).

record_source.description: How the opportunity was created: `manual`, `api`, `automation`, `import`... It never changes.

reference_value.description: Value in the reference currency of the pipeline, calculated by the server. `null` when the opportunity has no amount.

amount.description: Amount converted to the reference currency. `null` while the conversion is pending or unavailable.

basis.description: `latest` for the latest rate, `closure` for the rate of the closing date of a won or lost opportunity.

currency.description: Reference currency of the pipeline.

rate_date.description: Date of the exchange rate used. `null` when no conversion was needed.

status.description: `same_currency`, `converted`, `pending` (no rate yet) or `unavailable`.

weighted_amount.description: Converted amount multiplied by the effective probability (the forecast).

stage.description: Current stage of the opportunity. `null` when it has no stage (it is open and shows in the «no stage» column).

type.description: Stage type: `open`, `won` or `lost`.

uuid.description: UUID of the stage.

stage_entered_at.description: When the opportunity entered its current stage.

status.description: Commercial situation, derived from the stage type: `open`, `won` or `lost`. An opportunity without stage is `open`.

title.description: Name of the opportunity.

uuid.description: UUID of the opportunity.

value.description: Amount and currency of the opportunity. `null` when it has no amount.

amount.description: Decimal amount as a string, never a float.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. It must be one the pipeline accepts.

OpportunityAttribute-opportunity_attribu.description:
Opportunity attributes of the public API (plan fase 4, Task 20): the definitions of the custom fields of a opportunity, over
AttributeDefinitionManager. Generated from the approved proposal by fase-4/tools/gen_opportunity_attributes.py and

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. Only for `money` attributes; null for every other type.

current_value_count.description: Number of opportunities that currently have a value for this attribute.

description.description: Optional explanation of what the attribute holds.

ever_used.description: True if the attribute or any of its options has ever held a value, even if it has none now.

options.description: Options of an `enum` or `multi_enum` attribute, in display order. Empty for every other type.

label.description: Visible name of the option.

position.description: Position of the option in the list, starting at 1.

status.description: `active` options can be assigned; `archived` options keep the values already stored but cannot be assigned again.

uuid.description: UUID of the option. Use it as the value of the attribute in a record.

position.description: Position of the attribute among the opportunity attributes, starting at 1.

type.description: Type of value the attribute stores. Cannot be changed after creation.

uuid.description: UUID of the attribute.

version.description: Revision number. Send it back when you update, archive or restore so that a concurrent change is detected.

OpportunityAttributeType.description:
Opportunity attribute type:
* `text` - Short text
* `long_text` - Long text, several lines
* `integer` - Whole number
* `decimal` - Decimal number
* `percentage` - Percentage
* `money` - Amount of money in the currency of the attribute
* `boolean` - Yes or no
* `date` - Calendar date
* `datetime` - Date and time
* `enum` - One option from a list
* `multi_enum` - Several options from a list
* `email` - Email address
* `phone` - Phone number
* `url` - Web address
* `country` - Country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code)
* `language` - Language (ISO 639-1 code)
* `timezone` - IANA time zone name

OpportunityConversionStatus.description:
State of the conversion of an amount to a reference currency:
* `same_currency` - The amount is already in the reference currency
* `converted` - Converted with the rate of `rate_date`
* `pending` - There is no rate yet; the conversion is calculated later
* `unavailable` - The currency has no rate
* `no_amount` - The opportunity has no amount, so there is nothing to convert

OpportunityProbabilityMode.description:
Where the probability of an opportunity comes from:
* `stage` - The probability of the stage
* `custom` - A probability set by hand, allowed only in open stages of pipelines that permit it

OpportunityReferenceBasis.description:
Rate behind the reference value of an opportunity:
* `latest` - The latest rate
* `closure` - The rate of the closing date of a won or lost opportunity

OpportunityStatus.description:
Commercial situation of an opportunity, derived from the type of its stage:
* `open` - Being worked; also an opportunity without stage
* `won` - Closed as won
* `lost` - Closed as lost

Pipeline.description:
Pipelines of the public API (plan fase 4, Tasks 15 and 16). Generated from the approved proposal by
fase-4/tools/gen_pipeline_read.py and edited by hand afterwards: the texts are the proposal's.

`pipeline:list` is the summary every item of the list has; `pipeline:detail` adds what only `get_pipeline` returns
(the initial stage, the stages and the loss reasons).

access_level.description: Access of the user making the request to this pipeline: `read`, `work` or `admin`.

allow_custom_probability.description: Whether a deal in an open stage may override the probability of the stage.

allow_multiple_currencies.description: Whether deals may use currencies other than the reference currency.

default.description: true for the default pipeline of the account (exactly one).

initial_stage.description: UUID of the initial stage (an open stage). Deals created without stage do not use it.

loss_reasons.description: Loss reasons of the pipeline, active and archived, in order.

position.description: Position among the loss reasons: 0 is the first.

status.description: `active`, or `archived`: it can no longer be chosen but past deals keep it.

used.description: true when at least one closed deal uses it.

uuid.description: UUID of the loss reason.

name.description: Pipeline name, unique in the account (compared ignoring case).

reference_currency.description: Currency in which the forecast and totals of the pipeline are reported.

stages.description: Stages in order. Every pipeline has at least one open, one won and one lost stage.

loss_reason_mode.description: Only for lost stages: whether the loss reason is `required`, `optional` or `disabled` when a deal enters.

max_calendar_days.description: Calendar days a deal is expected to stay in this stage. `null` if there is no limit.

name.description: Stage name. Names are not forced to be unique; avoid repeating one, because operations that take a stage by name then ask for its UUID.

position.description: Position of the stage in the pipeline: 0 is the first.

probability.description: Win probability of deals in this stage: 0 to 99 for open stages, always 100 for won and 0 for lost.

required_attributes.description: `public_code` of the opportunity attributes a deal must have to enter this stage.

required_fields.description: Built-in fields a deal must have to enter this stage (`company`, `contacts`, `owner`, `amount_currency`, `expected_close_date`, `description`).

type.description: Stage type: `open` (the deal is being worked), `won` or `lost` (the deal is closed).

uuid.description: UUID of the stage.
UUID of the pipeline.

PipelineAccessLevel.description:
Access level of a user to a pipeline, from lowest to highest:
* `read` - See the pipeline and its opportunities
* `work` - Create and work opportunities
* `admin` - Manage the pipeline and delete its opportunities

PipelineLossReasonMode.description:
Whether a loss reason is asked when a deal enters a lost stage:
* `disabled` - No loss reason
* `optional` - A loss reason can be given
* `required` - A loss reason must be given

PipelineLossReasonStatus.description:
Loss reason status:
* `active` - Can be chosen
* `archived` - Can no longer be chosen; past deals keep it

PipelineStageType.description:
Pipeline stage type:
* `open` - The deal is being worked
* `won` - The deal is closed as won
* `lost` - The deal is closed as lost

SmsCampaign-campaign.read.description: SMS campaign response. SMS campaigns are exposed under /sms_campaigns.

audience.description: IRI of the audience the campaign is sent from.

channel.description: Channel of the campaign. Always `sms` here.

contact_targeting.description: Recipients chosen with the contacts engine, as Customer App does: a contact segment (`send_to_segment`) or the campaign's own filter, optionally on top of a segment (`send_to_custom_segment`). `null` when the campaign goes to the whole audience, to groups or to an old audience segment (`list_segment`). Recipients are always the confirmed subscribers of the campaign's audience and channel who match. Only `get_sms_campaign`, `create_sms_campaign` and `update_sms_campaign` fill it; `list_sms_campaigns` leaves it `null`, read the campaign to know its recipients.

contact_segment.description: IRI of the segment (`/contact_segments/{uuid}`): the target, or the base of the filter. `null` without segment or if the user lacks `contacts.read`.

contact_segment_deleted.description: True if that segment was deleted: the campaign cannot be sent until its recipients change (unless it was scheduled before).

error_code.description: Why the recipients cannot be calculated now (a code of the filter errors, e.g. `segment_reference_deleted` or `unknown_filter_field`); then `recipient_count` is 0 and the campaign cannot be sent. `null` when they can.

filter.description: The campaign's own conditions, in the shape of `filter` of `create_contact_segment`. `null` for `kind: segment` or if the user lacks `contacts.read`.

conditions.description: Conditions and groups of the top level, in order. At least one.

audience.description: Condition: UUID of the audience whose subscription is checked. Only for fields with `audience_required: true`, where it is required.

conditions.description: Group: its conditions (at least one), each with `field`, `operator`, `value` and `audience` as above. A group cannot contain a group.

field.description: Condition: `id` of a field of `list_contact_filter_fields`. Leave it out in a group.

match.description: Group: `all` or `any`, how its conditions combine. Leave it out in a condition.

value.description: Condition: value for the operator, shaped as its `value_shape` says. Leave it out when the shape is `none`.

match.description: How the top-level items combine: `all` (AND) or `any` (OR).

kind.description: `segment`: the campaign goes to a contact segment. `filter`: to its own filter.

pinned_at.description: When the revisions were fixed (scheduling or sending). `null` while following the latest.

revision_status.description: `following_latest`: the campaign uses the current revision of its segment (drafts). `pinned_current`: it was scheduled or sent with a revision that is still the current one. `pinned_outdated`: the segment changed after it was scheduled; the campaign keeps the old revision.

created_at.description: Date and time the campaign was created.

finished_at.description: Date and time the sending finished. Empty until the campaign has been sent.

groups.description: IRIs of the groups that receive the campaign. Empty unless it is sent to groups.

hash.description: Unique code of the campaign, used for tracking.

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

list_segment.description: IRI of the old audience segment that receives the campaign. `null` unless it goes to one; campaigns that use a contact segment or their own filter have it `null` and describe their recipients in `contact_targeting`.

send_to.description: Who receives the campaign: `send_to_all`, `send_to_groups` (see `groups`), `send_to_segment` (see `contact_targeting`, or `list_segment` for an old audience segment) or `send_to_custom_segment` (its own filter, see `contact_targeting`).

started_at.description: Date and time the sending started. Empty until the campaign starts sending.

status.description: Current state of the campaign.

title.description: Name of the campaign in your account.

type.description: Kind of campaign. SMS campaigns are always regular.

updated_at.description: Date and time the campaign was last changed.

uuid.description: Unique identifier of the campaign.

Task.description:
Tasks of the public API (plan fase 4, Tasks 17 and 18). The reads are generated from the approved proposal by
fase-4/tools/gen_task_read.py and the writes by fase-4/tools/gen_task_write.py, edited by hand afterwards: the texts
are the proposal's. Every operation checks the
CRM access in its provider or processor before anything else, because API Platform evaluates `security` after the
provider.

`list_tasks` pages by cursor (`paginationViaCursor` goes on the resource: on the operation API Platform 3.4.17 loses
it) and gives no total. `cursor` is the opaque position of each task, which API Platform copies into the `cursor[gt]`
of `hydra:next` (the last item) and the `cursor[lt]` of `hydra:previous` (the first one); it is never published.
`assignee`, `completed_by` and `created_by` are arrays so that they keep the shape of the proposal; the related
records are {@see \App\Application\Crm\RecordRelationView} arrays.

assignee.description: User responsible for the task. `null` when it is unassigned.

email.description: Email of the user; send it in `assignee` to assign this user.

name.description: Full name of the user (their email when they have no name).

uuid.description: UUID of the user.

can_delete.description: Whether the user who owns the token can delete this task: its creator, its assignee or an account admin with a token that reaches account administration (an API key, or OAuth with the `admin` scope).

can_edit.description: Whether the user who owns the token can edit, complete or reopen this task.

companies.description: The companies the task is linked to. Empty when it has none.

iri.description: IRI of the record; send it in the same field to link it.

label.description: Name of the record: the full name of a contact, the name of a company or opportunity.

secondary.description: Second line that tells records with the same name apart: the email of a contact, the primary domain of a company. `null` when there is none.

completed_at.description: When the task was completed. `null` while it is open.

completed_by.description: Who completed the task. `null` while it is open.

kind.description: Kind of actor: `user` for a person, otherwise `contact`, `automation`, `integration`, `system` or `external`.

name.description: Name of the actor. `null` when the person is no longer a member of the account.

contacts.description: The contacts the task is linked to. Empty when it has none.

iri.description: IRI of the record; send it in the same field to link it.

label.description: Name of the record: the full name of a contact, the name of a company or opportunity.

secondary.description: Second line that tells records with the same name apart: the email of a contact, the primary domain of a company. `null` when there is none.

created_at.description: When the task was created, ISO 8601.

created_by.description: Who decided to create the task. `null` when the creator is unknown. It is not the assignee.

kind.description: Kind of actor: `user` for a person, otherwise `contact`, `automation`, `integration`, `system` or `external`.

name.description: Name of the actor. `null` when the person is no longer a member of the account.

description_html.description: Longer description as limited HTML (paragraphs, line breaks, bold, italic and links). `null` when there is none.

due_at.description: When the task is due, ISO 8601 with the time zone offset (the instant is stored in UTC). `null` when it has no due date.

initiated_via.description: How the task was created: `ui` (the app), `maia`, `api`, `import`, `sync`, `automation` or `system`.

opportunities.description: The opportunities the task is linked to. Empty when it has none.

iri.description: IRI of the record; send it in the same field to link it.

label.description: Name of the record: the full name of a contact, the name of a company or opportunity.

secondary.description: Second line that tells records with the same name apart: the email of a contact, the primary domain of a company. `null` when there is none.

overdue.description: `true` when the task is open and its due date has passed. Always `false` for a completed task. It is calculated when you read it.

reminder_at.description: Instant of the reminder, calculated from `due_at` and `reminder_offset_minutes`. Read-only. `null` when there is no reminder.

reminder_offset_minutes.description: Minutes before `due_at` at which the assignee is reminded; `0` means at the due time. `null` when there is no reminder.

status.description: `open` while the task is pending, `completed` once it is done.

title.description: What has to be done.
title.example: Send the revised proposal to Ana

type.description: Kind of work. It only classifies the task: completing a `call` or `email` task does not make a call or send an email.

updated_at.description: When the task last changed, ISO 8601.

uuid.description: UUID of the task.

version.description: Version of the task; it grows with every change. Send it as `expected_version` to make sure nobody changed the task in between.

kind.description: Kind of actor: `user` for a person, otherwise `contact`, `automation`, `integration`, `system` or `external`.

name.description: Name of the actor. `null` when the person is no longer a member of the account.

description_html.description: Longer description as limited HTML (paragraphs, line breaks, bold, italic and links). `null` when there is none.

due_at.description: When the task is due, ISO 8601 with the time zone offset (the instant is stored in UTC). `null` when it has no due date.

overdue.description: `true` when the task is open and its due date has passed. Always `false` for a completed task. It is calculated when you read it.

reminder_at.description: Instant of the reminder, calculated from `due_at` and `reminder_offset_minutes`. Read-only. `null` when there is no reminder.

reminder_offset_minutes.description: Minutes before `due_at` at which the assignee is reminded; `0` means at the due time. `null` when there is no reminder.

status.description: `open` while the task is pending, `completed` once it is done.

version.description: Version of the task; it grows with every change. Send it as `expected_version` to make sure nobody changed the task in between.

TriggerType.description:
Suscriber status:
* `trigger.admin.manual` - Manual by an admin
* `trigger.form.completed` - Form completed
* `trigger.contact.suscribed` - Contact suscribed
* `trigger.contact.added.to.group` - Contact added to group
* `trigger.contact.removed.from.group` - Contact removed to group
* `trigger.send.a.campaign` - Send a campaign
* `trigger.click.on.campaign` - Click on campaign
* `trigger.click.on.campaign.link` - Click on campaign link
* `trigger.not.click.on.campaign` - Not click on campaign
* `trigger.open.on.campaign` - Open on campaign
* `trigger.not.open.on.campaign` - Not open on campaign
* `trigger.specific.date` - Specific date
* `trigger.aniversary.date` - Aniversary date
* `trigger.suscription.date` - Suscription date
* `trigger.buy.a.product` - Buy a product
* `trigger.time.since.last.purchase` - Time since last purchase
* `trigger.abandoned.cart` - Abandoned cart
* `trigger.payment.reminder` - Payment reminder
* `trigger.order.processed` - Order processed
* `trigger.order.paid` - Order paid
* `trigger.order.shipped` - Order shipped
* `trigger.order.cancelled` - Order canceled
* `trigger.order.refunded` - Order refunded
* `trigger.suscriber.revalidation` - Subscriber revalidation
* `trigger.poll.answered` - Survey poll answered

WebhookEventType.description:
Webhook event types:
Events of `marketing` webhooks (one audience):
* `member_subscribed` - triggered when a member subscribes to an audience
* `member_unsubscribed` - triggered when a member unsubscribes from an audience
* `member_added_to_group` - triggered when a member is added to a group
* `member_removed_from_group` - triggered when a member is removed from a group
* `member_campaign_opened` - triggered when a member opens a campaign
* `member_campaign_clicked` - triggered when a member clicks a link in a campaign
* `member_campaign_delivered` - triggered when a campaign email is delivered
* `member_campaign_bounced` - triggered when a member's email address bounces
* `member_campaign_complained` - triggered when a member reports a campaign as spam
* `member_automation_started` - triggered when a member starts an automation
* `member_automation_completed` - triggered when a member completes an automation
* `member_automation_cancelled` - triggered when a member cancels an automation
* `custom_automation_step` - triggered by a Send Webhook automation step
* `member_sms_subscribed` - triggered when a contact opts in to SMS
* `member_sms_unsubscribed` - triggered when a contact opts out of SMS
* `member_sms_delivered` - triggered when an SMS is delivered
* `member_sms_bounced` - triggered when an SMS hard-bounces (failed delivery)
* `member_sms_clicked` - triggered when a member clicks a link in an SMS campaign
* `member_sms_replied` - triggered when a contact replies to an SMS campaign

Events of `crm` webhooks (account-wide, without audience):
* `crm_contact_created` - triggered when a contact is created
* `crm_contact_updated` - triggered when a contact is updated
* `crm_contact_deleted` - triggered when a contact is deleted
* `crm_company_created` - triggered when a company is created
* `crm_company_updated` - triggered when a company is updated
* `crm_company_deleted` - triggered when a company is deleted
* `crm_opportunity_created` - triggered when an opportunity is created
* `crm_opportunity_updated` - triggered when an opportunity is updated
* `crm_opportunity_deleted` - triggered when an opportunity is deleted
* `crm_opportunity_stage_changed` - triggered when an opportunity moves to another stage

info.description:
The Easymailing API provides a comprehensive set of RESTful endpoints that allow you to programmatically manage campaigns, audiences, subscribers, statistics, and more.  
Built around REST principles, the API features predictable resource-oriented URLs, standard HTTP response codes, and commonly used methods such as GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE.  
This documentation outlines all available REST API methods, complete with example requests and responses. Additionally, you can import this documentation into tools like Postman to test and interact with the API using your personal authentication token.  

If you need additional functionality that the API doesn't currently support, please [contact us](https://ayuda.easymailing.com).

### Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)  
The Easymailing API is designed to be accessed from server-side applications only. Client-side requests are not permitted.  

### Authentication  
The Easymailing API supports two authentication methods:

#### Option 1: API Key (recommended for direct integrations)  
API keys are the quickest way to implement machine-to-machine authentication. Use this method when building your own integrations with Easymailing.  
- Use the `X-Auth-Token` header to provide your API key in each request.  
- You can generate your API key in the Easymailing control panel under **Config > API Keys**.  

Example request:  
```bash
curl -X GET 'https://api.easymailing.com/my_suscription' \
     --header 'Content-Type: application/ld+json' \
     --header 'X-Auth-Token: <YOUR_API_KEY>'
```

#### Option 2: OAuth2 Bearer Token (for third-party apps)  
If you are building a third-party application that connects to Easymailing on behalf of users, use OAuth2 authentication. Users authorize your app through the OAuth2 flow, and your app receives an access token to make API requests on their behalf.  
- Use the `Authorization` header with the Bearer token.  
- Refer to our [OAuth2 documentation](https://developers.easymailing.com/oauth) for details on implementing the authorization flow.  

Example request:  
```bash
curl -X GET 'https://api.easymailing.com/my_suscription' \
     --header 'Content-Type: application/ld+json' \
     --header 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>'
```

get.description:
Returns the activity timeline of one contact, company or opportunity, newest first: what happened and who did it, as the Activity tab of the record in the Customer App shows it. It covers changes to the record, tasks, notes, files, emails and meetings linked to it and, for a contact, also its subscriptions, campaign results, automations, orders, forms and surveys.

**When to use:** To know what has happened with a record before acting on it: the last emails and meetings, who changed what, which campaigns it received, how an opportunity moved through its stages. Narrow it with `category[]`, `type[]` and the dates when the record has a long history.

**When not to use:** It is read-only: to add something to the timeline, create a note with `create_note` or a task with `create_task`; the activity is written by the action itself. To read the full text of a note, use `get_note` or `list_notes`; for tasks, `list_tasks`. To read one member's subscription history in an audience, use `list_member_activities`, which is empty in accounts that already use the new Customer App. There is no combined timeline of the whole account: you must name the record.

**Filters:** Exactly one of `contact`, `company` or `opportunity` is required, with the UUID of the record. A UUID that is not valid, does not exist or belongs to a record the user cannot see gives `404`.
`category[]` and `type[]` keep only those categories and types; `occurred_from` and `occurred_to` keep a range of days in the time zone of the account. The order is fixed (most recent `occurred_at` first); there is no `order` parameter and no text search. A company or an opportunity only has `crm` rows, so another category gives an empty list.
Visibility is decided row by row: a task or note row is hidden to a user without `crm.tasks_notes.read` or who cannot see that task, and an email or meeting row is hidden to a user who cannot read that mailbox or calendar. Hidden rows are not removed: they come back with `availability` `unavailable` (or `deleted` when the email or meeting was deleted for good), no `data` and an anonymous actor, so the list never leaks their content. Rows from a Google mailbox or calendar that was disconnected are not returned at all.
Pagination: activity is paged with `itemsPerPage` (default 25, maximum 50) and an opaque `cursor[gt]`: to read the next page, call again with the same record and the same filters and the `cursor[gt]` of the `hydra:next` link of the previous response. The cursor only works for the same user, record and filters. The response gives the total number of rows in `hydra:totalItems`, counted when the first page is read (hidden rows count; rows written afterwards do not change it); keep following `hydra:next` until a page comes back empty.

**Permissions:** Requires any of the `contacts.read`, `crm.contacts_companies.read` or `crm.opportunities.read` capabilities. Reading a contact requires the `contacts.read` capability; no CRM seat is needed. The rows of the `crm` category (company, owner, opportunities, tasks, notes, files, emails and meetings) are included only if the user also has a CRM seat and `crm.contacts_companies.read`; without them they are left out silently. Reading a company requires a CRM seat and `crm.contacts_companies.read`. Reading an opportunity requires a CRM seat, `crm.opportunities.read` and read access to its pipeline.

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or deactivated credentials, or the account is not active, suspended or expired. An unknown API key or token answers `{"message": …}` as `application/json`; the other cases are problem+json with the reason in `detail`.

403.description:
The key or token lacks the capability listed under Permissions for the record you asked for (`contacts.read` for a contact). Use one that has it; the response does not say which permission is missing.

`crm_capability_required`: You asked for a company or an opportunity and the account does not have the CRM module active. Only an account admin can activate it.

`crm_permission_denied`: You asked for a company or an opportunity and the user's role lacks the capability listed under Permissions, or the token has no user behind it. Use credentials of a user who has it.

`crm_seat_required`: You asked for a company or an opportunity and the user has no CRM seat. Ask an account admin to assign one.

404.description: `unknown_record`: The contact, company or opportunity does not exist in this account, the value is not a UUID, or the user cannot see it (for an opportunity, no read access to its pipeline). Find it with `list_contacts`, `list_companies` or `list_opportunities`.

422.description:
`crm_activity_invalid_filter`: None of `contact`, `company` and `opportunity` was sent, more than one was sent, or another filter is not valid. Send exactly one record and check `category[]`, `type[]` and the dates.

`crm_activity_invalid_cursor`: `cursor[gt]` is malformed or was issued for another user, record or set of filters. Start again from the first page.

A query parameter is outside its limits: `itemsPerPage` outside 1 to 50, more than 8 categories or 60 types, a category that does not exist, or a date that is not `YYYY-MM-DD`. Read `violations[].propertyPath`.

429.description: Too many requests with the same API key (a fixed window of one minute). `Retry-After` says when to try again.

Retry-After.description: Moment from which to retry, as `Y-m-d H:i:s` in the server time zone (not seconds).

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

503.description:
`crm_capability_unavailable`: CRM access could not be checked right now. Nothing was changed; retry in a few seconds.

`tenant_account_not_ready`: The account access model is not ready yet. Retry later; if it persists, contact support.

Starts a background job that adds to the group the members of the audience that match your conditions. Members already in the group should be skipped (see side effects). It runs in the background and returns an async task straight away, not the final result: read it with `get_async_task` using the task `uuid` and repeat until `status` is `completed` or `failed`.

**When to use:** To fill a group from a one-off rule, for example everyone in Spain who opened a campaign, without creating a saved segment.

**When not to use:** To add one member, use `member_add_from_group`. To reuse a saved segment, use `async_task_segment_add_to_group`. To remove members, use `async_task_group_remove_from_conditions`.

**Side effects:** Starts an async task. For each member added it records an entry in the member's activity and fires the automations triggered by joining a group; the group's member count is refreshed. It does not fire the `member_added_to_group` webhook. A member who is already in this group but also in another group is selected again: their activity entry and group automations can run a second time, and they are counted in `result_meta.added`. Each condition has a `field` (IRI of a condition field from `list_audience_condition_fields`), an `operator` (one of the `operators` that field lists) and a `value` whose type depends on the field: text, integer, decimal, boolean, date string (`2026-01-15`) or an array for multi-select fields.
