post.description:
Starts a background job that unsubscribes the email and the SMS channel of the members of the segment that are confirmed. It runs in the background and returns an async task straight away, not the final result: read it with `get_async_task` using the task `uuid` and repeat until `status` is `completed` or `failed`. It is NOT the bulk version of `member_unsubscribe`: it writes the new status directly.

**When to use:** To stop sending to a whole slice of an audience at once, for example inactive contacts.

**When not to use:** It only accepts old audience segments (`list_audience_segments`), never contact segments. For a single member, use `member_unsubscribe`, which also fires the unsubscription webhook and cancels the member's automations. To delete the people instead of unsubscribing them, use `async_task_segment_delete_contacts`.

**Side effects:** Starts an async task. The affected members change to `suscriber.status.unsuscribed.admin` (email) and their SMS status to the same value, they stop receiving campaigns, and the unsubscription is recorded in the activity of each email-unsubscribed member. Unlike `member_unsubscribe` it does NOT fire the `member_unsubscribed` / `member_sms_unsubscribed` webhooks and does NOT cancel the automations the members are in. The audience statistics are refreshed afterwards. `result_meta.unsubscribed` counts only the members whose email status was confirmed. Channels that are not confirmed are left as they are. If no member of the segment has a confirmed email, the job ends without changing anyone, even if some have a confirmed SMS.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `marketing.audiences.write` capability.

get.description:
Lists the members of one audience, most recently updated first, with their status, groups, custom field values and engagement stats. A member is one person's subscription to this audience. Each member carries its `contact`, the IRI of the person.

**When to use:** To browse or export the people of an audience, or to find members by status, source, group or form. To look a person up by email in this audience, filter with `email`.

**When not to use:** To find out in which audiences a person is, whatever the audience, use `search_member`. To read one member whose UUID you know, use `get_audience_member`. To list the people of the account whatever their audiences, with their company, tags and attributes, use `list_contacts`.

**Filters:**
All filters are optional and combine with AND.
- `email`: partial match on the email address.
- `phone`: exact match, E.164.
- `status` / `sms_status`: exact subscription status of the email / SMS channel.
- `source` and `email_opt_in_source`: how the member entered the audience (both filter the same column).
- `sms_opt_in_source`: how the member opted in to SMS.
- `groups`: comma-separated group UUIDs; only members in all of them.
- `suscription_form`: members who signed up through that form.
Sorting: `order[field]=asc|desc` with `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `status`, `source`, `contact.email`, `uniqueOpens`, `uniqueClicks`, `deliveredEmails`, `orders`, `revenue` or `rating`. Default: `updatedAt` descending.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `contacts.read` and `marketing.audiences.read` capabilities.

post.description:
Adds a person to an audience and requests their email subscription, or merges the data you send into the member if that person is already in the audience. People are matched across the whole account by email, then by phone, so the same person is one contact with one member per audience. The response includes the `contact` IRI of the person.

**When to use:** To subscribe a new person or re-send a sign-up from a form, store or integration. It is safe to call again for the same email. Members are also created by `create_store_customer` (shop buyers) and by the public subscription forms.

**When not to use:** To create a person without subscribing them to any audience, use `create_contact`. To subscribe a contact you already have by UUID, use `subscribe_contact_to_audience`. To change data of a member you already have by UUID, use `update_audience_member`. To subscribe an existing member again use `member_subscribe`; to unsubscribe one use `member_unsubscribe`. To see in which audiences an email already is, use `search_member`. To register a shop buyer together with their customer record, use `create_store_customer`.

**Side effects:** What the person receives depends on their state. A new person (or one still unconfirmed) in a double opt-in audience gets a confirmation email and stays `suscriber.status.unconfirmed` until they confirm, unless `disable_double_opt_in=true`. In a single opt-in audience, or with `disable_double_opt_in=true`, they become `suscriber.status.confirmed` at once: the `member_subscribed` webhook fires, automations triggered by a subscription start, and the welcome email is sent if the audience has one (unless `disable_welcome_email=true`). An email on the audience's suppression list always gets a confirmation email instead. Someone who unsubscribed on their own (`suscriber.status.unsuscribed`) is not subscribed again: they get a confirmation email and stay unsubscribed until they confirm, even with `disable_double_opt_in=true`. Someone whose status is `suscriber.status.unsuscribed.admin` (unsubscribed through the API, by an administrator or by the cleaning rules) can be subscribed again normally: in a single opt-in audience, or with `disable_double_opt_in=true`, this call confirms them again at once unless their address is on the suppression list. Do not use it to bring back a person who asked to leave. An already confirmed member only gets their data updated. Confirmation emails are not repeated within 15 minutes. If a phone is sent, the SMS subscription follows the audience's SMS opt-in (a confirmation SMS in double opt-in, unless `disable_sms_double_opt_in=true`). Groups assigned fire the `member_added_to_group` webhook and group automations once the member is confirmed.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `contacts.write` and `marketing.audiences.write` capabilities.

WARNING: changing the `email` or the `phone` to a different value resets the subscription of that channel for the whole person, in EVERY audience they belong to, not only this one: their email `status` (or `sms_status`) becomes empty, so they stop being a confirmed recipient everywhere until each of their members is subscribed again. Any other field leaves the subscription status as it is.

**When to use:** To correct or complete the data of a member identified by UUID: name, location, custom fields or groups. Change the email or phone only when the user explicitly asks for it, after telling them that the person will have to be subscribed again in all their audiences.

**When not to use:** To subscribe or unsubscribe someone, use `member_subscribe` or `member_unsubscribe`. To add or remove one group without resending the whole list, use `member_add_from_group` or `member_remove_from_group`. To add a new person, use `create_audience_member`. There is no way to change the email and keep the person subscribed: afterwards the person has to be subscribed again with `member_subscribe`. The name, email, phone and location edited here belong to the person's contact and are shared by all their audiences; the same data can also be changed with `update_contact`, which additionally handles company, owner, tags and attributes.

**Side effects:** If `email` or `phone` really changes (a different address, ignoring case, or a different number): in every audience of the person, the email `status` (for `email`) or `sms_status` (for `phone`) is set to empty, and the consent recorded for that channel is invalidated. No confirmation message is sent to the new address or number, so the person is not subscribed again until you call `member_subscribe` on each audience (it may not be able to do it, see that operation). Groups the member enters or leaves because of the new `groups` list fire the `member_added_to_group` and `member_removed_from_group` webhooks and the group automations.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `contacts.write` and `marketing.audiences.write` capabilities.

put.description:
Asks to subscribe again the email channel, the SMS channel or both of a member who already exists in the audience. It is a request, not a guarantee: the channel is confirmed at once only in some cases (see side effects); otherwise the person gets a confirmation message and the status does not change until they confirm.

**When to use:** When a person who never confirmed, or who was unsubscribed through `member_unsubscribe` or after changing their email or phone, asks to receive messages again and you have their member UUID. Check the `status` and `sms_status` in the response: they tell what really happened.

**When not to use:** To add someone who is not in the audience yet, use `create_audience_member`. To unsubscribe, use `member_unsubscribe`. Never use it to override a person who unsubscribed themselves: in that case it only sends them a confirmation email. If you have the contact UUID instead of the member UUID, `subscribe_contact_to_audience` does the same.

**Side effects:** Email channel. In a double opt-in audience the person always gets a confirmation email and the status changes only when they confirm. In a single opt-in audience the email is confirmed at once, except when the person unsubscribed themselves (`suscriber.status.unsuscribed`) or the address is on the audience's suppression list: then they get a confirmation email and stay as they were until they confirm. Confirmation emails are not repeated within 15 minutes. SMS channel: in an audience with SMS double opt-in the status becomes `suscriber.status.unconfirmed` and a confirmation SMS is sent; otherwise it is confirmed at once. When a channel is confirmed at once, the `member_subscribed` or `member_sms_subscribed` webhook fires, the automations triggered by a subscription start and, for email, the audience's welcome email is sent if it has one. A channel the person has no email or phone for is ignored. A channel whose consent was recorded by the new Customer App (this includes a channel invalidated by changing the email or phone) is left as it is and the call still answers 200: always read `status` and `sms_status` in the response. The `disable_double_opt_in` and `disable_welcome_email` flags of member creation do not apply here.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `contacts.write` and `marketing.audiences.write` capabilities.

put.description:
Unsubscribes the confirmed email channel, SMS channel or both of one member of this audience. The member keeps their record, groups and history, but stops receiving campaigns and automations from this audience. Only channels that are currently confirmed change.

**When to use:** When a person asks to stop receiving messages, or when the user wants to stop sending to one person without deleting them.

**When not to use:** To delete the person from the audience, use `delete_audience_member`. To subscribe them again, use `member_subscribe`. For many members of a segment there is `async_task_segment_unsubscribe`, but it is NOT the bulk version of this operation: it changes the status directly, without webhook, without cancelling automations and without the other effects listed here. If you have the contact UUID instead of the member UUID, `unsubscribe_contact_from_audience` does the same.

**Side effects:** Email: the status becomes `suscriber.status.unsuscribed.admin`, the unsubscription is recorded in the member's activity, the automations the member is in are cancelled (`member_automation_cancelled` webhook) and the `member_unsubscribed` webhook fires. SMS: the status becomes `suscriber.status.unsuscribed.admin` and the `member_sms_unsubscribed` webhook fires (automations are not cancelled for an SMS-only unsubscription). The address is not added to the audience's suppression list, so `create_audience_member` or `member_subscribe` can bring the person back in a single opt-in audience without a confirmation.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `contacts.write` and `marketing.audiences.write` capabilities.

post.description:
Holds the contact before it moves to the next step, either for a relative amount of time (minutes, hours, days or weeks) or until a fixed moment: a time of day, certain weekdays, a day of the month or a calendar date. Its place in the flow is set with `parent`, `parent_yes` or `parent_no`; with none of them it becomes the first step.

**When to use:** Between steps of a flow: wait two days after a welcome email before the follow-up, or hold the next message until 9:00 the next morning.

**When not to use:** To branch on what the contact did, use `create_step_condition`; a delay only waits.

**Side effects:** The wait starts when the contact reaches the step. Time is counted in the contact's time zone, or in the audience's if the contact has none, or in UTC. A time-of-day wait ends at the next occurrence of that time, and a calendar date that has already passed lets the contact continue at once. Known issue: `day_week` is saved as the numbers you send (0 = Sunday), but the engine that resumes the contact reads weekday names, so a contact that reaches a `specific_day_week` wait may get stuck there; use another unit for now. If the chosen position is already occupied, the new step is inserted there and the step that was there moves after it.

**Permissions:** Requires the author role or higher, or the `marketing.automations.write` capability.

post.description:
Sends an HTTP POST with the contact, the automation and the step, plus any extra key-value pairs you add, when the contact reaches this step, and lets the contact continue without waiting for the response. Its place in the flow is set with `parent`, `parent_yes` or `parent_no`; with none of them it becomes the first step.

**When to use:** To tell another system (a CRM, a chat bridge, your own app) that a contact reached a point of the flow.

**When not to use:** To be notified of Easymailing events in general, such as subscriptions or clicks, create a webhook with `create_webhook`. To alert a person by email, use `create_step_send_notification`.

**Side effects:** Creates a webhook for this step, titled "Automation: <automation title>", with a generated signing secret if you do not send one; each request carries an `Easymailing-Webhook-Signature` header (HMAC-SHA256 of the body). Known behavior: webhooks are matched by event type, not by step, so when any send-webhook step runs, every active webhook of the audience that listens to this event receives the call, including the webhooks of the other send-webhook steps. The payload names the automation and the step, so a receiver can ignore the ones it does not want. If the chosen position is already occupied, the new step is inserted there and the step that was there moves after it.

**Permissions:** Requires the author role or higher, or the `marketing.automations.write` capability.

**When to use:** To remove one action from a flow, for example an email that is no longer wanted.

**When not to use:** To move a step instead of removing it, use `move_step_position`.

**Permissions:** Requires the author role or higher, or the `marketing.automations.write` capability.

post.description:
Starts the automation for a shopper whose cart in a store has not been modified for the chosen waiting time, optionally only when the cart contains (or, with `exclude`, does not contain) certain products or categories.

**When to use:** To send a cart-recovery email or SMS to shoppers who added products to a cart and never placed the order.

**When not to use:** For an order that was placed but not paid, use `create_trigger_payment_reminder`. To react when an order is paid, use `create_trigger_order_paid` (or `create_trigger_buy_a_product` for certain products). For a message weeks after buying, use `create_trigger_time_since_last_purchase`.

**Side effects:** Known limit: the scheduled check only looks at carts last modified within the previous 2 hours, so a waiting time above 2 hours matches no cart and the trigger never fires; the wait counts from the cart's last change, not from its creation. The run is cancelled automatically if the order is processed or paid first. The cart is attached to the run so emails can use its data, and it must belong to a customer linked to a contact of the audience. Works only while the automation is active and the trigger is enabled, and only for contacts with a confirmed subscription. A contact that is already running through the automation is not started again; after finishing, it can enter again only if `workflow_repeat` is true and 24 hours have passed.

**Permissions:** Requires the author role or higher, or the `marketing.automations.write` capability.

post.description:
Starts the automation every year on the day and month stored in a date custom field of the contact, such as a birthday or a customer-since date, from the start of that day, or a few days or weeks beforehand.

**When to use:** For birthday messages or yearly anniversaries of a date you keep in a custom field.

**When not to use:** For a one-off date, such as an event or a contract expiry, use `create_trigger_specific_date`. For the anniversary of the day the contact subscribed, use `create_trigger_suscription_date`. To welcome someone the day they subscribe, use `create_trigger_contact_subscribed`.

**Side effects:** The day is the contact's own time zone when it has one, otherwise the audience's. Contacts born on 29 February are matched on 28 February in years that are not leap years. Works only while the automation is active and the trigger is enabled, and only for contacts with a confirmed subscription. A contact is never started again within 6 months of its previous run, and enters again at all only if `workflow_repeat` is true.

**Permissions:** Requires the author role or higher, or the `marketing.automations.write` capability.

post.description:
Queues up to 500 API calls to be run one after another in the background, in the order given. It returns the batch at once; the calls run later. A call that fails does not stop the others.

Each call has `method` (POST, PUT, GET or DELETE), `path` (an endpoint of this API, for example `/audiences/{audienceUuid}/members`), an optional `body` (a JSON string), optional `params` (query parameters) and an optional `external_identifier` of yours to match results.

Each call is checked with the permissions of the token that created the batch, as if you sent it yourself: a call the token is not allowed to make is not run and shows a 403 in the results. The batch can therefore do anything those permissions allow, including deleting or sending.

The batch belongs to the user of the credential that creates it: only that user and an account administrator can read or delete it afterwards.

**When to use:** To load or change many records in one go, for example adding thousands of members or moving many members to groups, without waiting for each call.

**When not to use:** For one call, use the operation directly. To act on all members of a segment or group, use the asynchronous operations of Segments and Groups.

**Side effects:** Every call runs and takes effect in the background, with all the side effects of that operation (emails, automations, webhooks). A call that answers with a server error (500) is attempted up to 3 times. The calls run later with the credential that created the batch: if its user is deactivated before they run, the calls still pending fail with 401.

**Permissions:** No specific permission.

put.description:
Changes the configuration of one of the user's booking pages: title, hours, duration, calendars, form fields and the rest. Only the keys you send change.

**When to use:** To edit a draft, or to change a published or paused page (opening hours, a day off, fields of the form, calendars).

**When not to use:** To publish, pause or archive the page, use `publish_booking_page`, `pause_booking_page` or `archive_booking_page`. To change who can use the page, use `set_booking_page_sharing`. To change the sender or the email subjects, use `update_booking_email_settings`. An archived page cannot be edited.

**Side effects:** On a published page the change takes effect immediately for new bookings (the whole page is validated as if publishing it). A change of configuration makes the offer links created earlier with `create_booking_offer` stop working. Bookings already made are not touched. Nothing is sent and no activity entry is recorded.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. Booking pages have no separate read permission, so it is also required to read. Pages belong to the user who owns the token: each user manages only their own pages, and a page of another user is answered as not found.

**When to use:** Only when the user explicitly wants to retire the page for good, for example after replacing it with a new one.

**When not to use:** To close it temporarily, use `pause_booking_page`. To change it, use `update_booking_page`. There is no operation to delete a booking page.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. Booking pages have no separate read permission, so it is also required to read. Pages belong to the user who owns the token: each user manages only their own pages, and a page of another user is answered as not found.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. Booking pages have no separate read permission, so it is also required to read. **When to use:** When the page is complete and the user wants people to start booking, or to reopen a paused page.

**When not to use:** To close the link without losing the page, use `pause_booking_page`. If the user only wants to hand the link to one person for a few specific times, create a private proposal with `create_booking_offer` on an already published page.

**Side effects:** The page becomes public and the response carries `public_url`. Each booking then creates an event in the destination Google Calendar with the person who booked as attendee, so Google sends them the invitation; a booking can also create or update a contact and a company according to `contact_policy` and `company_policy`; and the booking emails leave from the page sender. Nothing is sent and Google is not called by this request. Offer links created earlier stop working.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. Booking pages have no separate read permission, so it is also required to read. get.description:
Returns the free times a published booking page can offer in a date window, after applying its opening hours, days off, notice, horizon, buffers, daily limit and the events in the host's Google calendars, plus the merged busy ranges.

**When to use:** To see which times can be proposed before calling `create_booking_offer`, or to tell the user when the host is free.

**When not to use:** It only works on a published page of the user or one shared with them: a draft or paused page answers not found. It does not book anything. To change the opening hours themselves, use `update_booking_page`.

**Side effects:** Reads the host's calendars from Google during the request, one call per calendar of the page, so it can take a few seconds. Nothing is written to Google and nothing is sent.

**Filters:** `from` and `to` are required, must carry a time zone and span at most 31 days; they are cut to the notice period and the horizon of the page. `duration` must be one of the page's `allowed_durations` (only `default_duration` if the page does not let people choose). `time_zone` is any IANA time zone and is only echoed back: all times in the response are UTC.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. The page must be published and either belong to the user who owns the token or be shared with them (`set_booking_page_sharing`).

post.description:
Creates a proposal of up to 10 specific times on a published booking page and returns one link per time. Whoever opens a link lands on the booking page with that time selected and still has to confirm the booking.

**When to use:** When the user wants to offer a person a few exact times, for example to paste the links into an email.

**When not to use:** To give a general link where the person picks any free time, use the page's `public_url`. This does not book a meeting and does not send anything; to book a meeting yourself with someone, create the meeting directly. Check the times first with `get_booking_page_availability`.

**Side effects:** Reads the host's calendars from Google during the request, once per option and calendar, so it can take several seconds. Nothing is written to Google and nothing is sent: the links are only returned to you, and the person who receives them (when you put them in an email) is the one who books. The offer does not block the calendar. Each link is revalidated when opened, so an option someone else books in the meantime stops working. The links stop working at `expires_at`, and when the page is paused, archived or its configuration changes.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. The page must be published and either belong to the user who owns the token or be shared with them (`set_booking_page_sharing`).

put.description:
Sets who else can use the user's booking page: nobody, the whole account, or chosen users and teams. People with access can put its link in their emails and propose times from the host's calendar; they cannot edit, publish or share the page.

**When to use:** When colleagues should be able to send the user's booking link or propose times from the user's availability, for example the sales team using a sales rep's page.

**When not to use:** Sharing does not publish the page or notify anyone, and it does not change the page's configuration: use `update_booking_page` and `publish_booking_page` for that. To see who can be added, use `list_booking_page_sharing_candidates`.

**Side effects:** The people who gain access can see, through `get_booking_page_availability` and `create_booking_offer`, when the host is busy (merged time ranges without event titles) and can create proposal links for the host. Nobody is notified. People who lose access stop seeing the page; offer links they already created keep working. The page version grows.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. Booking pages have no separate read permission, so it is also required to read. Pages belong to the user who owns the token: each user manages only their own pages, and a page of another user is answered as not found. Only the owner of the page can change its sharing.

get.description:
Returns the email campaigns of your account, newest first, with their status (draft, scheduled, sending, sent...), type, audience and configuration. SMS campaigns are not included: they have their own list.

**When to use:** To find a campaign by name, status, type or audience, to see what was sent last, or to get the UUID that the other campaign operations ask for.

**When not to use:** To read one campaign in full, with its recipient count and delivery warnings, use `get_campaign`. For SMS campaigns, use `list_sms_campaigns`.

**Filters:** Default order: newest created first.

- `title`: campaigns whose name contains the text.
- `status`: exact status, for example `campaign.status.sent` (same values as the `status` field).
- `type`: exact type, for example `campaign.regular` or `campaign.test.ab` (same values as the `type` field). Automation campaigns (`campaign.automation`) are listed too.
- `hash`: exact hash of the campaign, the code that follows `em_ch=` in the links of its emails.
- `audience`: UUID of the audience.

Sorting: `order[createdAt]`, `order[updatedAt]`, `order[status]`, `order[startedAt]` (when sending began) or `order[finishedAt]` (when it ended), each `asc` or `desc`. The newest created campaign is not always the last one sent: for the last sent, combine `status=campaign.status.sent` with `order[startedAt]=desc&itemsPerPage=1`.

**Permissions:** Requires the viewer role or higher, or the `marketing.campaigns.read` capability.

post.description:
Creates a regular email campaign as a draft: sender, subject, content, recipients and tracking are saved, but nothing is sent. The campaign stays a draft until someone sends or schedules it. To be valid it needs a `title`, an `audience`, who it goes to (`send_to`, with `groups`, `contact_segment` or `filter` when needed), `email_config` (from name, subject, and sender and reply-to unless the audience has defaults), `campaign_config` and the content (`template`, `template_html` or `template_simple_json_code`).

**When to use:** To prepare a one-off email for an audience, some of its groups, a contact segment or a filter of its own. Afterwards check it with `get_campaign` (`recipient_count`), send yourself a preview with `campaign_send_test`, and then send it (`campaign_send_now`) or schedule it (`campaign_schedule`).

**When not to use:** For an A/B test use `create_campaign_test_ab_subject`, `create_campaign_test_ab_sender` or `create_campaign_test_ab_template`. To ask inactive subscribers to confirm they want to stay, use `create_campaign_revalidation`. To send a survey, use `create_campaign_survey`. To start from an existing campaign, use `duplicate_campaign`. For text messages, use `create_sms_campaign`.

**Side effects:** Nothing is sent to anyone. If you send `template_html` or `template_simple_json_code`, a new template is created in your account; the campaign thumbnail is generated in the background. With `contact_segment`, a draft follows the current revision of the segment until it is scheduled or sent; then that revision is fixed.

**Permissions:** Requires the author role or higher, or the `marketing.campaigns.write` capability. Choosing `contact_segment` or `filter` also requires the `contacts.read` capability.

422.description:
The campaign is incomplete or inconsistent. Each entry in `violations[].propertyPath` names the field to fix: missing title, subject, from name or content; groups or segment from another audience; or no default sender in the audience when `email_config.from_email` or `reply_to` is omitted.

`invalid_contact_filter`: The `filter` does not have the documented shape: no `match` or `conditions`, a group inside a group, more than 10 groups or 50 conditions, a condition without `field` or `operator`, or `audience` missing on a field that requires it (or sent on one that does not). `violations[].propertyPath` points to the part to fix, e.g. `filter.conditions[2].audience`.

`unknown_filter_field`: A `field` is not in the catalog of this user (it does not exist, was archived, or the user cannot filter on it). Look it up again with `list_contact_filter_fields`.

`invalid_filter_operator`: The `operator` is not one of that field's `operators`. Use one listed by `get_contact_filter_field`.

`invalid_filter_value`: A `value` does not fit its operator: wrong `value_shape`, a value outside `constraints` (length, number range, date `YYYY-MM-DD`, `lower` above `upper`) or an option that is not in the field. Read the field again with `get_contact_filter_field`.

`invalid_filter_reference`: A referenced record (audience, group, tag, campaign, attribute option, user) does not exist in this account or cannot be used here. Look its UUID up again in the field's `options` or with `list_contact_filter_field_suggestions`.

`filter_too_complex`: The filter is larger than the engine evaluates. With `match: any` at the top level, the loose conditions plus the `all` groups plus every condition of the `any` groups can be at most 20; an `any` group holds at most 20 conditions; a campaign-activity condition names at most the allowed campaigns. Split it or simplify it.

`filter_strategy_unavailable`: One condition cannot be evaluated by the engine right now (for example an attribute whose storage is not ready). Nothing was saved; remove that condition and retry later. If it persists, contact support.

`campaign_field_not_allowed`: A `field` exists but cannot select campaign recipients (its `usable_in` does not include `campaign`, e.g. company fields). Remove that condition.

`campaign_filter_empty`: `send_to_custom_segment` was sent without conditions in `filter`. Add at least one, or use `send_to_segment` with `contact_segment`.

`segment_reference_deleted`: `contact_segment` was deleted. Choose another one with `list_contact_segments`.

`segment_reference_denied`: `contact_segment` uses fields this user cannot evaluate. Use credentials of a user who can, or another segment.

post.description:
Creates a draft email campaign that asks subscribers to confirm they still want to receive your emails. Nothing is sent when you create it. Once it is sent, recipients who do not click the confirmation link end up unsubscribed. The template must contain the confirmation link tag `link.list.revalidation_confirm_subscription`. To be valid it needs a `title`, an `audience`, who it goes to (`send_to`, with `groups` or `list_segment` when needed), `email_config` (sender and reply-to, unless the audience has defaults), `campaign_config` and the content (`template`, `template_html` or `template_simple_json_code`).

**When to use:** To clean an audience of people who no longer engage, or to re-confirm consent, before sending your regular campaigns.

**When not to use:** For an ordinary newsletter use `create_campaign`: sending a revalidation campaign unsubscribes the people who do not confirm. For other campaign types see `create_campaign_survey` and the A/B test operations.

**Side effects:** Nothing is sent to anyone. Creating it does not unsubscribe anyone; the unsubscribing happens when the campaign is sent. If no `subject` or `preview_text` is given, default texts asking the subscriber to confirm are used.

**Permissions:** Requires the author role or higher, or the `marketing.campaigns.write` capability.

post.description:
Creates a draft email campaign that carries a survey block, so recipients answer a quick poll from the email or open the survey page. Nothing is sent when you create it. With `survey` the campaign is linked to that survey right away; without it, link one later with `campaign_select_survey`. It needs a `title`, an `audience`, `send_to` (with `groups` or `list_segment` when needed), `email_config` (sender and reply-to, unless the audience has defaults) and `campaign_config`; the content is optional.

**When to use:** To ask your contacts a question or run a survey by email. The survey must already exist and be active in the same audience (see `list_surveys`, and `survey_activate` to activate it).

**When not to use:** For an ordinary email use `create_campaign`. To link a survey to a survey campaign that already exists, use `campaign_select_survey`.

**Side effects:** Nothing is sent to anyone. With `survey`, and if the campaign has no content, a template with the survey block is created and the survey question becomes the subject. The survey block (`{{ block.poll.<survey_uuid> }}`) must be in the template before sending; the API does not check this when sending. If the survey cannot be linked, the campaign has already been created without it.

SCHEDULES THE CAMPAIGN FOR REAL: sets the date and time at which it will be sent to all its recipients, with no further action. Nothing goes out now; at that time the same real send as `campaign_send_now` happens, to real people, and it cannot be recalled. Before sending, check with `get_campaign` that the campaign has recipients (`recipient_count` above 0), no entry in `warnings` has `blocks_sending: true`, and its status is draft, ready or scheduled. The API does not check recipients, credits or account status when scheduling: they are checked when the scheduled time arrives, and if the check fails the campaign moves to `campaign.status.error` and nothing is sent.

**When to use:** Only when the person has confirmed the campaign and the date at which it must go out to all its recipients.

**When not to use:** To send right away, use `campaign_send_now`. To cancel the schedule, use `campaign_unschedule`. To check the email first, use `campaign_send_test`. For an SMS campaign, use `schedule_sms_campaign`. Automation campaigns cannot be scheduled.

**Side effects:** The status becomes `campaign.status.scheduled` and the send is queued for the date. At that time real emails go out and email credits are used. Until then the campaign can be edited with `update_campaign` or cancelled with `campaign_unschedule`. Scheduling an already scheduled campaign replaces its date. With `campaign_confirmation_email`, a confirmation email goes to `mailing_confirm_emails` when the sending ends.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `marketing.campaigns.send` capability.

**When not to use:** To send to the actual recipients, use `campaign_send_now` or `campaign_schedule`. For an SMS campaign, use `send_sms_campaign_test`.

Creates a company in the CRM, standalone: it is not linked to any contact or audience. Every editable field (domains, owner, location, classification, social links and attribute values) can be sent in the same request, and they are all saved together or not at all. **When to use:** To register an organization the account does not have yet, before or after creating the people who work for it.

**When not to use:** To add a person, use `create_contact`; that operation can also link the person to a company. **Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability.

Permanently deletes a company. Its contacts and opportunities stay, no longer linked to it. There is no archive and no undo.

**When to use:** Only when the user explicitly asks to delete this company for good, for example a duplicate or a test record.

**When not to use:** To fix a wrong name, domain or owner, use `update_company`. To detach a person from the company without deleting it, use `update_contact` with `company` set to `null`. There is no merge of companies: to consolidate duplicates, move the contacts with `update_contact`, then delete the duplicate.

**Side effects:** Deleted with the company: its activity, its notes, its files (a Google Drive reference never deletes the original in Drive) and its attribute values; its domains are freed. Kept but unlinked from it: contacts (each gets a `company unlinked` entry in its activity), opportunities (same), tasks and meetings; connected emails stay, no longer shown under the company. If the account creates companies automatically from connected Gmail or Calendar, a new email or meeting with one of its domains can create it again; there is no list of suppressed domains. No webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.companies.delete` capability.

Lists every field the user can filter contacts on, with its operators, the shape of the value each operator expects and, for fixed lists, its options: contact data and attributes, tags, owner, company, location, audience subscriptions (status, source, dates, groups, consent, forms, audience custom fields) and email and SMS campaign activity.

**When to use:** Before writing the `filter` of `create_contact_segment`, `update_contact_segment`, `search_contacts`, `count_contacts` or a campaign: you need each field's `id`, an operator `id` and the right value.

**When not to use:** For the conditions of old audience segments, of bulk group actions by conditions and of automation condition steps, use `list_audience_condition_fields`: those are a different catalog. To read the values stored for one person, use `get_contact`.

**Filters:** All matching fields come in one response, in menu order; there is no pagination.
- `search`: fields whose `label` or `id` contains the text, ignoring case.
- `category`: only the fields under that category `id` (e.g. `audiences`).
- `usable_in`: only the fields usable there (`search`, `segment` or `campaign`).

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.read` capability. The catalog is shaped by the user's permissions, as in Customer App: audience and subscription fields need `marketing.audiences.read`; the owner, the company fields and the last email interaction need a CRM seat and `crm.contacts_companies.read`. A field the user cannot use is not listed.

get.description:
Returns one field of the contact filter catalog with its operators, value shapes, constraints and options.

**When to use:** To check which operators and values are valid for one field before writing a condition, or after a `invalid_filter_value` error.

**When not to use:** To find a field when you do not know its `id`, use `list_contact_filter_fields` with `search`. For values that come from the data (`options_mode: suggestions`), use `list_contact_filter_field_suggestions`.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.read` capability. The catalog is shaped by the user's permissions, as in Customer App: audience and subscription fields need `marketing.audiences.read`; the owner, the company fields and the last email interaction need a CRM seat and `crm.contacts_companies.read`. A field the user cannot use is not listed.

get.description:
Returns the values found in the account's data for a field whose `options_mode` is `suggestions` (for example the subscription sources, or the values used in a text attribute), each with its `value` and `label`.

**When to use:** To pick an existing value for a condition when the field has no fixed list, so that the condition matches what is really stored.

**When not to use:** For fields with `options_mode: closed`, the values are already in `options` of `get_contact_filter_field`. To choose campaigns for an activity condition with `specific_campaigns`, take their UUIDs from `list_campaigns` or `list_sms_campaigns`.

**Side effects:** Suggestions are read from a cache that refreshes by itself; a value created a moment ago can be missing.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.read` capability. The catalog is shaped by the user's permissions, as in Customer App: audience and subscription fields need `marketing.audiences.read`; the owner, the company fields and the last email interaction need a CRM seat and `crm.contacts_companies.read`. A field the user cannot use is not listed.

get.description:
Lists the segments of the account by name: saved filters over all the contacts of the account, whatever their audiences. They are the same segments Customer App shows in the Contacts filter and offers as recipients of email and SMS campaigns.

**When to use:** To find a segment by name before using it in a campaign (`contact_segment` of `create_campaign` or `create_sms_campaign`), counting it (`count_contacts`) or changing it.

**When not to use:** For the old segments that live inside one audience (only the classic panel shows them), use `list_audience_segments`. To see who matches a segment now, use `search_contacts` with `segment`.

**Filters:** There are no filters: the list is ordered by name (ignoring case). Pagination: `page` and `itemsPerPage` (default 100, maximum 100); the total is in `hydra:totalItems`.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.read` capability.

post.description:
Saves a filter over the contacts of the account as a named segment and publishes its first revision. The segment is global: it selects contacts, not members of one audience, and appears at once in Customer App (Contacts filter and campaign recipients).

**When to use:** When the user wants to reuse a selection of contacts, for example «engaged subscribers from Spain», to send campaigns to it or to watch how many people it has. Read the fields first with `list_contact_filter_fields`; to check the conditions before saving, count them with `count_contacts`.

**When not to use:** For a one-off selection that is not worth saving, send the `filter` straight to `search_contacts`, `count_contacts` or the campaign. To label people by hand use groups (`create_audience_group`). Old audience segments (`create_audience_segment`) are not visible in Customer App: do not use them for new work.

**Side effects:** The segment is shared with every user of the account. Right after saving, the contacts that match are counted and stored in `match_count`; if that count fails or takes too long the segment is saved anyway with `match_count: null`. The segment is recorded as created by the person who owns the key or token; there is no «via Maia» mark on segments. Nothing is sent and no webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.read` and `contacts.attributes.manage` capabilities. A segment is shared by the whole account, so it takes the same capabilities as a team saved view.

delete.description:
Deletes a segment: it disappears from the list, from the Contacts filter and from the campaign recipients picker, and its name can be used again. The contacts are not touched. Its revisions are kept so that scheduled and sent campaigns keep their recipients.

**When to use:** Only when the user explicitly wants the segment gone. Check `usage` with `get_contact_segment` first and tell the user which uses it has.

**When not to use:** To stop one campaign from using it, change that campaign's recipients (`update_campaign`, `update_sms_campaign`). To delete or unsubscribe the people it selects, there is no segment action yet; the classic `async_task_segment_*` actions only accept old audience segments.

**Side effects:** Nothing stops the deletion while campaigns use the segment. Draft and ready campaigns that target it can no longer be sent until their recipients are changed (`get_campaign` shows `contact_targeting.contact_segment_deleted: true` and an `error_code`); campaigns already scheduled keep the revision they were scheduled with and go out normally. Nothing is sent and no webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.read` and `contacts.attributes.manage` capabilities. A segment is shared by the whole account, so it takes the same capabilities as a team saved view.

put.description:
Renames a segment and/or replaces its conditions by publishing a new revision. Fields you leave out keep their value; `filter` replaces all the conditions, it is never merged. Every saved change, a rename too, publishes revision N+1 and raises `version`.

**When to use:** To fix or widen the conditions of a segment, or to give it a clearer name. Read it first with `get_contact_segment` and send its `version` as `expected_version`.

**When not to use:** To save different conditions as another segment, use `create_contact_segment`. To change who receives one campaign without touching the segment, change the campaign (`update_campaign`, `update_sms_campaign`).

**Side effects:** Draft and ready campaigns that target the segment follow the new revision; campaigns already scheduled keep the revision they were scheduled with, and sent ones never change. `match_count` is recalculated as in `create_contact_segment`. Recorded under the person who owns the key or token (no «via Maia» mark). Nothing is sent and no webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.read` and `contacts.attributes.manage` capabilities. A segment is shared by the whole account, so it takes the same capabilities as a team saved view.

get.description:
Returns the tags that exist in the account for contacts, in alphabetical order, so you can reuse an existing tag instead of creating a new one.

**When to use:** Before tagging a contact with `create_contact` or `update_contact`, to find the exact name of an existing tag.

**When not to use:** Tags label people across the whole account; to group the members of one audience, use groups (`list_audience_groups`).

**Filters:** `search` matches the tag name, ignoring case and as a partial match. Pagination: `page` and `itemsPerPage`.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.read` capability.

parameters.description: Text to find in the tag name.

get.description:
Returns the people of the account, newest first, one record per person whatever the audiences they belong to. Each contact carries its identity, company, owner, tags and attributes, not its audience subscriptions.

**When to use:** To find a person by name, email or phone, to list the people of a company (`company` filter), or to get the UUID of a contact before reading or changing it.

**When not to use:** To find the contacts that match conditions (audience and subscription status, tags, attributes, campaign activity) or a segment, use `search_contacts`; to only know how many they are, `count_contacts`. To see who is subscribed to one audience, with their subscription status and groups, use `list_audience_members`. To see the audiences of one contact, use `list_contact_audience_memberships`. To check whether an email is already subscribed anywhere, use `search_member`.

**Filters:** `search` matches, ignoring case and as a partial match, the first name, last name, full name, primary email and primary phone; leading and trailing spaces are ignored. `company` keeps only the contacts linked to that company; `exclude_company` keeps every other contact, including those without company; they cannot be combined. The order is fixed (newest first); there is no `order` parameter. Pagination: `page` and `itemsPerPage`, like the rest of the API; the response gives the total in `hydra:totalItems`. For filters by audience, status, tag, attribute or activity, use `search_contacts`.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.read` capability. The `company` and `exclude_company` filters, and the `company` and `owner` fields, also require a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.read` capability.

post.description:
Creates a person in the account with their data, tags and attributes, and optionally links them to an existing company. The person is not added to any audience and no email is sent. It needs at least an email or a phone, and it never merges with an existing contact: if the email or phone already belongs to another person the call fails.

**When to use:** To register a person who is not a subscriber yet, for example a lead, a customer or someone you met, so you can work with them in the CRM.

**When not to use:** To subscribe a person to an audience, use `create_audience_member`: it creates the contact if it does not exist, matches it by email or phone if it does, and requests the subscription. To subscribe a contact you already have, use `subscribe_contact_to_audience`. To change a contact that already exists, use `update_contact`. To register a company, use `create_company`.

**Side effects:** The creation is recorded in the contact's activity as done by the person who owns the key or token (marked «via Maia» when Maia made the request), and the contact's `record_source` is `api`. The contact belongs to no audience, receives no email and is not subscribed to anything. Retrying a request that already succeeded fails with `contact_identity_conflict` because the email or phone now exists; it does not create a second person. Tags that do not exist yet are created.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.read` and `contacts.write` capabilities. Sending `company` also requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability.

post.description:
Counts the distinct contacts of the account that are in a segment and/or match a filter, with the same engine and the same short-lived cache as the counters of Customer App. Nothing is changed.

**When to use:** To answer «how many contacts…» questions, to check a filter before saving it as a segment, or to know the current size of a segment (its `match_count` is only the count at publication).

**When not to use:** To get the contacts themselves, use `search_contacts`. To know how many people a campaign will reach (confirmed subscribers of its audience and channel), read `recipient_count` with `get_campaign` or `get_sms_campaign`: this count is not limited to an audience or a channel.

**Side effects:** The count can take a moment on large accounts. When it is not ready yet the answer is `state: pending` with `retry_after_ms`: call again with the same body after that time. A recent result is reused for a few seconds (`state: stale` while it is being refreshed); send `revalidate: true` to force a new count.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.read` capability. The fields usable in `filter` depend on the user's permissions, as in `list_contact_filter_fields`.

422.description:
`invalid_contact_filter`: The `filter` does not have the documented shape: no `match` or `conditions`, a group inside a group, more than 10 groups or 50 conditions, a condition without `field` or `operator`, or `audience` missing on a field that requires it (or sent on one that does not). `violations[].propertyPath` points to the part to fix, e.g. `filter.conditions[2].audience`.

`unknown_filter_field`: A `field` is not in the catalog of this user (it does not exist, was archived, or the user cannot filter on it). Look it up again with `list_contact_filter_fields`.

`invalid_filter_operator`: The `operator` is not one of that field's `operators`. Use one listed by `get_contact_filter_field`.

`invalid_filter_value`: A `value` does not fit its operator: wrong `value_shape`, a value outside `constraints` (length, number range, date `YYYY-MM-DD`, `lower` above `upper`) or an option that is not in the field. Read the field again with `get_contact_filter_field`.

`invalid_filter_reference`: A referenced record (audience, group, tag, campaign, attribute option, user) does not exist in this account or cannot be used here. Look its UUID up again in the field's `options` or with `list_contact_filter_field_suggestions`.

`filter_too_complex`: The filter is larger than the engine evaluates. With `match: any` at the top level, the loose conditions plus the `all` groups plus every condition of the `any` groups can be at most 20; an `any` group holds at most 20 conditions; a campaign-activity condition names at most the allowed campaigns. Split it or simplify it.

`filter_strategy_unavailable`: One condition cannot be evaluated by the engine right now (for example an attribute whose storage is not ready). Nothing was saved; remove that condition and retry later. If it persists, contact support.

`list_field_not_allowed`: A `field` exists but cannot select contacts here (its `usable_in` does not include `search`, e.g. a specific contact, which only campaigns accept). Remove that condition.

`segment_reference_not_found`: The `segment` does not exist in this account. Find its UUID with `list_contact_segments`.

`segment_reference_deleted`: The `segment` was deleted. Choose another one with `list_contact_segments`.

`segment_reference_denied`: The `segment` uses fields this user cannot evaluate (for example audience fields without `marketing.audiences.read`). Use credentials of a user who can, or another segment.

`segment_reference_invalid`: The stored definition of the `segment` is no longer valid (for example it uses an attribute or audience that was removed). Fix the segment with `update_contact_segment`.

post.description:
Returns, newest first, the contacts of the account that are in a segment and/or match a filter: audience and subscription status, groups, tags, attributes, location, owner, campaign activity… Each contact comes as in `list_contacts`. Nothing is changed.

**When to use:** To answer «who are the contacts that…» questions, to see a few examples of a segment, or to get the UUIDs of the people that match before acting on them one by one.

**When not to use:** To browse or find people by name, email or phone, use `list_contacts` (simpler and with a total). To only know how many match, use `count_contacts`. For the members of one audience with their subscription data, use `list_audience_members`.

**Filters:** Body, not query: `segment` and `filter` as described below; both are optional. The order is fixed (newest first). Pagination by cursor, without total: send `items_per_page` (default 30, maximum 50) and, for the next page, the same body with `cursor` set to the `next_cursor` of the previous answer; `next_cursor` is `null` on the last page. A cursor only works with the body it was issued for.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.read` capability. The fields usable in `filter` depend on the user's permissions, as in `list_contact_filter_fields`.

get.description:
Returns the audiences a person is subscribed to or has been subscribed to, one membership per audience, with the email and SMS status, the source and date of each opt-in, the groups and the consent. A person who is in no audience gets an empty list. The result is not paginated.

**When to use:** To answer in which audiences a person is and with which status, before subscribing or unsubscribing them, or to get the UUID of their member in each audience.

**When not to use:** To find a person by email and see their memberships in one call, use `search_member`. To list everyone in one audience, use `list_audience_members`. To read the person's own data (company, tags, attributes), use `get_contact`.

**Permissions:** Requires the `marketing.audiences.read` capability.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes the subscription of a person to one audience, with its groups, custom field values and history in that audience. The person stays as a contact of the account and in their other audiences, even if this was the last one.

**When to use:** Only when the user explicitly asks to take a person out of an audience for good.

**When not to use:** To stop sending to the person but keep their record and history in the audience, use `unsubscribe_contact_from_audience`. To delete the person from the account, use `delete_contact`. If you have the member UUID instead of the contact, `delete_audience_member` does the same.

**Side effects:** The membership and its history in this audience (groups, custom field values, activity) are deleted and cannot be recovered through the API; the consent recorded for it is invalidated. The counters of the audience and the subscriber count of the plan are updated. The person stays as a contact and in their other audiences.

put.description:
Requests the subscription of an existing contact to an audience, on the email channel, the SMS channel or both, using the contact's current primary email and phone. If the person is not in the audience yet, the membership (the member) is created; if they already are, their subscription is requested again. It is a request, not a guarantee: the channel is confirmed at once only in some cases (see side effects); otherwise the person gets a confirmation message and stays unconfirmed until they confirm.

**When to use:** When you already have the contact and want it in an audience, or when someone who never confirmed, or was unsubscribed through the API, asks to receive messages again. Check `status` and `sms_status` in the response: they tell what really happened.

**When not to use:** To create the person and subscribe them in one call, use `create_audience_member`. To create a person without subscribing them, use `create_contact`. If you have the member UUID instead of the contact, `member_subscribe` does the same. Never use it to override a person who unsubscribed themselves: in that case it only sends them a confirmation email.

**Side effects:** It follows the legacy subscription rules of the audience. Email channel: in a double opt-in audience the person always gets a confirmation email and the status changes only when they confirm; in a single opt-in audience the email is confirmed at once, except when the person unsubscribed themselves (`suscriber.status.unsuscribed`) or the address is on the audience's suppression list: then they get a confirmation email and stay as they were until they confirm. Confirmation emails are not repeated within 15 minutes. SMS channel: in an audience with SMS double opt-in the status becomes `suscriber.status.unconfirmed` and a confirmation SMS is sent; otherwise it is confirmed at once. When a channel is confirmed at once, the `member_subscribed` or `member_sms_subscribed` webhook fires, the automations triggered by a subscription start and, for email, the audience's welcome email is sent if it has one. A channel the contact has no email or phone for is ignored. A channel whose consent was recorded by the new Customer App (this includes a channel invalidated by changing the email or phone) is left as it is and the call still answers 200: always read the statuses in the response. The `disable_*` flags apply only when the membership did not exist and is created by this call.

**Permissions:** Requires the `marketing.audiences.write` capability.

put.description:
Unsubscribes the confirmed email channel, the SMS channel or both of a contact in one audience. The contact keeps their record, groups and history in that audience, but stops receiving its campaigns and automations. Only channels that are currently confirmed change; the other audiences of the person are not touched.

**When to use:** When a person asks to stop receiving messages from an audience, or when the user wants to stop sending to someone from one audience without deleting anything.

**When not to use:** To remove the person from the audience altogether, use `delete_contact_audience_membership`. To delete the person from the account, use `delete_contact`. SMS: the status becomes `suscriber.status.unsuscribed.admin` and the `member_sms_unsubscribed` webhook fires (automations are not cancelled for an SMS-only unsubscription). The address is not added to the audience's suppression list, so `create_audience_member` or `subscribe_contact_to_audience` can bring the person back in a single opt-in audience without a confirmation.

**Permissions:** Requires the `marketing.audiences.write` capability.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a person from the account: their data, tags, attribute values, notes and files, their activity and their subscriptions to every audience. The company and the opportunities of the person survive without the link, tasks survive without the association, and email suppressions already recorded stay. It cannot be undone.

**When not to use:** To stop sending emails to the person but keep their record, use `unsubscribe_contact_from_audience` or `member_unsubscribe`. To take the person out of one audience only, use `delete_contact_audience_membership`; removing the last membership never deletes the contact. This is not a legal data-erasure request process.

**Side effects:** The contact, its audience memberships (with their groups, custom field values and history), its attribute values, tags, notes, files and activity are deleted. Companies and opportunities are kept and lose the link; tasks are kept and lose the association with the contact; meetings and synced emails are kept and lose the link to the person. Suppressions already recorded stay and deleting does not add a new one. Aggregate statistics of past campaigns are kept without the personal link.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.delete` capability.

put.description:
Changes the data of a person: name, email, phone, job title, location, links, owner, company, tags and attribute values. Fields you leave out keep their value. Changing the primary `email` or `phone` keeps the person subscribed: a contact is the person, so in every audience where that channel was confirmed it stays confirmed with the new address or number. Only a subscription still waiting for confirmation is reset (its confirmation message went to the old address and can no longer be completed), and unsubscribed channels stay unsubscribed.

**When to use:** To correct or complete the data of a person identified by UUID, to update their email or phone when they change it, to assign an owner, to link them to a company or to set tags and attributes.

**When not to use:** To subscribe or unsubscribe the person, use `subscribe_contact_to_audience` or `unsubscribe_contact_from_audience`. To change data that belongs to one audience (its groups or custom fields), use `update_audience_member`. To add a new person, use `create_contact`.

**Side effects:** All the fields of the request are applied together: if one is rejected, nothing is saved and the contact stays as it was. Every field that really changes is recorded in the contact's activity as done by the person who owns the key or token (marked «via Maia» when Maia made the request); sending the value a field already has records nothing. If the primary `email` or `phone` really changes, confirmed subscriptions of that channel keep their status with the new destination; a pending confirmation of that channel is cancelled and its status emptied; no message is sent to the new address or number. Tags that do not exist yet are created.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.read` and `contacts.write` capabilities. Setting or removing `company` also requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability.

Uploads one file and stores it under the UUID you choose, ready to be listed in `attachment_ids` of a draft or a send. The body is the raw file; nothing is sent to anyone.

**When to use:** Before `create_email_draft`, `update_email_draft`, `send_email`, `schedule_email` or `send_email_batch` when the email carries a file.

**When not to use:** To forward the attachments of a received email, do not upload them: send `forwarded_attachment_ids` with `mode` `forward`. There is no operation to attach a file of the CRM Files directly: download it and upload it here.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability.

post.description:
Schedules one individual email for each of 2 to 50 recipients, starting at `scheduled_at` and then five minutes apart within the mailbox limits.

**When to use:** When the user wants to write to several people one by one starting at a given date and time, and has confirmed text, list and time. Confirm with the user before calling it.

**When not to use:** To send now, use `send_email_batch`. For one email to everyone, use `schedule_email`. To change the time: cancel with `cancel_email_batch` and schedule again.

**Side effects:** One email per recipient of `to`, each with their own unsubscribe link (if you include the unsubscribe block), spaced at least five minutes apart within the mailbox limits (12 per hour, 200 per day), so a batch of 50 takes hours to finish. A scheduled batch has no undo window. Each recipient counts against the user's limit of 100 scheduled emails. Released asynchronously by background jobs.

**Filters:** Opt-out protection as in `send_email`.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. The sender must be a mailbox the user can send from: one of their own or one shared with them (see `list_email_senders`). Writing from an opportunity also requires `crm.opportunities.read` and the Work level on its pipeline.

409.description:
`email_send_conflict`: The `reason` extension tells which: `recipient_opted_out`: Some recipient asked not to receive CRM email (the addresses come in the `addresses` extension). Nothing was created. Tell the user and, only if they confirm, repeat the request with those addresses in `acknowledged_opt_outs`; otherwise remove them. `replaced_send_changed`: The send named in `replaces_send` is alive again (queued, sending or sent). 422.description: `email_send_rejected`: The request was understood but the email cannot be used as it is; nothing was saved. The `reason` extension tells which: `batch_recipients_invalid`: A batch needs 2 to 50 addresses in `to` and none in `cc` or `bcc`. For one email to several people, use `send_email`. `too_many_individual_recipients`: More than 50 addresses in `to`. Split them into several batches. `recipients_required`: `to`, `cc` and `bcc` are all empty. Add at least one address. `recipients_invalid`: An address is not a valid email address. Fix or remove it. `subject_too_long`: `subject` is longer than 998 characters. Shorten it. `body_too_large`: `body_html` is too large. Shorten it or remove images. `body_invalid`: `body_html` cannot be parsed (too deeply nested or invalid encoding). Send simpler HTML. `inline_image_invalid`: An image in `body_html` cannot be sent. Remove or replace it. `inline_image_too_large`: An image in `body_html` is larger than 5 MB. Use a smaller one. `message_too_large`: The complete email is larger than Gmail accepts. Remove attachments or images. `attachments_too_large`: Attachments, inline images and forwarded attachments add up to more than 25 MB. Remove some. `attachment_missing`: An id in `attachment_ids` was never uploaded, belongs to someone else, already goes with another email, or expired (an upload that nobody sends is deleted after 24 hours). Upload it again with `upload_email_attachment`. `source_email_required`: `mode` is `reply`, `reply_all` or `forward` but `source_email` is missing or is not an email IRI. `source_email_not_full_access`: `source_email` does not exist, or the user cannot see the whole original email, so it cannot be answered or forwarded. Check the IRI; otherwise ask whoever owns the mailbox for full access. `source_email_not_hydrated`: The original email has not finished loading from Gmail yet. Retry in a moment. `forwarded_attachment_invalid`: An id in `forwarded_attachment_ids` is not an attachment of the original email. Take the ids from the original email. `forwarded_attachments_unavailable`: Attachments of the original email cannot be forwarded in this environment. Send without `forwarded_attachment_ids`. `contact_required`: `record` is a contact that does not exist. Check it with `get_contact`. `record_not_found`: `record` is a company or opportunity that does not exist or that the user cannot see. `record_required`: Exactly one record is needed (a contact, a company or an opportunity). `personalization_tag_unavailable`: A personalization tag in `subject` or `body_html` is not available for this record, is `pending`, or is malformed. List the usable ones with `list_email_personalization_tags`. `schedule_invalid`: `scheduled_at` is not an ISO 8601 date-time with a time zone offset (for example `2026-11-05T09:30:00+01:00`). `schedule_too_soon`: `scheduled_at` is less than 90 seconds from now. Pick a later time, or use `send_email`. `schedule_too_far`: `scheduled_at` is more than 365 days from now. Pick an earlier time. `too_many_scheduled_sends`: The user already has 100 scheduled emails (each recipient of a batch counts). Cancel some with `cancel_email_send` or wait for them to go out.

post.description:
Sends the same message as one individual email to each of 2 to 50 recipients from the user's Gmail mailbox, so nobody sees the others. Each recipient gets their own send, personalized and queued five minutes apart.

**When to use:** When the user wants to write to several people one by one (for example every contact of a company) and has confirmed the text and the list. It reaches many people, so confirm with the user before calling it.

**When not to use:** For one email addressed to several people who see each other, use `send_email` with several addresses in `to`. To prepare it without sending, use `create_email_draft`. For a mass mailing to an audience, use the email campaign operations: a batch is limited to 50 and to the user's mailbox limits.

**Side effects:** One email per recipient of `to`, each with their own unsubscribe link (if you include the unsubscribe block), spaced at least five minutes apart within the mailbox limits (12 per hour, 200 per day), so a batch of 50 takes hours to finish. The whole batch has ONE undo window of 10 seconds, plus 10 of grace. It is delivered asynchronously by background jobs; this call answers 202 with one send per recipient. If the record is a contact, each email is linked to the contact that owns that address; from a company or opportunity they are linked only to the record. Failures notify the user in the app. Replaying the same `idempotency_key` returns the same batch.

**Filters:** Opt-out protection as in `send_email`: 409 `recipient_opted_out` with the addresses, until `acknowledged_opt_outs` lists them.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. The sender must be a mailbox the user can send from: one of their own or one shared with them (see `list_email_senders`). Writing from an opportunity also requires `crm.opportunities.read` and the Work level on its pipeline.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. Drafts are private: only their author can read or change them. The sender must be a mailbox the user can send from: one of their own or one shared with them (see `list_email_senders`). Writing from an opportunity also requires `crm.opportunities.read` and the Work level on its pipeline.

put.description:
Changes a draft. Only the fields you send change; `null` or an empty list clears a field. `revision` is required and must be the one you last read.

**When to use:** To correct or complete a draft the user already has: new text, recipients, subject or attachments.

**When not to use:** To create a draft, use `create_email_draft`. To send it, use `send_email` or `schedule_email` with `draft`.

**Side effects:** Saves the draft and raises its `revision`. Nothing leaves the mailbox. Attachments removed from the list are deleted; new ones start counting against the CRM Files storage.

**Filters:** Read the draft with `get_email_draft` first to get its `revision`. If the user edits the same draft in the app at the same time, the one that saves second gets 409 `draft_conflict`.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. Drafts are private: only their author can read or change them. The sender must be a mailbox the user can send from: one of their own or one shared with them (see `list_email_senders`). Writing from an opportunity also requires `crm.opportunities.read` and the Work level on its pipeline.

get.description:
Says when a send requested now from a mailbox would leave, taking into account its limits (12 per hour, 200 per day) and, for separate emails, the five minutes between them. It is an estimate: the real time is fixed when you send and can move if others send at the same time.

**When to use:** Before `send_email_batch`, to tell the user how long a batch will take, or before any send to warn of a delay.

**When not to use:** It reserves nothing and sends nothing. For the real release time of an existing send, read `release_at` with `get_email_send`.

**Filters:** - `count` (required): number of recipients, 1 to 500 (2 to 50 with `separate=true`). A single email with many recipients counts as one: it is estimated as 1.
- `separate`: `true` to estimate separate emails (a batch).

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. The sender must be a mailbox the user can send from: one of their own or one shared with them.

get.description:
Lists the emails the user has sent from the CRM that have not gone out yet or that need attention: queued, scheduled and failed or unconfirmed ones.

**When to use:** To answer what is scheduled or waiting to go out, which emails failed, or what is pending for one contact, company or opportunity.

**When not to use:** To list emails that already left, use `list_sent_emails`. To read one send, use `get_email_send`. To read emails received or the history of a record, use the email read operations (`list_emails`).

**Filters:** Send exactly one filter, otherwise 422 `email_send_rejected` with `list_filter_required`.
- `view=scheduled`: the user's emails waiting for their time (scheduled ones, plus every email of a batch that still has one to leave so its progress shows). At most 500. An email still inside its 10 seconds to undo is not listed yet.
- `view=failed`: the user's failed or unconfirmed sends not yet discarded. At most 200.
- `contact`, `company`, `opportunity`: the user's sends written from that record that are still waiting or need attention (not the ones already sent).
Only the user's own sends are listed, never other people's. The list is not paginated.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.read` capability.

post.description:
Schedules an email from the user's connected Gmail mailbox to leave at a chosen time, written from a contact, company or opportunity. It is stored and released at `scheduled_at` or later, if the mailbox has reached its sending limit by then.

**When to use:** When the user wants the email to go out at a specific date and time (tomorrow at 9, next Monday) and has confirmed the final recipients, text and time. It reaches other people, so confirm with the user before calling it.

**When not to use:** To send right away, use `send_email`. To save without sending, use `create_email_draft`. To change the time of an email already scheduled: cancel it with `cancel_email_send` and schedule it again; to edit its text too, open it first with `reopen_email_send`.

**Side effects:** The email goes out through the Gmail account of the chosen sender, as the user, to the recipients in `to`, `cc` and `bcc`. Nothing leaves before `scheduled_at`. It is released asynchronously by a background job, so read `state` with `get_email_send`. There is no undo window, but it can be cancelled with `cancel_email_send` while `state` is `queued`, and brought forward with `send_queued_email_now`. A user can have at most 100 scheduled emails. A failed send notifies the user in the app.

**Filters:** The same opt-out protection as `send_email`: 409 `recipient_opted_out` with the addresses, until `acknowledged_opt_outs` lists them.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. The sender must be a mailbox the user can send from: one of their own or one shared with them (see `list_email_senders`). Writing from an opportunity also requires `crm.opportunities.read` and the Work level on its pipeline.

Retry in a moment. `forwarded_attachment_invalid`: An id in `forwarded_attachment_ids` is not an attachment of the original email. Take the ids from the original email. `forwarded_attachments_unavailable`: Attachments of the original email cannot be forwarded in this environment.
