post.description:
Sends an email from the user's connected Gmail mailbox to the given recipients, written from a contact, company or opportunity. The email is queued and leaves about 20 seconds later (10 seconds in which the user can still undo it plus 10 of grace), or later if the mailbox has reached its sending limit.

**When to use:** When the user has asked to send an email and has confirmed the final recipients, subject and text. Because it reaches other people and cannot be taken back once it leaves, confirm with the user before calling it.

**When not to use:** To prepare an email without sending it, use `create_email_draft`. To send at a given time, use `schedule_email`. To send a separate copy to each of several people, use `send_email_batch`. To send from an email campaign to an audience, use the campaign operations: this one is a personal 1-to-1 email from the user's own mailbox.

**Side effects:** The email goes out through the Gmail account of the chosen sender, as the user, to the recipients in `to`, `cc` and `bcc`. It is delivered asynchronously: this call only queues it and answers 202; the upload to Gmail happens in a background job, so read `state` with `get_email_send` to know when it is `sent`. Until `release_at` it can still be stopped with `cancel_email_send`. A copy synced from Gmail then appears in the email history of the record (`copy_visible`). A failed send notifies the user in the app. The email is limited to 12 per hour and 200 per day per mailbox; beyond that `release_at` moves later. If `draft` is given, the draft is deleted.

**Filters:** Optional unsubscribe link: include the unsubscribe block in `body_html` (see its description). Recipients who clicked such a link before are protected: the call answers 409 `recipient_opted_out` with their addresses until `acknowledged_opt_outs` lists them. Check beforehand with `check_email_recipients`.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. The sender must be a mailbox the user can send from: one of their own or one shared with them (see `list_email_senders`). Writing from an opportunity also requires `crm.opportunities.read` and the Work level on its pipeline.

get.description:
Lists the email sequences of the account, most recently edited first, with their state, number of emails and waits, running enrollments and published sender.

**When to use:** To find a sequence by name or state before reading, editing, publishing or enrolling contacts in it, or to see which sequences are active.

**When not to use:** To read the steps of one sequence use `get_email_sequence`: the list leaves them out. To see who is enrolled in a sequence use `list_email_sequence_enrollments`. For marketing emails to an audience use `list_campaigns`; for event-driven flows use `list_automations`.

**Filters:** All filters are optional and combine with AND.
- `search`: part of the title, case-insensitive; surrounding spaces are ignored (up to 120 characters).

Sorting: fixed, last edited first; there is no `order` parameter.
Pagination: `page` and `itemsPerPage` (default 25, maximum 100), like the rest of the API; the response gives the total in `hydra:totalItems`.

**Permissions:** Requires the `automations.read` capability.

post.description:
Enrolls up to 25 contacts in an `active` sequence. Each one starts receiving the emails of the published version from the mailbox of the sequence, at their primary email address.

**When to use:** When the user wants specific contacts to receive a sequence, right now or from a future date.

**When not to use:** It only works on an `active` sequence with a sound sender (`can_enroll` in `get_email_sequence`): publish a draft with `publish_email_sequence`, or `resume_email_sequence` a paused one. To enroll many contacts split them in calls of 25. To take someone out, use `exclude_email_sequence_enrollment`. This is not a campaign: it does not subscribe anybody to an audience.

**Side effects:** THIS REACHES PEOPLE. Each enrolled contact gets an enrollment and its first email is planned for the first slot the schedule allows from `start` (the schedule window, the mailbox limits and the account queue still apply: `now` does not mean this second). The request does not send anything itself: the emails are sent afterwards by Easymailing's background workers through the connected Gmail of the sender, as that person, from their address and with their signature, always with the unsubscribe footer; the next emails follow after each wait until the contact replies, books a meeting, bounces, unsubscribes or the sequence ends. An `enrolled` entry (with the person who enrolled) is added to the sequence activity. Contacts that unsubscribed or are already in another live sequence are skipped, never forced. Repeating a request is safe: a contact already enrolled comes back as `skipped` with `enrollment_conflict`, so nobody gets duplicate emails.

**Permissions:** Requires the `automations.work` and `contacts.read` capabilities. The account must also have the CRM Pro plan. The user who owns the token must own the mailbox the sequence sends from, or hold the send permission on it when it is shared; otherwise the answer is 403 `sender_not_allowed`. The user who enrolls and the owner of that mailbox also need a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability, which the engine checks while enrolling; without them the answer is 403 without code.

put.description:
Uploads a file to a sequence under an `assetUuid` you choose, so that an email of the draft can attach it. The request body is the raw file, not JSON.

**When to use:** Before referencing the file in a step: upload it here, then put its `assetUuid` as `asset_uuid` in `attachments` of that step with `update_email_sequence_draft`. Repeating the same request with the same bytes is safe: you get the same asset.

**When not to use:** A file that is not an attachment of a sequence goes elsewhere: a document of a contact, company or opportunity through `create_file`, an attachment of a one-off email through `upload_email_attachment`. There is no multipart or base64 form, and an uploaded file cannot be changed or deleted: an asset no draft or version references is purged after 24 hours.

**Side effects:** The file is stored in the private storage of the account before the answer and counts in the CRM Files storage of the account from that moment (unreferenced assets are purged after 24 hours and the space returned). A file is at most 20 MiB through the public API, and the attachments of one email at most 25 MB together (checked when the sequence is published). Each file is checked by its name and its real content: executables and the extensions Gmail blocks are refused. Nothing is sent and the draft is not changed until a step references the asset.

**Permissions:** Requires the `automations.work` and `contacts.read` capabilities. The account must also have the CRM Pro plan.

put.description:
Replaces the title and the whole draft of a sequence: sending options, sender, exit rules and ALL its steps. The draft may be incomplete; what stops it from being published is only checked by the validation and the publication.

**When to use:** To write or change a sequence: read it with `get_email_sequence`, change what you need and send back everything, with the `draft_version` you read as `expected_draft_version`.

**When not to use:** It is a full replacement, not a partial update: any step you leave out is deleted and every field is required. To publish what you saved use `publish_email_sequence`; to find out what would stop the publication use `get_email_sequence_validation`. To attach a file, upload it first with `upload_email_sequence_asset`. To choose the sender, take the mailbox and signature from `list_email_senders`. It does not change who is enrolled.

**Side effects:** The title and the draft are replaced and `draft_version` goes up by one; an audit event `automation.sequence.draft_saved` is recorded. The published version, the enrollments already running and the emails already queued are NOT changed: new enrollments keep using the published version until you call `publish_email_sequence`. Nothing is sent. Each step must carry exactly the keys listed under `steps`; a missing or extra key is `validation_failed` with `invalid_shape`.

**Filters:** Rules that are checked on save (the rest wait for the publication): at most 60 steps and 20 emails; every step `uuid` is a distinct lowercase UUID; a `wait` has 1 to 365 days; with `threading` on, every email after the first has `subject: null`; `schedule.start` is earlier than `schedule.end` and both are `HH:00` or `HH:30`; `time_zone` is an IANA zone; the draft is at most 256 KB. The `sender` is only checked when it changes: you must own the mailbox or hold its send permission, and the signature must belong to it.

**Permissions:** Requires the `automations.work` and `contacts.read` capabilities. The account must also have the CRM Pro plan.

**When to use:** To remove a contact from a sequence, for example because they asked, a deal closed or the emails no longer apply. Also for an enrollment in `technical-error` that you do not want to retry.

**When not to use:** To hold the emails for a while without ending it use `pause_email_sequence_enrollment`. To stop everybody use `pause_email_sequence`. It cannot be undone, but the contact can be enrolled again with `enroll_contacts_in_email_sequence` (it counts as a re-entry). It does not unsubscribe the contact from anything else.

**Side effects:** The enrollment finishes as `excluded` and its queued email is canceled; an email being sent at that very moment is not cut (you get 409 `enrollment_effect_in_flight`: retry in a minute). The contact and their other sequences, audiences and activity are not touched. An `exited` entry with reason `manual_exclusion` and the person who acted is added to the activity.

**Permissions:** Requires the `automations.work` capability. Only the sender of the enrollment (the owner of the sequence's mailbox) or a user with the `automations.manage` capability can act on it; anyone else gets 403. A manager acts without access to the mailbox or to the contact.

put.description:
Pauses one live enrollment: its next email waits until the enrollment is resumed. The rest of the sequence goes on.

**When to use:** To hold the emails to one person, for example because they asked for time, without removing them.

**When not to use:** To stop for good use `exclude_email_sequence_enrollment`. To stop the whole sequence use `pause_email_sequence`. To undo, `resume_email_sequence_enrollment`.

**Side effects:** The enrollment becomes `paused`, its next send time is cleared and nothing leaves for it until it is resumed. A `paused` entry with the person who acted is added to the activity. Nothing is sent.

**Permissions:** Requires the `automations.work` capability. Only the sender of the enrollment (the owner of the sequence's mailbox) or a user with the `automations.manage` capability can act on it; anyone else gets 403. A manager acts without access to the mailbox or to the contact.

get.description:
Lists the emails synchronized from connected Gmail mailboxes that belong to one contact, company or opportunity, newest first. Each email carries only what the user is allowed to see of it: participants and date, plus subject, snippet and attachment count when the user has full access. Bodies are not included; open one with `get_email`.

**When to use:** To see the email history with a person or company before a call or follow-up, or to find the email where something was agreed.

**When not to use:** You must name the record: there is no list of every email of the account. To read the body and attachments of one email, use `get_email`. To see which mailboxes can be filtered, use `list_email_mailboxes`. For everything that happened on the record (emails, notes, calls, stage changes), not just emails, use `list_activities`.

**Side effects:** Read-only for your data, with one background effect: emails of the page whose content is still `index_only` are queued to be downloaded from Gmail (their `content_state` becomes `hydrating`). Nothing is sent to anyone. If the user has no connected mailbox, or none that is readable, the list is simply empty with `hydra:totalItems` 0.

**Filters:** Exactly one of `contact`, `company` or `opportunity` is required, with the UUID of the record. Which emails belong to a record: for a contact, those whose sender or recipient is one of its email addresses (main or alias, exact match); for a company, those with a participant outside the account on one of its domains (public, disposable and prohibited domains never identify a company); for an opportunity, those with a participant that is exactly one of its contacts' addresses, only while the opportunity was open (from its creation to its close and again from a reopening). `search` looks only in what the user may see. `occurred_from` and `occurred_to` are UTC days, both inclusive. `direction` and `mailbox` narrow by direction and by holding mailbox. The order is fixed (newest first); there is no `order` parameter.
Pagination: pages by `itemsPerPage` (default 30, maximum 100) and an opaque `cursor[gt]`: call again with the `cursor[gt]` of the `hydra:next` link, with the same record and filters, and keep following `hydra:next` until a page comes back empty. `hydra:totalItems` is the number of emails of the whole result for this user, counted on the first page and carried inside the cursor, so it does not change between pages.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.read` capability. Reading the emails of an opportunity needs the `crm.opportunities.read` capability instead (it is always granted together with `crm.contacts_companies.read`) and read access to the pipeline of the opportunity. Only emails held by a mailbox the user owns, or one whose owner shared it with the user, can be seen at all, and each email shows only what the sharing level of that mailbox allows. Being the owner or assignee of a record gives no extra access to its emails.

parameters.name: contact

parameters.description: UUID of a company: the emails of that record. Send exactly one of `contact`, `company` and `opportunity`.
parameters.name: company

parameters.description: UUID of a opportunity: the emails of that record. Send exactly one of `contact`, `company` and `opportunity`.

parameters.description: Text to look for, up to 200 characters. It searches only what the user may see of each email: participants and subject, plus body and attachment names for emails with `full_access`.
parameters.name: search

parameters.description: First day to include (UTC, inclusive), as `YYYY-MM-DD`.
parameters.name: occurred_from

parameters.description: Last day to include (UTC, inclusive), as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Not before `occurred_from`.
parameters.name: occurred_to

parameters.description: Only received (`incoming`) or only sent (`outgoing`) emails.

parameters.description: UUID of a mailbox, from `list_email_mailboxes`: only emails held by it. A mailbox the user cannot read yields no emails, not an error.
parameters.name: mailbox

parameters.description: Emails per page. Default 30, maximum 100.
parameters.name: itemsPerPage

parameters.description: Opaque cursor of the next page, taken from the `hydra:next` link of the previous response. Use it only with the same record and the same filters.
parameters.name: cursor[gt]

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or deactivated credentials, or the account is not active, suspended or expired. An unknown API key or token answers `{"message": …}` as `application/json`; the other cases are problem+json with the reason in `detail`.

403.description:
`crm_capability_required`: The account does not have the CRM module active. Only an account admin can activate it.

`crm_permission_denied`: The user's role lacks the capability listed under Permissions, or (for an opportunity) has no read access to its pipeline. Use credentials of a user who has it.

`crm_seat_required`: The user has no CRM seat. Ask an account admin to assign one.

404.description: `not_found`: The contact, company or opportunity does not exist in this account, the user cannot see it, or the email is not part of it for this user. The answer is the same in every case on purpose. Find the record with `list_contacts` or `list_companies`, and the email with `list_emails`.

422.description:
`crm_email_record_required`: None, or more than one, of `contact`, `company` and `opportunity` was sent. Send exactly one, with the UUID of the record whose emails you are reading.

`crm_email_invalid_filters`: `search` is longer than 200 characters or not valid UTF-8, `occurred_from` or `occurred_to` is not a `YYYY-MM-DD` date (or `occurred_to` is before `occurred_from`), `direction` is not `incoming` or `outgoing`, or `mailbox` is not a UUID.

`crm_email_invalid_cursor`: `cursor[gt]` is malformed, was issued for another record, another user or other filters. Start again from the first page, or follow `hydra:next` unchanged.

`itemsPerPage` is outside 1 to 100, or a record parameter is longer than 36 characters. Read `violations[].propertyPath`.

get.description:
Downloads the bytes of one attachment of a synchronized email, read from Google at that moment. The response is the raw file, always as an attachment, not JSON.

**When to use:** To get a file the sender attached to an email, after finding its `uuid` in the `attachments` of `get_email`.

**When not to use:** Embedded images of the body are not downloaded here: use `get_email_inline_images`. Files stored in the CRM (not in Gmail) are other operations. Attachments are not kept by Easymailing: if Google no longer has the message, the download fails.

**Side effects:** Calls the Google API inside the request and streams the answer as it arrives; nothing is stored. It spends Gmail quota of the mailbox owner. Each person can have 2 downloads at once and each mailbox 4, with a per-minute rate (60 per person, 150 per mailbox); above it the answer is a 429 before Google is called. The response carries `Content-Disposition: attachment`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and a sandboxing `Content-Security-Policy`; the `Content-Type` is the one the sender declared only when it is a safe type, otherwise `application/octet-stream`, and `Content-Length` is the declared size when Google gave it. A download that Google cuts in the middle ends shorter than `Content-Length`, so check the length before trusting the file.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.read` capability. Reading the emails of an opportunity needs the `crm.opportunities.read` capability instead (it is always granted together with `crm.contacts_companies.read`) and read access to the pipeline of the opportunity. It also needs `full_access` to the email through at least one readable mailbox. Only emails held by a mailbox the user owns, or one whose owner shared it with the user, can be seen at all, and each email shows only what the sharing level of that mailbox allows. Being the owner or assignee of a record gives no extra access to its emails.

put.description:
Replaces, for one email or for all the emails of a record in the owner's mailbox, the complete list of members and teams who get full read access (body, attachments, participants). Whoever is not in the lists loses the access this grant gave them.

**When to use:** When the owner of a mailbox wants a colleague or a team to read a specific conversation, or the whole email history of a contact, company or opportunity, for example to hand a customer over.

**When not to use:** To share a whole mailbox, or to change what the rest of the account sees of it, the owner uses Email and calendar settings in the app: that is not available through the API. A grant never shows more than the owner sees: the blocklist, protected list and hidden recipients still apply. To only see the current sharing, use `get_email_access_grants`. Only the owner of a mailbox that holds the email can see or change who it is shared with; for anyone else it is a 404, exactly as if the email did not exist.

**Side effects:** The people and teams in the lists can read the email (or the emails of the record, now and, for `scope` `record`, those that arrive later with the same addresses or domains) from that moment, with full read access, and lose it when they are left out. Nobody is notified. The change is recorded in the sharing audit of the mailbox with counts only, under the person who made the call; the current code does not record the "via Maia" mark for it. It does not touch who can send from the mailbox. `scope` `message` applies to this email in every mailbox of the owner that holds it; `scope` `record` applies to the record the request was made through (its addresses or domains as they are today, plus the ones not yet covered when `include_new` is true).

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. Only the owner of a mailbox that holds the email can change who it is shared with; for anyone else it is a 404, exactly as if the email did not exist. A user who can only read the CRM can see the sharing with `get_email_access_grants` but not change it. For the emails of an opportunity the user also needs read access to the pipeline of the opportunity. Recipients must be active members with a CRM seat, or teams of the account.

**When to use:** To see which documents are kept on a record (contracts, proposals, images) before downloading one, renaming it or deciding whether another upload is needed.

**When not to use:** You must name the record: there is no list of all the files of the account. To read one file whose UUID you know, use `get_file`. To know how much storage the account has left, use `get_file_storage_usage`. For text written about a record, use `list_notes`.

**Filters:** Exactly one of `contact`, `company` or `opportunity` is required, with the UUID of the record; an empty value counts as not sent. A UUID that does not exist, or that the user cannot see, gives `404`.
- `created_by`: only files uploaded by that person or system, by the `created_by.uuid` of another file; `unattributed` returns the files nobody is attributed with.
- `search`: files whose `display_name` contains the text, ignoring case; `%`, `_` and `!` are searched literally. Up to 100 characters after trimming; blank means no search.
Only `available` files are listed: a file whose content has not been stored yet, or was refused, does not appear. The order is fixed (newest first); there is no `order` parameter.
Pagination: files are paged with `itemsPerPage` (default 30, maximum 100) and an opaque `cursor[gt]`: to read the next page, call again with the same filters and the `cursor[gt]` of the `hydra:next` link of the previous response. The response gives the number of files that match the filters in `hydra:totalItems`; keep following `hydra:next` until a page comes back empty.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.read` capability. A file inherits the access of the record it is attached to: for a file of an opportunity the user needs the `crm.opportunities.read` capability and `read` access to its pipeline instead. A file the user cannot reach is reported as not found, never as forbidden.

post.description:
First of the two steps to attach a file to a contact, company or opportunity: declares the file (record, name and exact size) and reserves its space in the storage of the account. The file only exists for the record once its bytes are sent with `set_file_content`.

**When to use:** When a person wants to attach a document or image to a record. Flow: 1) call `create_file` with a fresh UUID in the `Idempotency-Key` header; 2) within 30 minutes send the raw bytes, exactly `size_bytes` long, to `set_file_content` with the `uuid` of the response; 3) the file becomes `available` and appears in `list_files`. The file name must end in one of these extensions: csv, tsv, txt, rtf, pdf, doc, docx, xls, xlsx, ppt, pptx, odt, ods, odp, gif, jpg, jpeg, png, webp, svg, tif, tiff, zip, rar and tar; at most 20 MiB.

**When not to use:** To change the name or description of a file that already exists, use `update_file`. To write text about a record, use `create_note`. The API cannot attach files that are in Google Drive or at a URL; only bytes sent by the caller.

**Side effects:** Reserves `size_bytes` of the storage of the whole account for 30 minutes, which can make another upload fail with `crm_file_quota_exceeded` meanwhile; the reservation is returned when the upload completes, is cancelled with `delete_file`, or expires (expired reservations are cleaned up by an hourly job). Nothing is visible on the record yet: the activity entry and the listing appear only when the content is stored. Nothing is sent to anyone and no webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. A file inherits the access of the record it is attached to: for a file of an opportunity the user needs the `crm.opportunities.work` capability and `work` access to its pipeline instead. A file the user cannot reach is reported as not found, never as forbidden.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes an available file from its record and frees its storage. There is no trash and no undo. On a file whose upload is still in progress (`uploading`), it cancels the upload instead.

**When to use:** Only when the user explicitly asks to delete this file, for example one attached to the wrong record, or to replace it by a new version. To abandon an upload started with `create_file` that will not be completed, call it without `expected_version`.

**When not to use:** To rename it, use `update_file`. Deleting a contact, company or opportunity already removes its files; do not delete them one by one for that.

**Side effects:** A `file.removed` entry appears in the activity of the record, done by the person who owns the token (marked «via Maia» when Maia made the request). The space is returned to the account at once and the stored bytes are removed in the background. Cancelling an upload adds no activity entry and returns its reserved space. Nothing is sent to anyone and no webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. A file inherits the access of the record it is attached to: for a file of an opportunity the user needs the `crm.opportunities.work` capability and `work` access to its pipeline instead. A file the user cannot reach is reported as not found, never as forbidden.

put.description:
Second step of an upload: stores the bytes of a file declared with `create_file` and makes it available on its record. The request body is the raw file, not JSON.

**When to use:** Right after `create_file`, with its `uuid`, within 30 minutes. Send `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` and exactly `size_bytes` bytes as the body. The response is the file already `available`. If the response is lost, send the same request again: the same bytes give the same file without storing it twice.

**When not to use:** To replace the content of a file that is already available: it cannot be done; delete it with `delete_file` and upload the new one. To rename it, use `update_file`. There is no multipart or base64 form: the body is the binary itself.

**Side effects:** The file becomes `available` and its size is counted in the storage used by the account. A `file.uploaded` entry appears in the activity of the record, done by the person who owns the token (marked «via Maia» when Maia made the request). The content is checked to be what its extension says (a `.pdf` must really be a PDF); if it is not, or its size differs from `size_bytes`, the file is closed as `failed`, its reserved space is returned and a new `create_file` is needed. Nothing is sent to anyone, nothing is written to Google and no webhook fires. The call is synchronous: when it returns, the file is stored.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. A file inherits the access of the record it is attached to: for a file of an opportunity the user needs the `crm.opportunities.work` capability and `work` access to its pipeline instead. A file the user cannot reach is reported as not found, never as forbidden.

409.description:
`crm_file_idempotency_conflict`: The file is already `available` and these bytes are different from the ones it holds. Content cannot be replaced.

413.description: The body is larger than the 20 MiB the edge proxy accepts. This answer comes from the proxy, is not `application/problem+json` and has no `code`. Send at most 20 MiB.

422.description:
`crm_file_not_uploadable`: The file no longer accepts content: its upload already failed, was cancelled or was refused. Start again with `create_file` and a new `Idempotency-Key`.

`crm_file_reservation_expired`: More than 30 minutes passed since `create_file`. Start again with `create_file` and a new `Idempotency-Key`.

`crm_file_size_mismatch`: The body does not have exactly the `size_bytes` declared. The upload is closed as `failed`: start again with `create_file`.

`crm_file_size_invalid`: The body is larger than 20 MiB. The upload is closed as `failed`: start again with a smaller file.

`crm_file_content_mismatch`: The bytes are not of the type the file name claims (for example a program named `.pdf`). The upload is closed as `failed`: start again with the right file.

`crm_file_scan_rejected`: The content was refused by the content check. The upload is closed as `rejected`.

`crm_file_scan_failed`: The content check could not be completed, so the file was not accepted. The upload is closed as `failed`: start again.

`crm_file_invalid_uuid`: The path identifier is not a valid UUID.

get.description:
Lists the meetings of connected Google calendars that the user can see, in one of two ways: the upcoming meetings related to one contact, company or opportunity, or the meetings of the user's own calendars within a date range. A meeting is an event synchronized from Google Calendar that Easymailing links to CRM records.

**When to use:** To know what meetings are coming up with a person, company or deal (`contact`, `company` or `opportunity`), or what the user has on their calendar between two dates (`from` and `to`).

**When not to use:** To read one meeting in full (description, guests, linked records, permissions), use `get_meeting`. To schedule a meeting, use `create_meeting`. It does not list past meetings of a record: those appear in the activity timeline of the record. It does not list tasks (`list_tasks`) or notes (`list_notes`). The calendars you can write to are in `list_meeting_calendars`.

**Filters:** Send either exactly one of `contact`, `company` or `opportunity` (the record mode), or both `from` and `to` (the range mode), never both modes.
Record mode returns the `confirmed` meetings related to that record, a meeting being related through a guest, a company email domain or a link made by hand, that have not ended yet (an all-day meeting counts until its last day has passed). The record must exist and be visible to the user, otherwise `404`.
Range mode returns the `confirmed` meetings of the user's own calendars that overlap `[from, to)`, whether or not they are related to any CRM record. `from` and `to` are ISO 8601 with the time zone or offset, `to` is after `from` and at most 42 days later. All-day meetings are matched by calendar day in the time zone of the user's profile.
The order is fixed: by start time, then by UUID. There is no `order` parameter and no text search.
Pagination: meetings are paged with `itemsPerPage` (default 10, maximum 20) and an opaque `cursor[gt]`: to read the next page, call again with the same filters and the `cursor[gt]` of the `hydra:next` link of the previous response. The response gives the total number of meetings in `hydra:totalItems`; keep following `hydra:next` until a page comes back empty. The data is what Easymailing last synchronized from Google, so an event created or changed in Google a moment ago may not show up yet.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.read` capability. For an `opportunity` it requires instead the `crm.opportunities.read` capability and read access to its pipeline. The date range mode always requires `crm.contacts_companies.read`. A meeting is only visible if it sits in a calendar the user owns or in a calendar a colleague shared with them, and it never shows events that involve protected or blocked addresses of the connection.

post.description:
Creates an event with a start and end time in one of the user's own Google calendars, invites the guests you list, and links the meeting to the contacts, companies and opportunities you name. The write to Google happens during the request; the meeting appears in the CRM once Google confirms it. The response is a receipt (`202`), not the meeting.

**When to use:** To schedule a meeting with one or more contacts: a demo, a call, a follow-up. Take `connection_uuid` and `calendar_id` from `list_meeting_calendars` (an entry with `writable: true`).

**When not to use:** To change an existing meeting, use `update_meeting`; to cancel it, `cancel_meeting`. To only link records to a meeting that already exists, use `replace_meeting_relations`. All-day events cannot be created, and a meeting cannot be created without a contact. To let people book a slot themselves, use a booking page instead. For something to do without a time slot, use `create_task`.

**Side effects:** This reaches other people. Easymailing writes the event in the user's Google Calendar during the request (refreshing the Google access token if it expired), and Google, not Easymailing, sends the invitations: with `send_updates` `all` every address in `attendees` receives an email invitation from the connected Google account, which is the organizer; `external_only` limits that to guests who do not use Google Calendar; `none` sends no email (the guests are still on the event). With `conference` `google_meet` a Meet link is created and included in the invitation. Nobody is invited who is not in `attendees`. If Google does not answer clearly the receipt is `uncertain`: the event may already exist and the guests may already have been notified, and the confirmation continues in the background without writing again. Once confirmed, a `meeting.scheduled` entry appears in the activity of every related record, done by the person who owns the token (marked «via Maia» when Maia made the request), and guests who are not contacts yet may be created as contacts (and their companies) in the background, as the account's record creation settings dictate, with the owner of the Google connection as responsible. No automation or webhook fires (CRM webhook events do not exist yet).

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. Linking an opportunity also needs `crm.opportunities.work` and `work` access to its pipeline. The calendar must belong to the user who owns the token, be selected, be writable and have Calendar active on its Google connection.

get.description:
Lists the notes written on one contact, company or opportunity, newest first, with their text, author and dates.

**When to use:** To read what has been written down about a record: previous calls, agreements, context before a meeting or a follow-up.

**When not to use:** You must name the record: there is no list of all the notes of the account. To read one note whose UUID you know, use `get_note`. For things that have to be done, with a due date and a person responsible, use `list_tasks`.

**Filters:** Exactly one of `contact`, `company` or `opportunity` is required, with the UUID of the record. A UUID that does not exist, or that the user cannot see, gives `404`. The order is fixed (newest first); there is no `order` parameter and no text search.
Pagination: notes are paged with `itemsPerPage` (default 30, maximum 50) and an opaque `cursor[gt]`: to read the next page, call again with the same record and the `cursor[gt]` of the `hydra:next` link of the previous response. The response gives the total number of notes of the record in `hydra:totalItems`; keep following `hydra:next` until a page comes back empty. `hydra:previous` takes you back: it carries the `cursor[lt]` of the first note of the page and returns the page just before it; use it the same way, with the same record.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.tasks_notes.read` capability. The note is only visible to users who can see the record it belongs to: `crm.contacts_companies.read` for a contact or company, `crm.opportunities.read` plus access to the pipeline for an opportunity.

get.description:
Lists the opportunities (deals) of the account that sit in pipelines the user can read, most recently changed first, with their pipeline, stage, status, amount, probability, forecast, company, contacts and owner.

**When to use:** To browse the sales pipeline, to find the deals of a company, contact or owner, or the open, won or lost ones, before reading, editing or moving them.

**When not to use:** To read one opportunity whose UUID you know, use `get_opportunity`; the list leaves out the description, attributes and loss note. To see the stages and loss reasons of a pipeline, use `get_pipeline`. To find people or organizations, use `list_contacts` or `list_companies`.

**Filters:** All filters are optional and combine with AND.
- `search`: part of the title, case-insensitive.
- `pipeline`: UUID of a pipeline the user can read; any other UUID gives a validation error.
- `stage`: UUID of a stage.
- `status`: `open` (including those without stage), `won` or `lost`.
- `owner`: email of the owner user.
- `company`: UUID of the company.
- `contact`: UUID of a linked contact.
Sorting: `order[field]=asc|desc` with `title`, `value`, `probability`, `expected_close_date`, `closed_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `company`, `owner` or `stage`. Default: `updated_at` descending (up to 4 `order` fields).
Pagination: `page` and `itemsPerPage`, like the rest of the API; the response gives the total in `hydra:totalItems`.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.opportunities.read` capability. Only opportunities of pipelines the user has `read` access to are returned.

post.description:
Creates an opportunity (a deal) in a pipeline, optionally in a given stage and with amount, expected close date, company, contacts, owner and attribute values. Everything is saved together or not at all. It is recorded as created through the API.

**When to use:** To register a new deal for a company or contact, for example after a qualifying conversation.

**When not to use:** To change a deal that already exists, use `update_opportunity`; to move it between stages, `move_opportunity_stage`. Check first with `list_opportunities` (filters `company` and `contact`) that the deal does not exist, because nothing prevents duplicates. To add a person or an organization, use `create_contact` or `create_company`.

**Side effects:** The opportunity appears in the CRM with an `opportunity.created` entry in its activity, attributed to the person who owns the key or token, with the note «via Maia» when Maia made the call. Its `record_source` is `api`. If you send `owner`, that user gets the assignment notification (in-app and, by default, email) unless they are the caller. Nothing is sent to contacts, no automation runs and no webhook fires (CRM webhook events do not exist yet). Retrying a request that succeeded creates a second opportunity.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.opportunities.work` capability. It also needs `work` access to the pipeline where it is created.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes an opportunity. There is no trash and no undo.

**When to use:** Only when the user explicitly asks to delete this deal for good, for example a duplicate or a test record.

**When not to use:** If the deal was lost or is no longer worth pursuing, close it with `lose_opportunity` so it stays in the reports. To fix a wrong title, amount or owner, use `update_opportunity`.

**Side effects:** Deleted with the opportunity: its activity, its notes, its files (a Google Drive reference never deletes the original in Drive) and its attribute values; the links to its company and contacts. Company and contacts stay. Tasks stay and lose the association with the opportunity; synced emails and meetings stay and lose the link to it. The owner's pending assignment notification is closed. No webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.pipelines.manage` capability. It also needs `admin` access to the pipeline of the opportunity.

put.description:
Changes the data of an existing opportunity: title, description, amount, probability override, expected close date, company, contacts, owner and attribute values. Properties you leave out keep their value; `null` clears an optional one. It does not change the stage or the pipeline.

**When to use:** To correct or complete a deal, change its amount or expected date, link a company or contacts, assign an owner or set attributes.

**When not to use:** To change the stage use `move_opportunity_stage`; to close it, `win_opportunity` or `lose_opportunity`; to reopen it, `reopen_opportunity`; to change its pipeline, `move_opportunity_pipeline`. If the destination stage requires fields, send them in that move, not here. To add a deal, use `create_opportunity`.

**Side effects:** All properties of the request are applied together: if one is rejected, nothing is saved. Each field that really changes adds an `opportunity.fields_changed` entry to the activity (field, previous and new value), attributed to the person who owns the key or token, with the note «via Maia» when Maia made the call; saving the same value leaves no entry. Changing `value` of a won or lost deal revalues its closing snapshot. If it sets a new owner who is not the caller, that user gets the assignment notification (in-app and, by default, email); the previous owner's pending notification is closed. Nothing is sent and no automation or webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.opportunities.work` capability. It also needs `work` access to the pipeline of the opportunity.

put.description:
Closes an opportunity as lost: it moves to the lost stage of its pipeline, its probability becomes 0 and it records the closing date and, if given, the reason and a note.

**When to use:** When the user says the deal fell through, the customer chose someone else or it was discarded.

**When not to use:** To close it as won, use `win_opportunity`. To remove a record that should not exist, use `delete_opportunity`. To keep working it, use `move_opportunity_stage` or `reopen_opportunity`.

**Side effects:** Same record as `move_opportunity_stage`: an `opportunity.stage_changed` entry with kind `lost` and the reason name and note, attributed to the person who owns the key or token, with the note «via Maia» when Maia made the call. If it was won, it changes the outcome and keeps the first closing date. The reason and note are kept in the closing history even if the reason is archived later. Nothing is sent and no automation or webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.opportunities.work` capability. It also needs `work` access to the pipeline of the opportunity.

put.description:
Moves an opportunity to another pipeline and puts it in one of that pipeline's stages. Amount, company, contacts, tasks, notes, files and activity go with it; a custom probability is dropped and the destination stage defines it.

**When to use:** To pass a deal to a different sales process, for example from New business to Renewals.

**When not to use:** To move it between stages of the same pipeline, use `move_opportunity_stage`. Before moving a deal with an amount, run `preview_opportunity_pipeline_move` to know whether the currency needs to be confirmed.

**Side effects:** Adds an `opportunity.pipeline_changed` entry (from and to pipeline and stage, and amount if it changed), attributed to the person who owns the key or token, with the note «via Maia» when Maia made the call; it is not recorded as a stage change. Moving a closed deal to an open stage reopens it, and to a won or lost stage keeps it closed. The closing snapshot is revalued with the reference currency of the destination. If it sets a new owner who is not the caller, that user gets the assignment notification (in-app and, by default, email); the previous owner's pending notification is closed. Nothing is sent and no automation or webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.opportunities.work` capability. It also needs `work` access to the pipeline of the opportunity and to the destination one.

put.description:
Moves an opportunity to another stage of its pipeline. The move follows the stage type: entering a won or lost stage closes the deal, entering an open stage from a closed one reopens it.

**When to use:** To advance or move back a deal in its pipeline, for example from Qualified to Negotiation.

**When not to use:** To close a deal as won or lost, `win_opportunity` and `lose_opportunity` find the stage for you. To reopen a closed deal, use `reopen_opportunity`. To change the pipeline, use `move_opportunity_pipeline`. To change other data of the deal, use `update_opportunity`.

**Side effects:** Adds an `opportunity.stage_changed` entry to the activity (from stage, to stage and kind: progressed, won, lost, reopened), attributed to the person who owns the key or token, with the note «via Maia» when Maia made the call. The time in the previous stage is closed and a new stay starts. Entering a won stage sets probability 100, a lost stage 0, and the closing amount is valued at the closing date. Moving to the stage it is already in changes nothing. Nothing is sent and no automation or webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.opportunities.work` capability. It also needs `work` access to the pipeline of the opportunity.

put.description:
Reopens a won or lost opportunity: it goes back to an open stage (by default the initial stage of the pipeline), the closing date and loss reason leave the current state and the probability is the one of the stage.

**When to use:** When a closed deal comes back to life, for example the customer returns after a loss or a win was registered by mistake.

The previous closing (date, amount snapshot and loss reason) stays in the history, a custom probability set before is not restored and a later close gets a new closing date. Nothing is sent and no automation or webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.opportunities.work` capability. It also needs `work` access to the pipeline of the opportunity.

put.description:
Closes an opportunity as won: it moves to the won stage of its pipeline, its probability becomes 100 and the closing date and the value of the sale are recorded.

**When to use:** When the user says the deal was closed successfully, signed or bought.

**When not to use:** To close it as lost, use `lose_opportunity`. To put it in an open stage, use `move_opportunity_stage`. To undo a mistaken win and keep working the deal, use `reopen_opportunity`.

**Side effects:** Same record as `move_opportunity_stage`: an `opportunity.stage_changed` entry with kind `won`, attributed to the person who owns the key or token, with the note «via Maia» when Maia made the call. If it was lost, it changes the outcome and keeps the first closing date. If it is already in that won stage, nothing changes. The closing amount is valued at the rate of the closing date; with no rate yet the value is marked `pending` and filled later. Nothing is sent and no automation or webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.opportunities.work` capability. It also needs `work` access to the pipeline of the opportunity.

post.description:
Defines a new custom attribute for opportunities, placed after the existing ones. It is shared by all pipelines. Once created, it can be filled in on any opportunity through its `public_code`. Its visual presentation (languages, help text, display style) is left at the defaults and can be tuned in the app.

**When to use:** When the account needs to store a new piece of data on deals that the opportunity does not already have, for example the lead source, the contract type or the competitor.

**When not to use:** To change an existing attribute, use `update_opportunity_attribute`. To set a value on an opportunity, use `update_opportunity`: this operation only defines the field, it does not set any value. To make a pipeline stage require it, edit the pipeline in the app.

**Side effects:** Records the creation in the account's attribute change log, under the person who made the call. No webhook is fired.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.companies.attributes.manage` capability. It is the same capability that manages company attributes.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.companies.attributes.manage` capability. It is the same capability that manages company attributes.

put.description:
Looks up the DNS records of a verified domain (DKIM, mail server, DMARC and, with `links_aligned`, tracking) and marks the domain as authenticated when they are all right. The response says which checks passed (`checks`) and the values found (`results`). If any check fails, the domain is marked as NOT authenticated, even if it was authenticated before.

**When to use:** After creating the DNS records at your DNS provider, to verify them. Call it again if a check fails and you have corrected the records; DNS changes can take time to propagate.

**When not to use:** If the domain is not verified yet, confirm the email first (`resend_sender_domain_verification`).

**Side effects:** Changes the state of the domain on every call. When all checks pass: the domain becomes authenticated and aligned, campaigns from its addresses are signed with the domain's own DKIM and, if `links_aligned` is set and the tracking records are right, the SSL certificate of the tracking domain is requested in the background. When a check fails: the domain stops being authenticated, so campaigns lose the domain's own DKIM signature and, in accounts that must authenticate to send large volumes, campaigns of 1000 recipients or more are flagged as not sendable. Senders created later on an authenticated domain are confirmed on creation; existing ones are not changed.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `account.integrations.manage` capability.

get.description:
Lists the emails that already left through the CRM and whose copy is visible in the record: the ones the user sent plus those sent from mailboxes where the user has full access. No content: subject, recipients, date and sender.

**When to use:** To answer what was sent recently, to whom, or by whom.

**When not to use:** For emails not sent yet (queued, scheduled, failed) use `list_email_sends`. To read the content or the history of a record, use the email read operations (`list_emails`).

**Filters:** - `search`: text to look for (maximum 190 characters).
Sorting: newest first. Pagination: `page` and `itemsPerPage` (default 30, maximum 100); the total is returned in `hydra:totalItems`.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.read` capability.

get.description:
Returns the SMS campaigns of your account, newest first, with their status, audience, message and sender. Email campaigns are not included: they have their own list.

**When to use:** To find an SMS campaign by name, status or audience, to see what was sent last, or to get the UUID that the other SMS campaign operations ask for.

**When not to use:** To read one SMS campaign in full, with its recipient count and delivery warnings, use `get_sms_campaign`. For email campaigns, use `list_campaigns`.

**Filters:** Default order: newest created first.

- `title`: campaigns whose name contains the text.
- `status`: exact status, for example `campaign.status.sent` (same values as the `status` field).
- `type`: exact type; SMS campaigns are always `campaign.regular`.
- `hash`: exact hash of the campaign.
- `audience`: UUID of the audience.

Sorting: `order[createdAt]`, `order[updatedAt]`, `order[status]`, `order[startedAt]` (when sending began) or `order[finishedAt]` (when it ended), each `asc` or `desc`. For the last one sent, combine `status=campaign.status.sent` with `order[startedAt]=desc&itemsPerPage=1`.

**Permissions:** Requires the viewer role or higher, or the `marketing.campaigns.read` capability.

post.description:
Creates an SMS campaign as a draft: message, SMS sender, recipients and tracking are saved, but no SMS is sent. To be valid it needs a `title`, an `audience`, `send_to` (with `groups`, `contact_segment` or `filter` when needed) and `sms_config` with the `message` and an active `sms_sender`. Only contacts with a confirmed SMS subscription and a phone number receive it.

**When to use:** To prepare a text message for an audience, some of its groups, a contact segment or a filter of its own. Afterwards check it with `get_sms_campaign` (`recipient_count`), send a preview with `send_sms_campaign_test`, and then send it (`send_sms_campaign_now`) or schedule it (`schedule_sms_campaign`).

**When not to use:** For email use `create_campaign`. To start from an existing SMS campaign, use `duplicate_sms_campaign`.

**Side effects:** Nothing is sent to anyone.

**Permissions:** Requires the author role or higher, or the `marketing.campaigns.write` capability. Choosing `contact_segment` or `filter` also requires the `contacts.read` capability.

422.description:
The campaign is incomplete or inconsistent. Each entry in `violations[].propertyPath` names the field to fix: missing message or sender, an SMS sender that does not exist or is not active (see `list_sms_senders`), or groups or segment from another audience.

`invalid_contact_filter`: The `filter` does not have the documented shape: no `match` or `conditions`, a group inside a group, more than 10 groups or 50 conditions, a condition without `field` or `operator`, or `audience` missing on a field that requires it (or sent on one that does not). `violations[].propertyPath` points to the part to fix, e.g. `filter.conditions[2].audience`.

`unknown_filter_field`: A `field` is not in the catalog of this user (it does not exist, was archived, or the user cannot filter on it). Look it up again with `list_contact_filter_fields`.

`invalid_filter_operator`: The `operator` is not one of that field's `operators`. Use one listed by `get_contact_filter_field`.

`invalid_filter_value`: A `value` does not fit its operator: wrong `value_shape`, a value outside `constraints` (length, number range, date `YYYY-MM-DD`, `lower` above `upper`) or an option that is not in the field. Read the field again with `get_contact_filter_field`.

`invalid_filter_reference`: A referenced record (audience, group, tag, campaign, attribute option, user) does not exist in this account or cannot be used here. Look its UUID up again in the field's `options` or with `list_contact_filter_field_suggestions`.

`filter_too_complex`: The filter is larger than the engine evaluates. With `match: any` at the top level, the loose conditions plus the `all` groups plus every condition of the `any` groups can be at most 20; an `any` group holds at most 20 conditions; a campaign-activity condition names at most the allowed campaigns. Split it or simplify it.

`filter_strategy_unavailable`: One condition cannot be evaluated by the engine right now (for example an attribute whose storage is not ready). Nothing was saved; remove that condition and retry later. If it persists, contact support.

`campaign_field_not_allowed`: A `field` exists but cannot select campaign recipients (its `usable_in` does not include `campaign`, e.g. company fields). Remove that condition.

`campaign_filter_empty`: `send_to_custom_segment` was sent without conditions in `filter`. Add at least one, or use `send_to_segment` with `contact_segment`.

`segment_reference_deleted`: `contact_segment` was deleted. Choose another one with `list_contact_segments`.

`segment_reference_denied`: `contact_segment` uses fields this user cannot evaluate. Use credentials of a user who can, or another segment.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes an SMS campaign together with its statistics. It cannot be undone. A scheduled campaign is cancelled and will not go out; messages already delivered are not recalled.

**When to use:** To remove a draft you no longer need, to stop a scheduled SMS (there is no operation to unschedule an SMS campaign), or to clear an old campaign and its results.

**When not to use:** To keep a copy of the campaign, use `duplicate_sms_campaign` first. For an email campaign, use `delete_campaign`. Automation campaigns cannot be deleted.

**Side effects:** Deletes the campaign and its statistics, whatever its status. Contacts are not affected.

**Permissions:** Requires the author role or higher, or the `marketing.campaigns.delete` capability.

put.description:
SCHEDULES THE CAMPAIGN FOR REAL: sets the date and time at which the text message will be sent to all its recipients, with no further action. Nothing goes out now; at that time the same real send as `send_sms_campaign_now` happens, to real people, and it cannot be recalled. Before sending, check with `get_sms_campaign` that the campaign has recipients (`recipient_count` above 0), no entry in `warnings` has `blocks_sending: true` (for example not enough SMS credits), and its status is draft, ready or scheduled. The API does not check recipients, credits or account status when scheduling: they are checked when the scheduled time arrives, and if the check fails the campaign moves to `campaign.status.error` and nothing is sent.

**When to use:** Only when the person has confirmed the SMS campaign and the date at which it must go out to all its recipients.

**When not to use:** To send right away, use `send_sms_campaign_now`. To check the message first, use `send_sms_campaign_test`. For an email campaign, use `campaign_schedule`.

**Side effects:** The status becomes `campaign.status.scheduled` and the send is queued for the date. At that time real SMS go out and SMS credits are used. Until then the campaign can be edited with `update_sms_campaign`. Scheduling an already scheduled campaign replaces its date. There is no operation to cancel a scheduled SMS campaign: to stop it, delete it with `delete_sms_campaign`.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `marketing.campaigns.send` capability.

put.description:
SENDS THE CAMPAIGN FOR REAL: starts delivering the text message right away to every recipient of the campaign, meaning the contacts with a confirmed SMS subscription and a phone number. These are real SMS to real people; once it starts it cannot be undone or recalled. Before sending, check with `get_sms_campaign` that the campaign has recipients (`recipient_count` above 0), no entry in `warnings` has `blocks_sending: true` (for example not enough SMS credits), and its status is draft, ready or scheduled. The checks run at the moment of sending, not before: if one fails the request is rejected.

**When to use:** Only when the person has confirmed that this SMS campaign must go out now to all its recipients.

**When not to use:** To send at a later time, use `schedule_sms_campaign`. To see the message on a phone, use `send_sms_campaign_test`: it sends only to the numbers you list. For an email campaign, use `campaign_send_now`.

**Side effects:** Real delivery: the status becomes `campaign.status.sending` and then `campaign.status.sent`, and SMS credits of the plan are used as the messages go out. A scheduled campaign can also be sent now; its schedule is cancelled. put.description:
Changes the data of a customer and re-processes their audience member with the same rules as `create_store_customer`. If you send a different `email`, it does not rename the existing member: the new email is subscribed as a member (a new one if nobody has it) and the customer is linked to it; the previous member is left as it was.

**When to use:** When the buyer changes their details in the shop and the change must reach the audience.

**When not to use:** To register a new buyer use `create_store_customer`.

**Side effects:** The member is processed again like on creation: depending on the audience and on its current status it can receive the confirmation or welcome email (a person who unsubscribed on their own gets a confirmation email, at most once every 15 minutes, every time the shop syncs them; a member with status `suscriber.status.unsuscribed.admin` is confirmed again at once in a single opt-in audience). A new email creates a new member with its own subscription. The store's group is added to the member and the group webhook and automations fire for it. The query flags `disable_double_opt_in`, `disable_welcome_email` and `disable_sms_double_opt_in` (all `true`/`false`) turn the confirmation and welcome messages off.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `marketing.audiences.write` capability.

get.description:
Lists CRM tasks with their status, due date, person responsible and the contacts, companies and opportunities they are linked to. With no filters it returns the open tasks assigned to the user who owns the token, the most urgent first (overdue ones on top).

**When to use:** To answer what is pending: the user's own tasks, overdue tasks, tasks due today or this week, the tasks of a teammate, unassigned tasks, or everything open on one contact, company or opportunity.

**When not to use:** To read one task whose UUID you know, use `get_task`. To read the notes of a record, use `list_notes`. To find a valid person to assign a task to, use `list_task_assignees`. There is no text search on tasks: narrow by person, record, date, priority or type and read `title`.

**Filters:** All filters are optional and combine with AND.
- `assignee`: `me` (the user who owns the token), `unassigned`, `all`, or the email of an active user of the account. Default: `me`, or `all` when you filter by `contact`, `company` or `opportunity`.
- `include_completed`: `false` (default) returns only open tasks; `true` returns open and completed tasks. There is no filter for completed tasks only: read `status`.
- `priority`, `type`: exact value.
- `due_from` (inclusive) and `due_to` (exclusive): bounds of `due_at`, ISO 8601 with a time zone. Tasks without a due date are left out when either one is sent.
- `contact`, `company`, `opportunity`: only tasks linked to that record, by its UUID. Send one at most. A UUID that does not exist, or that the user cannot see, gives `404`.
Overdue tasks: send `due_to` set to the current instant and leave `include_completed` out. Tasks due on a given day: `due_from` at the start of the day and `due_to` at the start of the next, in the user time zone.
Sorting: `sort=due` (default) puts overdue tasks first, then open tasks by due date, then open tasks without due date, then completed ones (most recently completed first); `priority` orders from `high` to `none` and then by due date; `title` is alphabetical, ignoring case. There is no sort direction.
Pagination: tasks are paged with `itemsPerPage` (default 30, maximum 50) and an opaque `cursor[gt]`: to read the next page, call again with the same filters and the `cursor[gt]` of the `hydra:next` link of the previous response. The total number of tasks is not returned. Keep following `hydra:next` until a page comes back empty. `hydra:previous` takes you back: it carries the `cursor[lt]` of the first task of the page and returns the page just before it; use it the same way, with the same filters.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.tasks_notes.read` capability. A task linked to contacts or companies is only visible to users who also have `crm.contacts_companies.read`, and a task linked to an opportunity only to users who can see its pipeline; a task the user cannot fully see is treated as if it did not exist.

post.description:
Creates an open task with a title and, optionally, a description, priority, type, person responsible, due date, reminder and links to contacts, companies and opportunities.

**When to use:** To record something that has to be done: a follow-up call to a contact, a proposal to send, a renewal to review. Link it to the records it is about so it shows up on them.

**When not to use:** To write down information without a deadline or an action, such as what was said in a meeting, use `create_note`. To change a task that already exists, use `update_task`; to mark it done, `complete_task`.

**Side effects:** The task is created open and, if it is linked to records, a `task.created` entry appears in the activity of each of them, done by the person who owns the token (marked «via Maia» when Maia made the request; `initiated_via` says `api` or `maia`). A task without links leaves no entry. All fields are applied together: if one is rejected, nothing is saved. If the task is assigned to a user other than the one who owns the token, that user gets a notification (in the app and by email, according to their notification preferences). If a reminder is set, the assignee also gets a notification at `reminder_at`; it is delivered by the same notification system as the Customer App. Nothing is sent to the contacts and no automation or webhook fires (CRM webhook events do not exist yet).

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.tasks_notes.write` capability. The user must also be able to see every contact, company and opportunity the task is linked to (`crm.contacts_companies.read` for contacts and companies, access to the pipeline for opportunities).

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a task, open or completed. There is no archive and no undo.

**When to use:** Only when the user explicitly asks to delete this task, for example one created by mistake or a duplicate.

**When not to use:** If the work is finished, use `complete_task`: the task stays in the history of its records. To fix a title, date or assignee, use `update_task`.

**Side effects:** The task disappears from its records and from every list; the `task.created`, `task.completed` and `task.reopened` entries already in their activity stay, and no deletion entry is added. The assignee's pending assignment and reminder notices are withdrawn. No webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.tasks_notes.write` capability. The user must also be able to see every contact, company and opportunity the task is linked to (`crm.contacts_companies.read` for contacts and companies, access to the pipeline for opportunities). Only the creator of the task, its assignee or an account admin can delete it; an admin needs a token that reaches account administration (an API key, or OAuth with the `admin` scope) to delete tasks of other people.

**When to use:** When the user says a task is done. It is safe to repeat: completing an already completed task changes nothing.

post.description:
Registers a URL of yours to be called whenever one of the chosen events happens in an audience (`marketing` scope) or in the CRM of the account (`crm` scope). Each delivery is signed with the secret you give.

**Scope:** A webhook is either `marketing` or `crm`. A `marketing` webhook receives the events of one audience (members, campaigns, automations and SMS) and needs `audience`. A `crm` webhook receives the events of contacts, companies and opportunities of the whole account and has no `audience`. The two kinds of events are never mixed in one webhook, and `scope` cannot change after the webhook is created.

**When to use:** To keep another system in sync with an audience, for example to learn when someone subscribes, unsubscribes or opens a campaign; or with the CRM, to learn when a contact, company or opportunity is created, updated or deleted.

**When not to use:** To change an existing webhook use `update_webhook`.

**Side effects:** From now on, every matching event in the audience (or, for `crm`, in the account) is sent to the URL. A failed delivery is attempted up to 3 times in total, with growing waits between attempts.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `account.integrations.manage` capability.

**Scope:** `scope` cannot change: sending a different value fails with 422, and omitting it keeps the current one. Events must belong to the scope of the webhook, and a `crm` webhook never has `audience`.

**When to use:** To point the webhook to a new URL, change which events it receives, rotate the secret, or turn it back on after it was deactivated.

**When not to use:** To stop deliveries for good use `delete_webhook`.
