tags.description: A contact is a person in the account: one record per person, identified by their email or phone, with or without audiences, company or opportunities. Contact data (name, company, tags, attributes) is kept once; the person's subscription to each audience is a membership of that contact, which the Audiences category also shows as a member.
tags.name: Contacts

tags.description: A contact segment is a saved filter over all the contacts of the account, whatever their audiences: «confirmed email subscribers of the newsletter who opened one of the last 5 campaigns», «contacts in Spain with the VIP tag». Who is inside updates by itself as data changes. Segments are shared by the whole account, are versioned (every change publishes a new revision; scheduled campaigns keep the revision they were scheduled with) and are the segments Customer App shows in Contacts and offers as campaign recipients. Their conditions use the fields of `list_contact_filter_fields`. The older segments that live inside one audience are `list_audience_segments`, kept only for the classic panel.
tags.name: Contact segments

tags.description: The catalog of fields you can filter contacts on and the shape of a filter. The same catalog feeds the Contacts filter of Customer App, contact segments and the recipients of email and SMS campaigns, so a filter written here selects exactly what the app shows. Each field lists its operators and the value each operator expects; subscription fields also need the audience. It replaces condition fields for everything that works on contacts; condition fields stay for old audience segments and automation conditions.
tags.name: Contact filters

tags.description: A company is an organization your contacts work for, with its own domains, owner, location and attributes. It is shared by the whole account and is not tied to any audience. A contact belongs to at most one company; a company can have many contacts. A domain belongs to only one company.
tags.name: Companies

tags.description: An opportunity is a potential sale: a deal with an amount, an expected close date, a company, contacts and an owner that moves through the stages of a pipeline until it is won or lost. Opportunities live in pipelines and inherit their access: a user sees, works or deletes an opportunity only with the matching access to its pipeline, besides the account capability. Opportunities are independent of audiences.
tags.name: Opportunities

tags.description: A pipeline is a sales process: an ordered list of stages (open, won and lost) that opportunities go through, with a reference currency, entry requirements per stage and the loss reasons offered when a deal is lost. Stages and loss reasons belong to one pipeline and are managed under it. Who can see or work a pipeline is set in the app; each user sees only the pipelines they have been granted.
tags.name: Pipelines

tags.description: A task is a to-do of the team: a title, an optional due date and an optional person responsible, which can be linked to any number of contacts, companies and opportunities. A task is open or completed; creating, completing and reopening it is recorded in the activity of every record it is linked to. A task with no links is visible to the whole account; a task linked to records is visible only to users who can see all of them. Tasks are not notes: a note is text kept on one record, with no deadline or person responsible.
tags.name: Tasks

tags.description: A note is free text kept on one contact, company or opportunity: what was said in a call, an agreement, context for the next conversation. It has an optional title, an author and a history of edits, and it appears in the activity of its record. A note belongs to exactly one record and is visible only to users who can see that record; only an account admin or its author can edit or delete it. A note has no due date or person responsible: for something to do, use a task.
tags.name: Notes

tags.description: A file is a document or image (PDF, Office, OpenDocument, images, CSV, ZIP… up to 20 MiB) kept on one contact, company or opportunity: contracts, proposals, signed copies. It has a name, an optional description and the person who uploaded it, and it appears in the activity of its record when it is added or removed. A file belongs to exactly one record and is visible only to users who can see that record. Uploading takes two calls: `create_file` declares the file and reserves its space, `set_file_content` sends the bytes. The storage of the whole account is limited by its CRM plan (`get_file_storage_usage`). For text written about a record use notes; for things to do use tasks.
tags.name: Files

tags.description: Emails synchronized from the Gmail mailboxes that users connected to Easymailing, shown on the contact, company or opportunity they belong to. An email appears on a contact when one of its addresses took part, on a company when someone from one of its domains did, and on an opportunity when one of its contacts did while it was open. Each user sees only emails of mailboxes they own or whose owner shared them with the account, and only as much of each as the sharing level allows: participants and date, plus subject, or everything. Bodies and attachments are read from the stored copy and from Google on demand. Sending, replying and drafts are other operations.
tags.name: Emails

tags.description: An email draft is an email that is being written and has not been sent. Drafts belong to the person who started them: nobody else can see or use them. Creating or editing a draft never sends anything, so it is the safe way to prepare an email for someone to review; to send it use `send_email` or `schedule_email` with the draft. Drafts can be incomplete (no recipients, no subject, no sender). A person can keep up to 200 drafts, and each save raises a `revision` so two devices cannot overwrite each other.
tags.name: Email drafts

tags.description: A send is one email written from a contact, company or opportunity and sent from a connected Gmail mailbox. Sending is asynchronous: `send_email` or `schedule_email` queue the email and answer 202; it leaves about 20 seconds later (ten seconds to undo plus ten of grace), at the scheduled time, or later if the mailbox has reached its limit of 12 emails per hour and 200 per day. While `state` is `queued` it can be cancelled; once it is `sending` or `sent` it cannot be recalled. Sends are private to the person who made them. Writing an email without sending it is `create_email_draft`. These emails reach other people: confirm the final text, recipients and time with the user before sending or scheduling.
tags.name: Email sends

tags.description: A batch sends the same message as a separate, individual email to each of 2 to 50 people from the user's Gmail mailbox: nobody sees the other recipients. The emails leave five minutes apart within the mailbox limit of 12 per hour and 200 per day, so a large batch takes hours. The whole batch has one undo window and can be cancelled at once or one email at a time while queued. A batch is not an email campaign: for mass mailings to an audience use the campaign operations. Batches reach many people: confirm text and list with the user before sending.
tags.name: Email batches

tags.description: Everything needed to prepare an email from the CRM before it is saved as a draft or sent: the mailboxes the user can send from and their signatures, the sending limits and when an email would leave, the contacts of a company or opportunity to write to, the personalization tags and their preview, a check of the recipients (people who opted out) and the upload of attachments. Nothing in this group sends an email. To save it use `create_email_draft`; to send it, `send_email`, `schedule_email` or `send_email_batch`.
tags.name: Email composing

tags.description: A contact opts out of CRM email when they click the unsubscribe link of a 1-to-1 email sent from the CRM. From then on, sending to their address answers `recipient_opted_out` until the sender confirms that they still want to write to them (or the opt-out is removed). It is stored per address and covers only emails sent from the CRM: it does not change the contact's subscriptions to audiences or email campaigns.
tags.name: Email opt-outs

tags.description: An email sequence is a series of personal emails with waits in between that Easymailing sends one contact at a time from a connected Gmail mailbox (the mailbox of a person, with their signature), to follow up with contacts, customers and warm leads. The sequence stops by itself for a contact who replies, books a meeting, bounces or unsubscribes. It is not a newsletter or a campaign to an audience (see email campaigns) and not an event-driven flow (see automations). How it works: you write a DRAFT (steps, schedule, sender, exit rules), publish it as an immutable VERSION and then ENROLL contacts. Each enrollment stays on the version it entered with, so editing and publishing again only affects contacts enrolled afterwards. Nothing is sent by creating, editing or publishing a sequence: emails leave only for enrolled contacts, from the sender's mailbox, within the schedule window, and always with an unsubscribe footer. Typical flow: `create_email_sequence`, `upload_email_sequence_asset` (only for attachments), `update_email_sequence_draft`, `get_email_sequence_validation`, `publish_email_sequence`, `enroll_contacts_in_email_sequence`, then follow it with `list_email_sequence_enrollments`, `list_email_sequence_activity` and `get_email_sequence_statistics`. To stop emails to people already enrolled, pause the sequence or exclude the enrollment. Creating and editing sequences needs the CRM Pro plan; reading them does not.
tags.name: Email sequences

tags.description: A meeting is an event of a connected Google calendar that Easymailing links to the CRM: a demo, a call, a visit. It has a time, guests with their answers, an optional video call, and the contacts, companies and opportunities it is related to, which show it in their activity. Google Calendar is the source of truth: meetings are read from the last synchronization, and creating, changing or cancelling one writes the event in the user's own Google calendar, where Google emails the invitations. A meeting is only visible to people who can see its calendar: the owner, or colleagues the owner shared it with. A meeting is not a booking page slot and not a task: it has no due date or responsible person.
tags.name: Meetings

tags.description: A booking page is a public scheduling link of one user: the host sets opening hours, duration, calendars and a form, publishes it, and anyone with the link picks a free time and books a meeting that is created in the host's Google Calendar. Each page belongs to the user who creates it; that user can share it with colleagues so they can insert its link in emails or propose exact times from the host's availability. A page goes from draft to published, can be paused and finally archived, and sends two emails to the people who book (a confirmation and a data check) from the sender chosen for the page. These operations manage the pages and propose times; the visitor's own booking happens on the public page and is not part of the API. Meetings that result from a booking are meetings, not booking pages.
tags.name: Booking pages

tags.description: The activity of a record is its timeline: everything that happened to a contact, company or opportunity, newest first. It is written by the product itself when something happens (a field changes, an opportunity moves stage, a note or task is created, an email arrives, a meeting is scheduled, a campaign is sent or opened) and cannot be edited or created through the API. Each row has a type, who did it, how (`initiated_via`, with `maia` for what Maia did) and data that depends on the type. What the user may not see of a record (an email of a mailbox they cannot read, a task of a pipeline they cannot access) is returned as an unavailable row, without its content.
tags.name: Activity

tags.description: Contact attributes are the custom fields you define for people in the CRM (customer tier, birthday, interests...). They belong to the contact itself, not to an audience: every audience sees the same value. Each attribute has a type and a stable `public_code`, which is the key used in the `attributes` object of a contact. Contact attributes are different from the custom fields of an audience, which store data on each member of that audience.
tags.name: Contact attributes

tags.description: Company attributes are the custom fields you define for organizations in the CRM (industry segment, contract renewal, annual budget...). Each attribute has a type and a stable `public_code`, which is the key used in the `attributes` object of a company.
tags.name: Company attributes

tags.description: Opportunity attributes are the custom fields you define for deals in the CRM (lead source, contract type, estimated budget...). They are defined once for the whole account, not per pipeline: every opportunity of every pipeline can use them, and a pipeline stage can require one before an opportunity may enter it. Each attribute has a type and a stable `public_code`, which is the key used in the `attributes` object of an opportunity.
tags.name: Opportunity attributes

tags.description: Audiences are the lists that hold your subscribers. Each audience has its own members, groups, segments and custom fields, plus sending defaults: sender, double opt-in and GDPR.
tags.name: Audiences

tags.description: A member is one person's subscription to one audience. The same person (same email or phone) is a single contact in the account and a separate member in each audience they belong to, each with its own status, groups and custom field values. Each member exposes the contact it belongs to in its `contact` property: the contact is the person (data shared by all their audiences, see the `Contacts` operations) and the member is their subscription to this audience.
tags.name: Members

tags.description: Groups are labels you assign to the members of one audience by hand or by rule, to target campaigns and automations. Bulk group actions run in the background and return an async task you follow with `get_async_task`.
tags.name: Groups

tags.description: Old segments that live inside one audience and select its members with up to five conditions. They are kept for the classic panel and for existing campaigns and automations, but Customer App does not show them: for new segments use contact segments (`list_contact_segments`), which work over all the contacts of the account. Bulk actions on an old segment run in the background and return an async task you follow with `get_async_task`.
tags.name: Audience segments

tags.description: Custom fields store extra data on each member of an audience (company, birthday, interests). Their `template_tag` personalizes emails, and their values are set when you create or update a member.
tags.name: Custom fields

tags.description: Condition fields are the member properties you can filter on in old audience segments, in bulk group actions by conditions and in automation condition steps. Each one lists the operators it accepts. For contact segments and campaign filters, use the contact filter catalog (`list_contact_filter_fields`).
tags.name: Condition fields

tags.description: Merge tags are the placeholders you can use in the emails of an audience to insert member data, custom field values and required links such as the unsubscribe link.
tags.name: Merge tags

tags.description: Embedded and popup sign-up forms of an audience: they add the people who fill them to the audience. Forms made in the new Easymailing panel can be read here but not changed.
tags.name: Subscription forms

tags.description: Quick polls and multi-question surveys that you link to email campaigns to collect answers from your subscribers, and their aggregated results.
tags.name: Surveys

tags.description: One-off email campaigns sent to an audience, some of its groups, a contact segment or a filter of their own: regular newsletters, A/B tests, revalidation and survey campaigns. Create and edit them, send test emails, and send or schedule them.
tags.name: Email campaigns

tags.description: Text message (SMS) campaigns sent to contacts with a confirmed SMS subscription in an audience, some of its groups, a contact segment or a filter of their own. Create and edit them, send test messages, and send or schedule them.
tags.name: SMS campaigns

tags.description: Automated workflows that run a series of steps for the contacts of one audience. You create the automation, give it triggers (what starts it for a contact) and steps (what happens to the contact), then activate it. It starts as a draft and sends nothing until it is active.
tags.name: Automations

tags.description: The events and dates that start an automation for a contact: a form completed, a campaign clicked, an order paid, a date reached, a call from your own system. An automation can have several triggers, and every new automation already gets one manual trigger.
tags.name: Automation triggers

tags.description: The actions an automation performs on each contact once a trigger has started it, arranged as a flow: send an email or an SMS, wait, check a condition and branch, change groups, fields or score, call a webhook, start another automation, jump to another step or unsubscribe the contact.
tags.name: Automation steps

tags.description: Email designs you can assign to campaigns and automations: either your own HTML or a design built with the visual editor.
tags.name: Templates

tags.description: Base designs of your own account that you marked as master in the panel, to start new templates from.
tags.name: Master templates

tags.description: Ready-made email designs offered by Easymailing, with the types and industries to browse them, that you copy into your own templates.
tags.name: Themes

tags.description: Brand styles of the account: colors, fonts, button style, logos and social links that give emails and landing pages their visual identity.
tags.name: Brand settings

tags.description: Online stores (WooCommerce, Shopify, your own shop) connected to an audience, so their customers, products and orders can be tracked and used in automations.
tags.name: Stores

tags.description: Groupings of the products of a store (for example "Shoes"), used to organize the catalog.
tags.name: Product categories

tags.description: The products of a store catalog. Orders refer to them through their variants.
tags.name: Products

tags.description: The purchasable options of a product (size, color), each with its own price and stock. Orders list variants.
tags.name: Product variants

tags.description: The buyers of a store. Each customer is tied to a member of the store's audience, so purchases can be used in segments and automations.
tags.name: Store customers

tags.description: Orders and carts of a store, with the steps of their life (cart, processed, paid, shipped, cancelled, refunded). Each step feeds revenue statistics and can start automations.
tags.name: Orders

tags.description: Email addresses that can appear as the sender (From) of campaigns. Each one must be confirmed by following a link sent to that address.
tags.name: Email senders

tags.description: Names that appear as the sender of SMS messages. Each one is validated before it can be used in SMS campaigns.
tags.name: SMS senders

tags.description: Your own domains authenticated for sending (SPF/DKIM/DMARC records), so campaigns go out with your domain and better deliverability.
tags.name: Sending domains

tags.description: Notifications Easymailing sends to your own server when something happens in an audience (a member subscribes, opens an email, joins a group...), with the log of what was sent.
tags.name: Webhooks

tags.description: Data protection (GDPR) settings shared by the audiences: who is responsible for the data (data managers) and why it is collected (treatment purposes).
tags.name: Privacy

tags.description: The plan of the account and how much of it is used: subscribers, credits, limits, AI cost and SMS credits.
tags.name: Plan & usage

tags.description: Invoices Easymailing has issued to the account for its subscription.
tags.name: Invoices

tags.description: Requests for help sent to the Easymailing support team, and their replies, for the user making the call.
tags.name: Support tickets

tags.description: Many API calls sent at once and run in the background. Each call in the batch is checked against the permissions of the credential that created the batch. A batch belongs to the user who created it: only that user and an account administrator can read, delete or download it; for anyone else it does not exist (404). Batches created before this rule was introduced have no creator and stay visible to every credential of the account until they expire, 15 days after creation.
tags.name: Batch operations

tags.description: Where to follow long operations that run in the background. The operations that return a task are in Groups and Segments; here you check how they went and download their file.
tags.name: Async tasks

post.description:
Sent when a company is created, whatever the channel. `event_data.record` is the company as it was saved.

Sent to `crm` webhooks (account-wide, without audience) subscribed to this event.

Easymailing sends the events in batches: the body is a JSON array of up to 100 events of the same webhook. Process them idempotently: an event can arrive more than once.

parameters.description: Identifier of this delivery (UUID). Retries of the same batch keep it: use it to discard duplicates.
parameters.name: Easymailing-Webhook-Id

parameters.description: Signature of the request: `sha256=` followed by the hexadecimal HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, computed with the secret of the webhook. Compute it over the body exactly as received and compare it in constant time.
parameters.name: Easymailing-Webhook-Signature

attributes.description: Custom attribute values keyed by attribute key. Always a JSON object (`{}` when empty).

id.description: Identifier of the event for this webhook: `/webhooks/{webhook_id}/webhook_events/{event_id}`. Unique per event and webhook; use it to discard duplicates.

2XX.description: Any 2XX status acknowledges the whole batch. A 404 or 410 deactivates the webhook. Any other status or a network error makes the batch be retried later, a limited number of times.

post.description:
Sent when a company is deleted. `event_data.record` is the last representation of the company before its deletion.

Sent when a contact subscribes to the audience. `event_data.source` tells where the subscription came from and `subscription_form` the form used, if any.

Sent to `marketing` webhooks subscribed to this event, for contacts of the webhook audience.

Easymailing sends the events in batches: the body is a JSON array of up to 100 events of the same webhook. Process them idempotently: an event can arrive more than once.

parameters.description: Identifier of this delivery (UUID). Retries of the same batch keep it: use it to discard duplicates.
parameters.name: Easymailing-Webhook-Id

parameters.description: Signature of the request: `sha256=` followed by the hexadecimal HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, computed with the secret of the webhook. Compute it over the body exactly as received and compare it in constant time.
parameters.name: Easymailing-Webhook-Signature

id.description: Identifier of the event for this webhook: `/webhooks/{webhook_id}/webhook_events/{event_id}`. Unique per event and webhook; use it to discard duplicates.

2XX.description: Any 2XX status acknowledges the whole batch. A 404 or 410 deactivates the webhook. Any other status or a network error makes the batch be retried later, a limited number of times.
